Those who listen hear many secrets in the earth, and one Uthek has heard is of a red crystal called draenethyst, newly arrived in this land and brought from a place of flying mountains and ruling demons. A shard of it, Uthek says, will make the magic strong. The lost one Ongeku holds a shard in the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. When you return, Uthek will look for proof that the Gelkis can still call you friend.

quest:1374.text: Khan Jehn. Following Ongeku, Uthek the Wise tells you the earth says the Magram are growing weak, and that the hour has come to slay their Khan. Uthek wants the head of Khan Jehn brought to Gelkis Village. Uthek the Wise at Gelkis Village says the earth speaks to Uthek, and it tells of the Magram growing weak. Uthek names their Khan, Jehn, as the one to strike down and asks for the head of the Magram Khan. Uthek expects you to still count as a friend of the Gelkis when you come back.

quest:1375.text: Khan Shaka. Warug of the Magram, pleased with your help after Gizmo for Warug, now wants the head of Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis. He means to stare at it and laugh at his enemy. In Magram Village, Warug tells you that you have helped the Magram and he likes you. Now he wants you to kill Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis, and bring him the head. He says he wants to stare at it and laugh at him. He expects you to stay on good terms with the Magram.

quest:1382.text: Strange Alliance. Captain Pentigast sees luck in the way the centaur clans of Desolace fight each other, since as one force they could not be stopped. The Gelkis are locked in brutal war with the Magram, so Pentigast sends you to Uthek the Wise in southwestern Desolace to seek an alliance. Captain Pentigast counts it good fortune that the centaur clans war on one another, for joined together they could not be stopped. Pentigast wants to push that edge. The Gelkis and Magram are locked in brutal war, so striking at the Magram might win the Gelkis over. Uthek the Wise can be found where the Gelkis camps begin, in the southwest of Desolace, and through her an alliance might be struck. She turns you away at first, telling you to leave and to return after killing many Magram.

quest:1384.text: Raid on the Kolkar. After Strange Alliance, Uthek the Wise sends you against the Kolkar centaurs to the northeast. Kill them, take their charms, and bring ten of those charms back to Uthek. Uthek scoffs at the Kolkar centaurs for thinking their magic strong; in Uthek's view they know nothing of magic. You go northeast to the Kolkar, kill them, and take their charms. Uthek wants ten Crude Charms to throw in the fire, laughing as they burn.

quest:1385.text: Brutal Politics. Captain Pentigast believes whichever centaur clan wins the wars of Desolace will spill out and threaten the Alliance strongholds. To learn how to beat them, Pentigast wants an alliance with one clan: fight the Gelkis, win over the Magram, and speak with Warug. War rages across Desolace, centaur against centaur, and the Alliance believes the winner will spill out against its strongholds. That cannot be allowed. To learn how to beat the centaurs, Captain Pentigast says, the Alliance needs one of the clans as a friend. The Magram fight the Gelkis, so striking at the Gelkis might make the Magram weigh an alliance. Earn their favor, then go to Warug in the Magram village, in Desolace's southeast. Warug warns that to be a friend of the Magram, you must kill Gelkis.

quest:1386.text: Assault on the Kolkar. After Brutal Politics, Warug in Magram Village wants proof that you can kill Kolkar the way the Magram do. Head north and slay Kolkar centaurs, scouts and maulers. Warug sneers that the Kolkar believe themselves strong while the Magram laugh at them as they kill them. Warug wants you to prove you can kill Kolkar as the Magram do, so you head north: twelve Kolkar centaurs, twelve scouts and six maulers are to fall.

quest:1387.text: Centaur Bounty. Corporal Melkins at Nijel's Point says every centaur clan in Desolace shares one trait, cruelty, and that peace will not come while the centaur remain. Melkins asks you to hunt them across the land and bring fifteen of their ears. At Nijel's Point, Corporal Melkins describes a centaur race split among many clans, each with a leader and plans of its own, yet alike in cruelty. Peace, Melkins says, will only come if the centaurs are removed. Wandering Desolace, you hunt centaur and take their ears. Melkins wants a great many, fifteen in all, and calls the work a service to the Alliance that brings the war's end nearer.

quest:1394.text: Final Passage. Parqual Fintallas tells you that you have passed this test and the ones before it. You are sent back to Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles, who will sense the change in you and see whether you have grown strong in mind, body and spirit, enough to be honoured for your efforts. This is the last step of the Test of Faith, the chain of trials that Dorn Plainstalker began. Dorn waits in the Weathered Nook, in a cave reached by a ramp, north of Freewind Post. Parqual Fintallas urges you to stay true to the balance you have shown throughout these trials.

quest:1431.text: Alliance Relations. Thrall seeks a careful hand to preserve peace with the Alliance. In Orgrimmar, Craven Drok sends seasoned Horde adventurers to find Keldran near the western exit. The work calls for quiet diplomacy and intelligence to protect Thrall’s fragile peace. Thrall knows war with the Alliance could ruin his young nation. Raised in human captivity, the Warchief learned human statecraft and military strategy. Craven Drok watches for warriors and champions with patience for a subtler path, one that looks beyond raw force. Near Orgrimmar’s western exit, Keldran keeps a humble dwelling. He practices magic and covert arts, working with appearances, perception, and statecraft. Keldran seeks discreet operatives to serve the Warchief as the Horde faces a tense standoff with its bitter rivals.

quest:1432.text: Alliance Relations. In Orgrimmar, Alliance advances across Kalimdor raise fears of dangerous political fallout. The Horde sends orders to Desolace to purge demons before the Alliance can accuse Thrall's people of renewed ties to the Burning Legion. Alliance scouts and expeditions crossing Kalimdor put the Horde in a delicate position. Demonic remnants across central Kalimdor could confirm old suspicions that the orcs and their allies still serve the Burning Legion. With Warchief Thrall's sanction, Keldran oversees operations from Orgrimmar to clear those remnants before hostile Alliance factions can use them to justify war. Orders south lead through the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains and into Desolace. Just north of the vast Kodo Graveyard stands Ghost Walker Post. Horde agents such as Takata Steelblade watch the wastes, where rampant centaur tribes and spreading demonic corruption both threaten the region.

quest:1437.text: Vahlarriel's Search. Vahlarriel Demonslayer has come to Desolace to learn what became of two missing nobles of House Malem, a Darnassian merchant family. Their father fears the worst, and the last word of the pair places them in the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks back. Vahlarriel asks you to find their wagon. Vahlarriel Demonslayer is looking for Tyranis and Dalinda Malem, whose father fears the worst and has charged Vahlarriel with doing everything possible to find them. The search has barely begun, and Vahlarriel hopes it will not keep them in Desolace long. The pair were last reported crossing the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks ago. Vahlarriel asks you to find their wagon in Desolace and to come at once when you do. Its charred remains lie there, with a chest among them.

quest:1438.text: Vahlarriel's Search. After the second part of Vahlarriel's Search, Vahlarriel Demonslayer sends you to look for Dalinda and Tyranis Malem, beginning at the fortress. Word of it goes to Vahlarriel's superiors in Darnassus, who worry about Tyranis's motives and want Dalinda brought home safe above all. Vahlarriel Demonslayer wants you to look for both Dalinda and Tyranis, beginning at the fortress, and return with what you learn. Vahlarriel will contact superiors in Darnassus right away. A private word follows: they worry about why Tyranis came to Desolace, and they care most that Dalinda gets home safe. As for Tyranis, they want him gauged first, before any homecoming.

quest:1439.text: Search for Tyranis. Dalinda Malem tells you the orcs slaughtered all their guards and servants before bringing her and Tyranis here. Tyranis tried to speak to them, and she cannot leave until she knows what has become of her brother. She asks you to find him and come back when his fate is known. Dalinda tells you that orcs killed every guard and servant of theirs before dragging her and Tyranis to this place. She expected to die at once, yet the orcs clearly had other designs. Tyranis tried talking to them, perhaps hoping his arcane learning would impress them, though she cannot say why. She will not escape until she knows his fate, so she asks you to find him and return when you do. He is in a building left of the fortress entrance. Dalinda dreads that Tyranis, if allowed, will seek the Burning Blade's secrets and become one of them. Power has always drawn him, as it does anyone magic seduces. To her people even studying such things is a grave crime, and she doubts she could face her family with word that his spirit toyed with that danger.

quest:1440.text: Return to Vahlarriel. Dalinda Malem is ready to leave Thunder Axe Fortress. She thanks you for what you have done for her and her family, and says the time is yours to choose. You escort her out, then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer. Dalinda asks whether the time has come, and offers thanks for all you have done for her and her family, in case things do not go as hoped. If you are ready, nothing else keeps her here, and she will go when you judge the moment right. You escort her out of Thunder Axe Fortress and then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer in Desolace.

quest:1442.text: Seeking the Kor Gem. You cross the sea to Darkshore in search of a Kor gem for Jordan Stilwell. Thundris Windweaver sends an Alliance paladin initiate into Blackfathom Deeps, where naga corrupt the potent stone. Jordan needs it for his craft. Paladins in training cross continental borders to Darkshore for materials needed by the human smith Jordan Stilwell. In Auberdine, the night elf Thundris Windweaver remembers the blacksmith with respect. Night elves keep their distance, and some fallen humans have betrayed their trust, yet Thundris still believes paladins can follow a righteous path. He tells them where ancient gems can be found. Blackfathom Deeps lies beneath the foggy northwestern coast of Ashenvale. Twilight's Hammer cultists and treacherous sea-dwellers inhabit its submerged halls. Naga priestesses there channel foul magic through ancient Kor gems. The gem you seek is deep within the temple complex, amid its dark halls and dangerous inhabitants.

quest:1454.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor tells you of Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck his ship in the northwest waters of Desolace, and he left a valuable chest behind and teleported away. The chest and what is inside are to be found. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor tells you of a first order of business. It concerns Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck Karnitol's ship in the northwest waters of Desolace. Karnitol and his servants tried to carry one of his costlier chests to shore, but the giants swarmed in, and he gave up the chest and teleported himself and his servants out. The chest and its contents are to be found, then returned to Karnitol in Stormwind. It lies along the northern coastline, in the Ethel Rethor stretch.

quest:1455.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. The chest of the mage Karnitol has been pried open, and it is completely empty. Long, deep scratches on its sides and top suggest neither man nor giant was responsible, and you return to Kreldig Ungor at Nijel's Point. You study what forced the chest open. Long, deep scratches run along its sides and top. They point to something that was neither man nor giant, and they do not look like the work of a dagger or sword. The chest is completely empty. With nothing else to be done, you close it and prepare to leave, knowing Kreldig Ungor will be disappointed.

quest:1456.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor still thinks Karnitol's belongings can be found. Up the same coast, by Ranazjar Isle, the Slitherblade naga hold a place among night elf ruins that lie at the bottom of the sea, and Kreldig reckons the satchel is most likely there. Following the second part of the Karnitol shipwreck search, Kreldig Ungor tells you hope is not lost. Along the same coast but farther north, close to Ranazjar Isle, sunken night elf ruins lie on the ocean floor, and the Slitherblade naga call them home. Kreldig judges it the likeliest place for Karnitol's satchel. A Recovery Diver's Potion is provided. Kreldig figures a scouting party that came so far south had to be a strong one. So in looking for Karnitol's belongings, Kreldig would try the more powerful naga first, the tidehunters and the sea witches.

quest:1457.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor sends you to Ironforge with Karnitol's satchel, to put it in the hands of Roetten Stonehammer, who will pay you for the work. Kreldig Ungor tells you to carry Karnitol's things back to Roetten Stonehammer in Ironforge, who will pay you for the work. With a laugh, Kreldig adds that Roetten may be so pleased that you get asked to join the Reclaimers full time. The way back should be made carefully and without dawdling, since Karnitol has little patience, though he is a generous man.

quest:1458.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor is gathering reagents for the gnome mage Leftwitch, who lives in Kharanos, and the Reclaimers are short-handed. He wants claws and horns from the Hatefury satyrs to the east before the rest of the list can begin. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor has another job on his hands: fetching reagents for Leftwitch, the gnome mage who lives in Kharanos. Roetten reckons it is easy coin, since the Reclaimers are already out in Desolace, and Kreldig says he does not care that the crew is short-handed. The first items on the list should be simple enough. Kreldig wants ten claws and ten horns taken from the Hatefury satyrs to the east, who are found in the Sargeron ruins due east of Nijel's Point. Once he has them, the rest of the list can begin.

quest:1459.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Next on Leftwitch's list for Kreldig Ungor is venom from the scorpashi and hides from aged kodo. Kreldig cannot say where to find either, since he does not know Desolace well. Following the first part of Leftwitch's list, Kreldig Ungor turns to the next items. They look simple enough, but the instructions are exact. The mage wants venom from the scorpashi, any of them will do, and hides from kodo, but only aged kodo. Dying and ancient kodo are no use. Kreldig wants seven vials of venom and three hides. Mages, Kreldig muses, ask for some odd things. Kreldig has no idea where the kodo and the scorpashi roam. Kreldig barely knows the area and has had no time to explore it.

quest:1465.text: Vahlarriel's Search. Going on with the search of the Malems' wagon, you turn up a pendant and a trail of footprints heading south. Smoke rises from a big fort far off. Vahlarriel Demonslayer at Nijel's Point should be shown the pendant and told about the sign that the Malems may live. Searching the wagon further, you turn up a pendant, and beyond it footprints leading south. Far off, smoke rises from a big fort. A tended fire makes it, not buildings burning, and your instincts say that if the Malems are still alive, they were taken that way. Vahlarriel Demonslayer at Nijel's Point should see the Malem Pendant, and should hear of the footprints leading south.

quest:1472.text: Devourer of Souls. Devourer of Souls is an introductory step in a Forsaken warlock's journey to summon and bind a succubus. Directed by Carendin Halgar in the Undercity's Temple of the Damned, the practitioner must confer with his assistant, Godrick Farsan, to learn how to lure such a creature from the Twisting Nether. The ritual demands an irresistible stimulus: the hearts of pure and loving mortals. Carendin Halgar teaches that a succubus cannot simply be pulled across the threshold on command; it must be enticed. Driven by an insatiable hunger to ruin virtue and consume mortal essence, the demon requires a specific lure. The warlock's strategy relies on exploiting this singular desire by offering up the hearts of genuinely virtuous, loving men as bait. Halgar directs his acolytes to Godrick Farsan, who knows where such rare quarry can be harvested. Located deeper within the Temple of the Damned, Godrick Farsan assists Carendin with the practical preparations of demonic binding. Though Farsan has lost his physical eyesight, he claims his condition grants him a profound second sight—allowing him to perceive underlying spiritual currents and far-off souls with uncanny clarity. He serves as the guide for locating the pure hearts necessary to draw the demon forth.

quest:1474.text: The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation in an Undercity warlock's journey to summon and command a succubus. Directed by Carendin Halgar, the practitioner uses pure hearts to draw a demon from the Twisting Nether into a ritual circle, subjugating its will through combat. Within the dark alcoves of the Magic Quarter, Forsaken warlocks refine their command over demonic entities. Summoning a succubus is considered a critical rite of passage. Unlike the brute force of a voidwalker or the minor malice of an imp, a succubus wields seductive and mental enchantments capable of ensnaring the caster. Carendin Halgar requires initiates to prove their mind and magic are ironclad before trusting them with permanent dominion over such an entity.

quest:1476.text: Hearts of the Pure. Hearts of the Pure is a sinister warlock trial assigned in the Undercity by Godrick Farsan on behalf of Carendin Halgar. In order to prepare the ritual bait needed to bind a succubus, an aspiring summoner must hunt down and butcher two uniquely righteous human men. Their pure hearts serve as an irresistible temptation for the demonic temptress awaiting summoning. Binding a succubus requires an understanding of temptation that cuts both ways. While the Nether's sirens prey upon desire and ruin, nothing draws them out of the Twisting Nether quite like untainted virtue ripe for corruption. Within the Temple of the Damned, master summoner Carendin Halgar delegates the groundwork to Godrick Farsan, who scours human lands for souls whose goodness remains pristine and unbroken. Farsan identifies two distinct paragons of virtue. The first is Dalin Forgewright, an honorable man attending to desperate Lordaeron refugees barred from sanctuary outside the sealed Greymane Wall in southern Silverpine. The second is Comar Villard, a faithful husband tirelessly searching the perilous marshlands of the Wetlands for any trace of his lost wife. To a Forsaken warlock, their devotion, empathy, and loyalty make them prime sacrifices.

quest:148.text: Supplies from Darkshire. Supplies from Darkshire is an Alliance quest in Duskwood where the hermit Abercrombie asks passing travelers to run an errand to Darkshire on his behalf. Claiming to be too frail to make the dangerous trek through the haunted forest, he seeks a rare material known as Ghost Hair Thread from Madame Eva. Isolated in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery in western Duskwood, the hermit Abercrombie cuts a pitiful figure. When approached by travelers, he laments his old age and frail body, claiming he cannot survive the journey through the woods to purchase goods from Darkshire. His requested errand appears simple: travel back to the township's town square and speak with Madame Eva to procure a spool of Ghost Hair Thread.

quest:1480.text: The Corrupter. A piece of flayed demon skin, taken from the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress, smells rotten yet is surprisingly pliable. Red markings of some language cover one side, and at the bottom is a clear symbol that looks like a signature. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may be able to tell you more. The torn skin stinks of rot, yet it bends easily, though it seems dry and fragile. Unrolled, it carries red markings on one side, a written language of some sort. At the bottom is a plain symbol, which you take to be a signature. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may know more about the skin. Maurin holds that the Burning Blade are coming to see how weak they are, with poor magic and little strength. Whatever power they have comes from those they serve, not from any grasp of true power and knowledge.

quest:1481.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, but first any wards the creature holds against scrying must be broken. For that, Maurin wants the scalp of a Hatefury shadowstalker, hunted in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, given the proper reagents. If the lord is as powerful as Maurin suspects, those must come from deadly creatures, and Maurin is sure you, acting in the Warchief's name, will take up the challenge. The first need is to break any wards the demon has against scrying. For that Maurin wants a scalp from a satyr, though only a Hatefury shadowstalker's will serve. They are to be sought in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast, near Sargeron. Maurin cautions you against bringing back the wrong scalp. The wrong reagents could get people killed, since the demon lord may carry contingency spells meant to slay anyone who tries to scry on him. Maurin adds that fate has already dealt out enough pain.

quest:1482.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter wants an oracle crystal, which the naga craft for their oracles, in order to find the demon lord Azrethoc. A vast coral reef lies northwest along the coast, home to the Slitherblade naga, and they will not welcome you. Maurin Bonesplitter says an oracle crystal will do the job of finding the demon lord Azrethoc, whose signature was on the skin you brought. Naga craft such crystals, and their oracles use them. Up the coast to the northwest lies a vast coral reef which the naga have made their home while near the shore, and the oracles can be found in that place. The Slitherblade there are deadly and will take your intrusion badly, so Maurin urges you to go carefully and quickly. Maurin points out that finding and destroying Lord Azrethoc would earn both of you much favor with the Warchief. Working together, and swiftly, would serve the ends of each.

quest:1483.text: Ziz Fizziks. This quest sends travelers from Ratchet to check on Ziz Fizziks, a disgruntled goblin engineer stationed on the western ridge of Windshear Crag. Offended when the Venture Company hired a gnome engineer over him, Ziz defected to the Tinkers' Union under Sputtervalve's demanding direction. The Venture Company relies on ruthless exploitation and mechanical innovation, but it crossed a line for Ziz Fizziks when it brought on a gnome engineer named Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. Deeply insulted by having to work alongside a gnomish rival, Ziz immediately sought a way out. He reached out to Sputtervalve, a contact representing the Tinkers' Union, begging for a transfer away from Gerenzo's oversight. Securing a new position with the Tinkers' Union did not grant Ziz the easy life he anticipated. Stationed on the western edge of Windshear Crag, he quickly discovered that Sputtervalve is just as much of a slave driver as any Venture Company foreman. Even so, Ziz considers heavy labor under a demanding goblin superior far preferable to sharing an engineering workshop with a gnome.

quest:1484.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter has found the demon lord far more dangerous than expected. He is certain Takata Steelblade doubts his abilities, and leaving the swordsman uninformed of what happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin sends you to speak with Takata, who is nearby. Maurin Bonesplitter finds the creature much more dangerous than he had anticipated. No doubt Takata Steelblade questions whether Maurin can handle it, and not being told of what just happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin asks you to speak to the swordsman and offer to slay the demon, should Takata allow it. Maurin cautions you not to press Takata too hard, since it is better if Takata believes the idea is his own. Takata Steelblade is close at hand, just across the path from Maurin, on a cliff overlooking the Kodo Graveyard.

quest:1487.text: Deviate Eradication. Deviate Eradication is a task assigned by the night elf druid Ebru above the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. While other disciples focus on waking their slumbering leader, Ebru asks adventurers to purge the caverns of mutated deviate beasts spawned by his twisted vision. Ridding the subterranean oasis of these horrors is an essential step in stemming the corruption threatening the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex brought his followers to the subterranean springs of the Barrens with an ambitious vision: tap into the Emerald Dream to regrow the parched plains into a lush, thriving woodland. Instead, Naralex became ensnared within the Dream, his slumber twisting into an agonizing nightmare. Rather than healing the land, the power surging through the caverns warped the native wildlife and plant life into monstrous, aggressive mutants known as deviate beasts. Perched in the cliff-face cavern overlooking the cave entrance, Ebru and a handful of surviving Disciples of Naralex watch in despair as their numbers dwindle. While some among them dedicate their energy toward awakening their fallen master, Ebru recognizes an immediate crisis. Left unchecked, the rapidly multiplying deviate vipers, shamblers, ravagers, and dreadfangs will spill outward into the Barrens. Ebru therefore recruits passing adventurers to descend into the deep tunnels and cull the aberrant monstrosities at their source.

quest:149.text: Ghost Hair Thread. Ghost Hair Thread is an errand undertaken for the fortune-teller Madame Eva in Darkshire. In order to gather the ghost hair she needs to spin Ghost Hair Thread, travelers are sent south to seek out Blind Mary, a tormented spirit who dwells in an abandoned farmhouse. By presenting her with an ethereal comb, one can gather the necessary strands from her ghostly tresses. Madame Eva of Darkshire requires specialized, otherworldly materials to spin Ghost Hair Thread for Abercrombie. Standard threads of linen and wool will not suffice for the rituals of Duskwood; instead, she requires ethereal strands harvested directly from a spirit. To secure this macabre component without violence, Eva provides a delicate Spectral Comb capable of passing through the veil of death to gather loose spectral hair. South of Darkshire, tucked away in the shadowy hills, lies an abandoned farmstead haunted by the wailing apparition known as Blind Mary. Consumed by self-loathing, the spirit constantly laments her hideous appearance and screams at intruders to avert their eyes, having torn out her own eyes in anguish over what she has become. The gift of the Spectral Comb offers her a fleeting moment of comfort, coaxing her to groom her ghostly hair despite her unending torment.

quest:150.text: Murloc Poachers. Dockmaster Baren of Lakeshire needs adventurers to thin the swelling ranks of murlocs along Lake Everstill before they deplete the town's primary food source. What begins as a practical pest-control bounty raises an unsettling ecological question: why are coastal creatures settling so deep into the inland mountains? Lake Everstill is the lifeblood of Lakeshire, keeping the mountain town fed and supplying its market with fresh catches. When large tribes of murlocs began dropping anchor along the shallows, Dockmaster Baren realized the town faced an ecological crisis. The ravenous fish-men were aggressively scouring the waters, threatening to wipe out the local fish populations entirely if left unchecked. Murlocs are typically coastal scavengers, making their massive presence high up in the Redridge Mountains an unusual sight. Dockmaster Baren openly wonders why they have traveled so far from the open ocean. Whether driven inland by maritime predators, fleeing territorial squabbles, or drawn by Lake Everstill's bountiful waters, their displacement hints at deeper disruptions elsewhere in the region.

quest:1505.text: Veteran Uzzek. Veteran Uzzek is a Horde quest that sends promising young warriors to seek out a seasoned combat instructor. Stationed just south of Far Watch Post between Durotar and the Barrens, Uzzek teaches new recruits that true martial greatness requires disciplined study as well as strength. In the culture of the Horde, martial strength is unquestioned and revered above all else. Yet brute force alone does not make a champion. Seasoned commanders know that the greatest warriors are also humble students of the craft, willing to hone their instincts through discipline and study. Aspiring fighters ready to advance beyond basic training are directed to seek out those who have survived the crucible of war. To receive advanced combat guidance, young fighters travel to the arid borderlands between Durotar and the Barrens. Just south of Far Watch Post, the fortified orc garrison watching the eastern frontier, resides Uzzek. A veteran of countless bloody conflicts, Uzzek now dedicates his years to mentoring promising new recruits in the vital arts of combat and tactical survival.

quest:1507.text: Devourer of Souls. Gan'rul Bloodeye sends an aspiring Horde warlock to begin the path to summoning and commanding a succubus. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the warlock seeks Cazul's counsel on luring and binding the demon. Horde warlocks who master lesser demons such as imps and voidwalkers may seek a succubus next. Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the dark arts beneath Orgrimmar and judges when a warlock is ready to call one from the Twisting Nether. A succubus can turn the frail against themselves, so binding one takes subtlety as well as strength. A succubus preys on mortal desire, so raw incantations cannot call one alone. The summoner must lure it with an object filled with pure love and devotion. Gan'rul is unwilling or unable to provide such a relic himself, so he sends the warlock across the Cleft of Shadow to Cazul. The ancient warlock knows the arcane and demonic rites needed for the next part of the ritual.

quest:1508.text: Blind Cazul. In the Cleft of Shadow, an initiate seeks Blind Cazul’s help with a succubus ritual. The sightless warlock points toward an object charged with mortal emotion. A succubus answers to mortal longing, sorrow, and desire. To draw one across the veil, an aspiring summoner needs more than willpower; the demon is known to devour souls. Blind Cazul understands what the initiate seeks and knows where to find a fitting lure. Though blind, Blind Cazul senses the lives and sorrows within Orgrimmar’s red ramparts. He sends the initiate to Zankaja, an orc woman who lives atop the bluffs near the wind rider roost. She anxiously awaits her mate Dogran’s return, and her despair can draw a demon’s attention.

quest:1509.text: News of Dogran. A missing grunt named Dogran leaves Zankaja waiting in Orgrimmar. His mate has heard nothing for days, so she sends you to question his superior, Gazrog, at the Crossroads. For a warlock, the search also serves a ritual to bind a succubus. Zankaja waits on the bluffs of Orgrimmar, fearing for her mate Dogran. He was sent to the Crossroads on an honorable promotion, but his return is overdue and she has heard nothing for days. She asks you to seek news from his commander, Gazrog. She does not know that dark arts are at work behind the search.

quest:1510.text: News of Dogran. This quest sends Horde adventurers deep into the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains to contact the Darkspear troll Ken'zigla at Malaka'jin. An injured grunt from Camp Taurajo named Dogran lies wounded, and the first runner sent to fetch a lifesaving herbal draught never returned. Dogran, a Horde grunt stationed at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens, was grievously wounded during a skirmish against entrenched quilboar. The grunts with him made it back and tried to rescue him, but his wounds had festered so badly that they were afraid to move him without patching him up first. Desperate for a potent remedy, Taurajo sent word north to the Crossroads, hoping to procure a traditional healing draught prepared by the jungle trolls of Malaka'jin.

quest:1511.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. Ken'zigla's Draught is an urgent courier task in the Horde warlock chain to summon a succubus. Entrusted with a potent medicinal concoction from Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, the warlock must rush across Kalimdor to Camp Taurajo to save an operative named Dogran. In the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, the troll apothecary Ken'zigla anticipated trouble. Knowing that an earlier emissary sent to secure medicine for the missing scout Dogran never made it back, Ken'zigla prepared a second dose of his potent restorative draught. The concoction is volatile and powerful: half a dose grants a mortally wounded soldier the vigor to move without causing his injuries to hemorrhage, while the rest must be withheld until the next day to complete recovery.

quest:1512.text: Love's Gift. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye awaits a pendant for the succubus rite. Dogran gives up a treasured keepsake after being found and revived in the Barrens. A warlock needs a talisman charged with strong, unblemished emotion to summon and control a succubus. These demons feed on mortal desire and twist genuine affection into anguish. Dogran's pendant bears his devotion and their parting. Bring it to Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar's shadowy clefts, where it is cleaned and polished. Its bright emotional force can draw the soul-devourer across the Twisting Nether.

quest:1513.text: The Binding. At Neeru Fireblade's circle in Orgrimmar, a warlock faces the trial of binding a succubus. Dogran's Pendant draws the demon from the Twisting Nether, where spellcraft and force of arms must break its will. Beneath the clefts of Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade keeps a tent with a circle prepared for dangerous rites. Under Gan'rul Bloodeye's guidance, you activate its runes and face the summoned succubus in battle. Calling a demon is only the beginning; you must overpower it alone and bend its spirit to your will.

quest:1515.text: Dogran's Captivity. At Camp Taurajo, a warlock faces a vital trial in Horde training: rescue a captured orc warrior. With Ken'zigla's Draught, you must find battered Grunt Dogran in a quilboar camp and give him strength to escape. Grunt Logmar at Camp Taurajo will not risk Horde soldiers in a costly attack on the entrenched quilboar. Dogran's fate rests with you, an aspiring warlock armed only with Ken'zigla's Draught. Travel north through the brambles and hostile camps to find where the quilboar hold him captive.

quest:1529.text: Call of Water. Call of Water is an initiation rite that directs rising Horde shaman from the heights of Thunder Bluff toward the eastern shores of the Barrens. To commune with the cleansing element of water, an initiate must seek out the recluse Islen Waterseer. This meeting marks the first step on a spiritual journey to earn the Water Totem. Having mastered the unyielding earth and the untamed flame, an aspiring shaman is eventually deemed ready to study the deeper mysteries of the elements. In Thunder Bluff, trainers like Xanis Flameweaver recognize when a student has shown enough discipline to approach the fluid, cleansing spirit of water. The journey requires leaving the windswept mesas of Mulgore behind and traveling east across the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens. The path leads to Islen Waterseer, a quiet mystic who lives away from the bustling settlements, residing in a humble fishing shack on the eastern coast south of Ratchet and the mouth of the Southfury River. Standing at the edge of the great ocean, Islen reads the readiness of travelers by how the elements linger about them. Seeing the steady earth, the brisk wind, and the warmth of fire already bound to the seeker's spirit, she prepares them for the trials required to understand water's purity.

quest:1530.text: Call of Water. Islen Waterseer sends Horde shamans south through the Barrens to seek Brine. There, they learn what water can cleanse and heal. Islen Waterseer teaches that water brings rebirth. Its flow can carve rock, wash away impurities, and mend flesh, but its healing depends on purity. Polluted water brings blight instead of life. Every shaman must understand this balance before seeking communion with water. You travel far south through the arid Barrens to find Brine. Quilboar raids trouble the wastes, yet Brine lives alone without guards or fear. She holds the knowledge and trials that help you bind yourself to water.

quest:1531.text: Call of Air. At Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder sends seasoned shamans south to seek the Air Totem. Prate Cloudseer guides them toward the final elemental pillar of their craft. A shaman who has earned the favor of earth, fire, and water now stands ready to harness air, the last of the four elements. In Orgrimmar, troll trainer Searn Firewarder recognizes when a disciple has reached the height of early training and is prepared for this final foundational step. He sends the shaman south across the Barrens, then down into the canyon labyrinth of Thousand Needles. Prate Cloudseer waits in a high cave among the sandstone mesas of Thousand Needles. The hermit lives quietly with her partner, far from Horde encampments. She demands deference before revealing the secrets of the wind. Meet her with proper respect, and she shares the knowledge and focus to manifest the Air Totem, completing the shaman's elemental circle.

quest:1532.text: Call of Air. Call of Air marks a major milestone in a Horde shaman's spiritual path, directing them to seek communion with the unpredictable element of wind. Offered by Xanis Flameweaver in Thunder Bluff, this quest bids seasoned initiates journey south into Thousand Needles to learn from Prate Cloudseer. Mastering air grants a shaman the sacred totem required to channel the swiftest forces of nature. Having already attuned to the stability of earth, the ferocity of fire, and the restorative depths of water, a shaman reaches the final elemental pillar: air. Xanis Flameweaver, guiding practitioners from the heights of Thunder Bluff, acknowledges that the winds are far more fickle and difficult to control than the previous elements. The trial demands humility, focus, and an innate respect for the sky's tempestuous nature. To attune to the winds, the shaman must travel south past the vast plains of the Barrens and descend into the wind-carved canyons of Thousand Needles. There, far to the east, dwells the hermit mystic Prate Cloudseer. Tucked away in a secluded cliffside cave where the canyon drafts howl day and night, she tests the initiate's preparedness before bestowing the Air Totem, the instrument essential for summoning gusts, lightning, and swift wind spirits.

quest:1534.text: Call of Water. A shaman travels from the Barrens to the Ruins of Stardust for the final gathering trial in the journey to earn Call of Water. Brine sends the initiate north into Ashenvale to draw pure water from its ancient fountain. After gathering water from the pool below Brine’s hut in the Barrens and the pure well of Tarren Mill, the shaman needs one final essence. Brine sends the initiate north across the dry plains and into Ashenvale, an ancient woodland sacred to the night elves. The dry Barrens give way to Ashenvale’s deep canopy, where water takes another form. A shaman must understand this variety to live in harmony with the element. Beyond the shimmering waters of Mystral Lake, near the mountain pass between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains, lie the Ruins of Stardust. An ancient fountain rests among quiet waters and old stones in this secluded elven sanctum. Untamed elemental and nature spirits guard the ruins and resent intruders. The shaman must tread carefully to draw water from the fountain.

quest:1535.text: Call of Water. Brine sends shamans into the Barrens to gather water for a sapta. The trial begins with a sample from the guarded pool below her hill, where water means survival. Brine asks shaman initiates to study water in all its forms before she grants the water sapta that lets them commune with the spirits. In the arid Barrens, water means the difference between survival and starvation. She asks them to notice what water makes possible: forests flourish where it flows, deserts starve where it is absent, and living beings will kill to protect even the humblest spring. Native quilboar fiercely guard the watering hole beneath Brine's hill. They treat every pool as a priceless hoard and feast whenever rain comes. Brine regrets the violence their hoarding brings, but their insular greed and divided clans keep their threat contained. For the other races surviving on the plains, that leaves a precarious balance.

quest:1536.text: Call of Water. You set out from the Barrens for a pure spring in Forsaken-held Tarren Mill. The water will help Brine prepare the Water Sapta, and its survival offers a lesson in hope. Brine sends you across the sea to Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills for water to prepare the Water Sapta. Human resistance and the newly allied Forsaken surround the town, yet its small central well gives pure spring water. To Brine, the spring is a sacred remnant of cleanliness in an unhallowed land. Brine sees the pure well in Tarren Mill as more than an ingredient. She compares its endurance to Warchief Thrall, who bore hardship, captivity, and sorrow before rising to lead the orcish people. Thrall gives the Horde hope, and the well shows that life and purity can endure through tragedy and corruption.

quest:154.text: Return the Comb. Return the Comb is an Alliance errand in Duskwood that concludes the haunting transaction with the spirit Blind Mary. After being presented with a comb to harvest strands of her spectral hair, the tortured ghost is overcome with despair over her lost beauty and casts the implement away. Returning the hair-laden comb to Madame Eva allows the mystic to spin the ethereal Ghost Hair Thread. Blind Mary lingers in a decrepit shack south of Darkshire, eternally mourning her tragic death and changed state. When approached with Madame Eva's comb, the reminder of mundane grooming only deepens her sorrow. Realizing she is now nothing more than an apparition—a monster stripped of mortal grace whom no one will ever love again—she recoils in horror, thrusting the comb and the ghostly hair tangled in its teeth back into the traveler's hands. Madame Eva awaits the return of the comb in Darkshire, well aware of the macabre nature of the task. With the ghostly hair secured, the fortune teller possesses the rare spiritual medium necessary to spin a spool of Ghost Hair Thread. Eva spins these ethereal fibers into thread, paying travelers for any stray hairs left over from the delicate spinning process.

quest:156.text: Gather Rot Blossoms. Tavernkeep Smitts of Darkshire requires rot blossoms to concoct a batch of his infamous 'zombie juice'. These macabre flora sprout directly from the decaying skulls of skeletal horrors and fiends prowling Duskwood's restless graveyards. While most barkeeps pride themselves on aged ales and fine wines, Tavernkeep Smitts of the Scarlet Raven Tavern occasionally brews more unsettling fare. His recipe for 'zombie juice' demands rot blossoms—foul, necrotic vegetation that takes root within the empty skulls of animated skeletons. Smitts himself is sensible enough never to get close to the undead, leaving the gruesome harvest to passing mercenaries. Gathering these blooms requires cutting down the skeletal horrors and fiends wandering the overgrown plots of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery or the vast expanse of Raven Hill Cemetery. Duskwood's local militia, the Night Watch, is perpetually stretched thin fighting back the creeping terrors of the woods. Smitts ensures that any adventurer braving the tombstones is duly commended to Commander Althea Ebonlocke for culling the restless dead.

quest:157.text: Deliver the Thread. Deliver the Thread is an Alliance errand in Duskwood that ferries a spool of Ghost Hair Thread from Madame Eva in Darkshire across the haunted forest to Abercrombie. The eccentric hermit living near Raven Hill Cemetery claims he needs the enchanted thread to ward his ramshackle hut against restless spirits. However, Madame Eva's dark remarks about the thread hint that there may be far more sinister uses for it. Once Madame Eva finishes spinning spectral hair gathered from the ghost Blind Mary, she entrusts the Ghost Hair Thread to any traveler willing to carry it west. The journey requires crossing the shadowed expanse of Duskwood, slipping past lurking spiders and roaming undead to reach Abercrombie's dilapidated shack just north of the vast cemetery grounds.

quest:158.text: Zombie Juice. Zombie Juice is an errand run on behalf of Abercrombie, the peculiar hermit dwelling in the haunted wilds of Duskwood. Claiming to suffer from the oppressive midnight chill, he dispatches travelers to Darkshire's tavern to secure an unusually potent concoction. Dwelling alone among the horrors of the shadowed woods, the hermit Abercrombie frequently sends sympathetic travelers on strange errands. Claiming that the creeping dusk drains his warmth and vitality, he asks that an adventurer make the trek east to Darkshire. His target is Tavernkeep Smitts of the Scarlet Raven Tavern, from whom he seeks a bottle of a potent, ominously named brew known as Zombie Juice to put fire back in his veins. Darkshire's tavern sees plenty of weary guards and frightened townsfolk, but requests for Zombie Juice are rare even for Tavernkeep Smitts. The drink carries a reputation for being dangerously strong. While Smitts recognizes the vintage, Abercrombie's thirst for such a morbid concoction raises quiet eyebrows in a region already besieged by the restless dead.

quest:159.text: Juice Delivery. Juice Delivery is an errand running between Darkshire and the western edge of Duskwood. Tavernkeep Smitts entrusts you with a potent concoction known as Zombie Juice to deliver to the reclusive hermit, Abercrombie. While ostensibly meant to keep the shivering old man warm, the brew's uncanny potency raises eyebrows. Tavernkeep Smitts of Darkshire brews a legendary draught known colloquially as Zombie Juice. When the order is finally filled, Smitts hands over the bottle with a stern warning to handle it gingerly, remarking that the concoction is stout enough to raise the dead. For a tired adventurer running errands across a haunted forest, delivering high-proof moonshine to an eccentric loner feels like routine charity.

quest:160.text: Note to the Mayor. Note to the Mayor is an Alliance errand in Duskwood that links the eccentric hermit Abercrombie to the leadership of Darkshire. After aiding the reclusive old man, adventurers are asked to hand-deliver a personal message to Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke. However, the missive immediately stirs suspicion rather than warmth. After helping Abercrombie recover his stolen chest from the ogres of the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, the hermit sends you back down the mist-shrouded roads toward town. Cackling with delight, Abercrombie claims that he and Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke are old friends. He insists that upon discovering what the adventurer has accomplished, the mayor will be just as thrilled as he is.

quest:163.text: Raven Hill. Reports of shifting shadows and flickering window light in the abandoned settlement of Raven Hill have set the Night Watch on edge. Dispatched by Elaine Carevin in Darkshire, travelers are sent west across the haunted woods to confront whatever sinister presence has taken shelter among the ruins. To the rangers of the Night Watch, the far western edge of Duskwood has long been surrendered to the dead and the wilderness. Yet complete abandonment would be preferable to unexpected activity. Calor, a watcher patrolling the gloomy roads, noticed movement among the silent houses of Raven Hill two nights in a row, punctuated by the unsettling flicker of a lantern in a window. In a land plagued by ghouls, skeletons, and beasts, any unexplained signs of life demand immediate investigation.

quest:164.text: Deliveries to Sven. Deliveries to Sven is an Alliance task given by Elaine Carevin in Darkshire, requesting that vital provisions be carried out to a lonely camp on the northwest frontier of Duskwood. There, Sven Yorgen and his few remaining followers wage a desperate, solitary struggle against the horrors of the blighted woods. The errand connects town folk struggling in the gloom with an isolated band on the edge of the wilderness. While Darkshire barely holds its own walls against wolves, spiders, and the restless dead, some refuse to cower behind palisades. Sven Yorgen and a meager handful of companions established a solitary encampment along the northwestern perimeter of Duskwood. So pressed are they by constant danger that they cannot spare a single man to make the perilous trek back to town for provisions. Elaine Carevin steps in to coordinate aid, relying on brave travelers to ensure these frontier fighters do not starve. The Carevin family holds high regard for Sven, viewing his fierce stand as true devotion to the Light. Elaine's willingness to organize and dispatch supplies highlights the quiet networks of survival that keep Duskwood from completely collapsing into shadow. When Sven receives the crate, he recognizes the enduring support of the Carevins, though his thoughts remain consumed by the grim battle at hand.

quest:1649.text: The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall awaits paladins seeking trials of faith and courage in Stormwind. The Tome of Valor guides their first steps toward proving their devotion to the Church. The Tome of Valor teaches that valor must be forged through hardship. Its sacred text compares virtues to precious ores, valuable when found but needing refinement to endure. Through hard trials and true commitment, a paladin binds faith, compassion, and courage into a strength that can resist the evils threatening Azeroth. After reading the Tome of Valor, you are directed to Duthorian Rall, a respected leader among the paladins in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. He hears petitions from those seeking the trials of valor. The tests are no mere ritual: defending the innocent and upholding the Church may demand your life, and only the steadfast earn recognition in the order.

quest:165.text: The Hermit. Concerned by the prolonged absence of an elderly recluse, Elaine Carevin in Darkshire asks travelers to check on him. The lonely old man, Abercrombie, lives in a rickety shack perched right on the edge of Raven Hill Cemetery. In a beleaguered settlement like Darkshire, it is easy to lose track of eccentric loners until their absence becomes alarming. Elaine Carevin recalls an old man who once regularly trekked into town for provisions before abruptly vanishing from sight. Given the relentless dangers haunting the roads of Duskwood, she directs wandering adventurers to inspect his shack overlooking the haunted expanse of Raven Hill Cemetery to make sure he hasn't met a grim fate. Reaching the lonely hut reveals that its resident, an old man named Abercrombie, is still among the living. He chuckles softly at the mention of the Carevins, claiming that his long absence is merely the consequence of advancing age and the treacherous monsters prowling the woods. Relieved to find an able traveler at his door, Abercrombie wastes no time in asking whether they might run a few helpful errands for him.

quest:1650.text: The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall sends a paladin to protect Daphne Stilwell on Westfall's distant shore. With her husband away, Defias bandits threaten her homestead. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall tests aspiring paladins by asking them to defend the realm's people. After accepting the mantle of valor, you put those ideals to work where law and authority have failed. Daphne Stilwell and her husband Jordan keep an outpost at Westfall's isolated Longshore. Jordan is away in Ironforge, consulting dwarven blacksmiths, and Defias Brotherhood activity is rampant. Duthorian sends you west to protect Daphne before the thieves overwhelm her homestead.

quest:1651.text: The Tome of Valor. At Daphne Stilwell's farm in Westfall, a paladin faces a trial of valor. The Defias Brotherhood is pressing the homestead, and Daphne needs a defender at her side. Daphne Stilwell's homestead in Westfall lies in land contested by the Defias Brotherhood. While seeking the virtues recorded in the Tome of Valor, you are sent to defend her farm. The Defias have tried repeatedly to overrun the property and kill Daphne. After earlier clashes, another attack is expected. You must stand beside her house instead of retreating to safer ground. Daphne and you face wave after wave of Defias raiders. She has only her personal firearm, while you have the blessings of the Holy Light. The fight tests whether you can protect someone vulnerable under heavy pressure. True valor is not the pursuit of personal glory, but the willingness to stand between innocent civilians and ruthless violence.

quest:1652.text: The Tome of Valor. At the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, word returns that Daphne Stilwell is safe. After defending her Westfall homestead from bandits, an aspiring paladin reports to Duthorian Rall, completing the Church of the Holy Light's trials of valor. The Church's charge is to shield the innocent without thought for oneself. Daphne Stilwell's homestead in Westfall is safe after an initiate of the Church of the Holy Light defended it from bandits. Back at the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, the aspiring paladin reports her safety to Duthorian Rall. The defense shows the courage and conviction expected of one who stands between danger and the defenseless. Daphne's husband, Jordan Stilwell, is in Ironforge, where he lends his renowned craftsmanship to the Alliance. With Daphne safe and the homestead guarded, Duthorian Rall prepares to send word north to Jordan. Reassured that his family is protected, the artisan can focus on his work. Their distant homes are bound by the aid the Alliance gives across its lands.

quest:1653.text: The Test of Righteousness. In Ironforge, glad tidings bring Jordan Stilwell news of his wife. Duthorian Rall sends you from Westfall to tell the devout smith that Daphne survived the Defias attack. Duthorian Rall sends you from Cathedral Square with news for Jordan Stilwell. You have guarded Daphne Stilwell through a Defias ambush at her Westfall homestead, and she survived. Her husband left for Ironforge believing his family was in danger. Rall asks you to carry the news in person, so Jordan can know his wife is safe. Jordan Stilwell was once destined to join the paladins, but chose to follow his father's craft as a master weaponsmith. He works at his anvil outside Ironforge's gates, keeping his faith as he shapes weapons. When you tell him Daphne survived the Defias attack, gratitude moves him to help you forge a blessed weapon of righteousness.

quest:1654.text: The Test of Righteousness. The Test of Righteousness represents a defining trial for rising paladins seeking a sanctified weapon of the Light. The master weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell offers to craft an extraordinary holy armament, tasking the champion with scouring distant lands for rare smithing components, including his lost family hammer. Outside the grand gates of Ironforge, Jordan Stilwell seeks a worthy companion of the Light. Recognising the deeds of a rising paladin, the smith proposes a sacred pact: he will forge a legendary weapon that stands as an enduring symbol of devotion, provided the paladin undertakes the perilous legwork required to secure the master-grade materials. Crafting a weapon fit to channel the Light demands ingredients from across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Stilwell's design requires four distinct items: sturdy Whitestone Oak lumber, refined ore from master prospectors, a purified Kor Gem thrumming with raw power, and the reclamation of Jordan's own smithing hammer, left behind when he escaped Shadowfang Keep. Tracking them down forces the paladin to test their mettle against distant threats.

quest:1655.text: Bailor's Ore Shipment. Bailor's Ore Shipment is a task undertaken by paladins seeking refined metal for Jordan Stilwell's sanctified weapon. The shipment of alloy was plundered by the Mo'grosh ogres during an ambush along the roadway from the Wetlands. When Jordan Stilwell required a specialized shipment of ore refined by his old friend Bailor Stonehand, the delivery never made it safely into Ironforge's hands. While winding its way southward out of the Wetlands into Loch Modan, the supply caravan was ambushed and slaughtered by the Mo'grosh ogres. The last surviving guard managed to limp into camp only to succumb to his injuries shortly after, leaving the shipment lost in ogre territory. Bailor Stonehand, camped in Loch Modan, directs paladins across the waters of the Loch toward the northeastern hills. There, among the encampments of the Mo'grosh ogres, the stolen crate of alloy sits abandoned as plunder. Recovering the crate proves a paladin's resolve to venture into hostile territory, allowing Bailor to honor his original agreement with Jordan Stilwell.

quest:1656.text: A Task Unfinished. A Task Unfinished is a simple delivery quest highlighting the strain young tauren endure during their coming-of-age rites on Red Cloud Mesa. Overburdened by the demands of their trials and a filial chore, an exhausted youth asks a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down to Innkeeper Kauth in Bloodhoof Village. High upon Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren face rigorous trials of passage to prove their readiness for the wider world. Balancing traditional rites against ordinary tribal chores can push a youth to the brink of physical exhaustion. Faced with an unfinished Rite of Strength and an urgent chore from their father, one young tauren seeks the aid of a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down the mesa. The destination for the furs is Bloodhoof Village, a welcoming haven resting in the open plains below. Innkeeper Kauth eagerly receives the delivery, intending to turn the pelt bundle into warm blankets for weary wanderers. The errand highlights both the hospitality of the plains tauren and the importance of rest, showing that community support underpins every solitary trial of strength.

quest:166.text: The Defias Brotherhood. This mission represents the culmination of Gryan Stoutmantle's long campaign to reclaim Westfall from outlaw rule. Tasked with entering the Deadmines, Alliance champions must breach the criminal hideout and strike down the mastermind Edwin VanCleef himself. For months, Gryan Stoutmantle and the beleaguered People's Militia have fought a desperate holding action against the Defias Brotherhood across Westfall. With the true location of the thieves' stronghold uncovered beneath Moonbrook, Stoutmantle issues his final, grim decree: Edwin VanCleef must be assassinated to break the back of the rebellion once and for all.

quest:167.text: Oh Brother. . .. "Oh Brother. . ." is an Alliance mission given by Wilder Thistlenettle in Stormwind City. Distraught over a cave-in during an expedition into the depths beneath Moonbrook, Wilder asks adventurers to search the labyrinthine mines for his missing sibling, Foreman Thistlenettle, or recover his Explorers' League Badge. Wilder Thistlenettle and his brother entered the cavernous subterranean tunnels beneath Moonbrook as members of a mining company. However, things turned catastrophic when hostile thieves swarmed the area and a violent cave-in sealed off the lower tunnels. Wilder managed to escape to Stormwind, but his brother and the rest of the crew were left trapped behind the rubble.

quest:169.text: Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg. Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg is an Alliance bounty posted in Redridge Mountains targeting the warlord behind the Blackrock invasion of Stonewatch. Magistrate Solomon offers a generous reward for anyone daring enough to assault the conquered keep and bring back the commander's severed head. Gath'Ilzogg is the brutal commander directing Blackrock clan raids across the Redridge Mountains. Under his direction, the orcs stormed and conquered Stonewatch Keep, turning a former human bastion into a fortified staging ground for assaults on the surrounding settlements. From the keep's highest ramparts, he plots further incursions into Lakeshire, threatening to cut Redridge off from the rest of the kingdom. With Stormwind's royal army failing to deploy reinforcements to the border regions, Magistrate Solomon has taken matters into his own hands. The township of Lakeshire simply lacks the military manpower to retake Stonewatch Keep by force. By posting a public bounty on Gath'Ilzogg, Solomon aims to decapitate the Blackrock leadership and spark the first stage of reclaiming the keep for the crown.

quest:1698.text: Yorus Barleybrew. At the Lakeshire Inn, Yorus Barleybrew awaits Alliance warriors bold enough to answer his challenge. Trainers across Alliance capitals send seasoned fighters from Stormwind toward the Redridge borderlands to meet the eccentric dwarf and face his test of arms. Across Alliance capitals, warrior trainers watch fighters who have outgrown their first drills. When an apprentice proves their mettle around their twentieth season, trainers such as Kelv Sternhammer, Wu Shen, and Darnath Bladesinger pass along word of Yorus Barleybrew. The dwarf offers no standard military order. Instead, he has issued an open wager and a test of arms to any Alliance warrior bold enough to answer. Yorus Barleybrew waits at the tavern in Lakeshire, on the front lines of Redridge's struggle against encroaching gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Those who find him meet a boastful dwarf with a hearty drink in hand, ready to judge any challenger who claims true fighting spirit. For warriors seeking to prove themselves beyond the capital's safe cobbled streets, his trial opens onto the harsher battles of the frontier.

quest:1699.text: The Rethban Gauntlet. The Rethban Gauntlet is an eccentric endurance trial devised by the dwarven brewer Yorus Barleybrew in Lakeshire. Challengers must drink a potent swig of his family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder and sprint north into the gnoll-infested Rethban Caverns and back before an hour elapses. In the town of Lakeshire, where grim talk of gnoll raids and missing town guards usually dominates the inn, the dwarf Yorus Barleybrew brings a distinctly dwarven flavor of entertainment. His self-styled challenge, the Rethban Gauntlet, tests an adventurer's mettle, speed, and liver all at once. Participants are required to down a draught of his family's signature concoction, Barleybrew Scalder, right before setting off on foot toward the northern foothills. The trial is far more perilous than a simple drunken footrace. Between Lakeshire and the destination lies Redridge territory teeming with aggressive Redridge gnolls. To successfully complete the gauntlet, the runner must fight or slip past the packs, reach the first fork inside the dark tunnels of Rethban Caverns, and hustle back to Yorus within an hour—all while battling the overwhelming, staggering effects of the fiery dwarven alcohol.

quest:1700.text: Grimand Elmore. Following the creation of specialized armor, the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard sends a copy of his findings across the district to Grimand Elmore. The brief errand carries technical notes between two headstrong weaponsmiths sharing space in Stormwind City. Having forged the specialized Fire Hardened Mail, Furen Longbeard documents the intricate heat-treating techniques and elemental principles he uncovered during the process. Rather than keeping the knowledge entirely to himself, he commits the notes to parchment and tasks an adventurer with delivering them straight to Grimand Elmore, a seasoned crafter operating out of a nearby weapon shop. Grimand Elmore's immediate reaction upon receiving the manuscript is wounded pride. Adamant that he taught Furen everything the younger dwarf knows, Grimand bristles at the notion that his former pupil could offer him instruction. Despite his outward indignation, the craftsman cannot resist perusing the text, quickly finding an intriguing idea hidden within the notes that he is eager to test for himself.

quest:1701.text: Fire Hardened Mail. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard has a new armor design for an Alliance warrior. The dwarf armorer offers to forge Fire Hardened Mail if the warrior brings him rare materials from both continents. Furen Longbeard has forged an exceptional buckler for the aspiring warrior and now proposes a greater work: mail made to withstand fierce blows. His craft calls for more than iron or steel. He needs rare materials touched by elemental heat and natural resilience. Furen cannot leave his Stormwind forge, so the warrior seeking the armor must gather these dangerous ingredients. Furen sends the warrior to distant wilds and dangerous depths for the parts he needs. The recipe calls for fangs from venomous spiders in the damp crevices of the Wetlands, along with scorched and galvanized horns from fierce chimaeras in the Stonetalon Mountains. To bind and temper those beast parts into mail, Furen also needs volatile phlogiston from Roogug, a geomancer deep within Razorfen Kraul's thorny maze in the Barrens.

quest:1702.text: The Shieldsmith. In Stormwind, Yorus Barleybrew sends warriors back after a harrowing trial in the Redridge Mountains. He gives them a cask of Barleybrew Scalder to take to Furen Longbeard, who will fashion a stout shield. After you prove your mettle against the gnolls and perils of the Rethban Gauntlet, Yorus Barleybrew honors his bargain. The promised reward cannot be hammered out in Lakeshire, so he directs promising fighters back to Stormwind City. A dwarven armorer there stands ready to repay a personal debt. Yorus gives you a heavy cask of Barleybrew Scalder instead of a letter of credit. Take it to Furen Longbeard in Stormwind's Dwarven District, where soot and hammer-clatter fill the air. The seasoned smith recognizes the name behind the delivery and lends his craft to a warrior seeking a stout shield.

quest:1703.text: Mathiel. Furen Longbeard sends his crafting notes across the sea to Mathiel in Darnassus. The night elf smith works on the Warrior's Terrace, where dwarven mail forging may reach a new pair of hands. Furen Longbeard has mastered the forging of fire-hardened armor and chooses to share what he has learned with other Alliance craftsmen. He copies his technical diagrams and sends you across the continents to Mathiel, a smith on Teldrassil. On Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace, Mathiel tends a forge for the Sentinels and other fighters who defend the night elf capital. Furen's notes carry dwarven methods from the underground forges of Khaz Modan to kaldorei armorers, whose craft is shaped by their bond with nature.

quest:1704.text: Klockmort Spannerspan. This quest sends an adventurer from Stormwind to Ironforge to deliver trade secrets to Klockmort Spannerspan in Tinkertown. After mastering the art of fire-hardened armor, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard eagerly shares his metallurgical discoveries with his gnomish colleague. It serves as an essential link in the journey of an aspiring warrior looking to test exotic crafting methods. Having successfully forged a set of fire-hardened mail, Furen Longbeard compiles his detailed findings to pass along to a fellow craftsman. Rather than hoarding his newly discovered techniques, Furen trusts you to carry his notes from Stormwind to Ironforge and into the clatter and steam of Tinkertown, where the gnomish blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan plies his trade. Gnome blacksmiths are relatively rare compared to their dwarven hosts, and Klockmort is enthusiastic about pushing the boundaries of traditional metalwork. Upon inspecting Furen's notes, Klockmort becomes wildly excited over the breakthrough, eager to integrate these fiery techniques into his own exotic projects.

quest:1705.text: Burning Blood. In Stormwind, Grimand Elmore turns to Furen Longbeard’s smithing methods. He needs burning blood and a burning rock from Duskwood to test the armorcrafting technique himself. Grimand Elmore is one of the Alliance’s accomplished armorers, and he rarely accepts that another smith might surpass his methods. Hearing of Furen Longbeard’s unusual smithing discoveries stirs his professional curiosity. Grimand agrees to test Furen’s methods by making a piece of armor. He needs strange, volatile components from the dark reaches of the south to quench and temper the metal to his exact requirements; ordinary water and common coals will not do. Grimand sends you to Duskwood, to the abandoned mine called Roland’s Doom. Savage Nightbane worgen have overrun its tunnels, their cursed veins pulsing with burning ichor. He needs vials of their burning blood and a rare, flaming core called a burning rock, carried by the pack’s leader, Gutspill. Bring these scorching materials back so Grimand can test Furen’s methods at the forge.

quest:1706.text: Grimand's Armor. In Stormwind, Grimand's Armor takes shape through a test of Furen Longbeard's methods. Grimand Elmore crafts a helm from rare materials, meant to endure punishing blows in battle. For an Alliance warrior, it marks a step toward mastery. Grimand Elmore tests Furen Longbeard's daring smithing methods at his forge in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Grimand had doubted the dwarven master armorer's theories. To put them to the test, a warrior gathers rare elemental and beast components in hostile territory and brings them to Grimand. He uses the materials to forge a reinforced helm built to endure crushing impacts. Grimand's finished coif shows that Furen's metallurgic insights were sound. He treats the metal to withstand pressure and physical blows that would warp ordinary steel. Grimand gives the coif to the warrior who helped him, honoring Furen's craft and the warrior's resolve. The armor can help them hold the frontline against Azeroth's greatest threats.

quest:1708.text: Iron Coral. Iron Coral is an Alliance quest given by the gnome blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan in Tinker Town, Ironforge. Eager to test newly shared smithing methods on a custom suit of armor, Klockmort sends you to dive for rare searing coral along the coast of the Wetlands. Completing his request allows him to fuse gnomish ingenuity with dwarven craftsmanship. After exchanging insights with the master dwarven smith Furen Longbeard, Klockmort Spannerspan is bursting with inspiration. The eccentric gnome blacksmith wants to combine Furen's metallurgy with his own tinkering ideas to craft an exceptionally resilient suit of armor. To pull off this daring metallurgical experiment, standard mountain ores will not suffice; Klockmort requires an unusual, naturally hardened marine element known as searing coral. Searing coral is a volatile, tough oceanic deposit found in only one specific region: submerged off the coast south of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Retrieving twenty clusters means wading through treacherous marshland waters, braving native aquatic predators, and hauling the dripping harvests back to Ironforge. For Klockmort, however, the prize is well worth the damp excursion, as he intends to smelt and hammer the coral directly into his experimental plating.

quest:1709.text: Klockmort's Creation. Klockmort's Creation marks the successful forging of a specialized suit of armor in Ironforge's Tinker Town. Utilizing an unconventional technique devised by the master armorsmith Furen Longbeard, the gnome blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan shapes raw materials into an extraordinarily resilient piece of gear. Forging heavy armor typically belongs to the great anvils of the Great Forge, but Klockmort Spannerspan operates out of Tinker Town. The creation of this armor represents a collaborative triumph between dwarven metallurgical tradition and gnomish mechanical innovation. By adapting Furen Longbeard's rigorous methods, Klockmort finishes a pair of armored gauntlets engineered to endure punishment that would crush ordinary steel. According to Klockmort, the resulting armor boasts structural integrity so great that a siege engine could roll directly over it without causing permanent distortion. The secret lies in the peculiar treatment of rare components, proving that combining ancient dwarven forging techniques with gnomish ingenuity yields armor capable of withstanding the fiercest frontline battles.

quest:1710.text: Sunscorched Shells. In Darnassus, Mathiel seeks wyvern eggshells to strengthen a new mailcrafting technique. The armorer works with the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard and sends warriors to gather shells from Highperch in Thousand Needles. Mathiel works from the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus and looks beyond night elven methods. He corresponds with Furen Longbeard, a skilled dwarven armorer in Stormwind, and draws on Furen's discoveries in metalwork and armor-smithing. Mathiel hopes to make mail reinforced with natural materials that can withstand great strain. To test the idea, he needs materials found nowhere near Teldrassil. Mathiel's experiment calls for shells from Highperch, far south across the sea in the canyon gorges of Thousand Needles. Wyverns nest high above the salt flats and red stone mesas, beneath Kalimdor's blazing sun. Constant exposure to heat and altitude hardens their eggshells. Mathiel plans to grind the sun-baked fragments into a resilient lacquer and coat chainmail links, making armor that bends while enduring exceptional strain.

quest:1711.text: Mathiel's Armor. At the forge in Darnassus, Mathiel's Armor brings night elf and dwarven craft together. Mathiel works in the Warrior's Terrace, using methods devised by Furen Longbeard to shape exotic materials into armor for Alliance warriors. Night elf armorers have favored methods honed over millennia, with work shaped by nature, supple leathers, and carefully worked metals. Trade with the Eastern Kingdoms has led smiths such as Mathiel to try new ways. He brings the dwarven techniques devised by Furen Longbeard together with elven craft. Mathiel needs sunscorched eggshells from the Highperch wyvern nests in Thousand Needles. He renders the sun-hardened shells into lacquer and uses Furen's heat-treatment formulas to forge resilient leggings for the front lines.

quest:1712.text: Cyclonian. Cyclonian is a mighty wind lord whose defeat has been sought for ages. To challenge him, a champion must gather the components required to summon the elemental and strike him down to claim his whirlwind heart. Defeating the wind lord allows the heart's power to be infused into a formidable weapon. Cyclonian is a raging elemental wind lord whose presence commands reverence and caution. For ages, an attentive watcher has kept vigil over the summoning site, waiting for a combatant possesses enough raw martial prowess to challenge and destroy this tempestuous entity. Calling forth Cyclonian requires a ritual of summoning using rare materials detailed upon a special parchment. Once summoned, the wind lord must be faced in direct combat, testing whether the challenger is truly a champion or merely another victim of his howling gale.

quest:1716.text: Devourer of Souls. An Alliance warlock crosses the sea to seek Takar the Seer’s counsel on summoning a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder sends Stormwind initiates into the Barrens for the wisdom they need. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder guides promising warlocks toward summoning a succubus. The demon devours souls, destroys hearts, and dominates minds, so it cannot be called blindly into Azeroth. A warlock needs a potent lure: an object tied to pure love. That token draws the succubus from the Twisting Nether, where the warlock can defeat and bind it. Stormwind’s covens cannot teach them where to find such an object. Gakin sends his pupils across the Great Sea to Kalimdor in search of the needed catalyst. Takar the Seer waits in the arid Barrens, near the Horde settlement of Camp Taurajo. To reach him, an Alliance warlock must cross wilderness patrolled by hostile centaur, quilboar, and Horde warriors. The journey tests whether a summoner can survive before the ritual even begins.

quest:1717.text: Gakin's Summons. A summons delivered to promising Alliance warlocks in Ironforge, directing them south to Stormwind. Gakin the Darkbinder awaits beneath the city's Mage Quarter to oversee their advancement into commanding greater fiends. Demonology remains a practice conducted entirely in shadows across Alliance lands. In Ironforge, Lago Blackwrench quietly keeps tabs on wandering practitioners on behalf of the brotherhood in Stormwind. When a warlock shows sufficient mastery over their initial minions, word travels quickly. Lago passes along the directive: drop whatever business keeps you in the snowy mountains of Khaz Modan and report south without delay. Deep beneath the cobblestones of Stormwind's Mage Quarter, beneath the tavern known as The Slaughtered Lamb, Gakin the Darkbinder coordinates the development of the city's warlocks. Gakin views every capable student as a valuable, hazardous investment. Receiving his summons marks the threshold of true demonic binding, beginning the trials required to subjugate a succubus from the Twisting Nether.

quest:1718.text: The Islander. The Islander is an invitation extended by veteran warrior trainers across Azeroth to those who have proven their basic mettle in battle. It directs rising fighters to Fray Island off the Merchant Coast, where an insular brotherhood of warriors tests their peers in raw martial combat. Meeting the chief warrior Klannoc Macleod marks a pivotal step toward mastering advanced combat disciplines. Warrior trainers in capital cities across both the Alliance and the Horde recognize when a student has outgrown basic drills. Rather than formal rank or political loyalty, martial progression demands that combatants measure themselves against true peers. The journey sends warriors away from civilized sparring yards toward a rugged isle isolated in the Great Sea. Fray Island sits east off the Merchant Coast, just south of the goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. It is reached by swimming the waters over submerged sandbar shallows. On this rock, political ties dissolve in favor of martial fraternity; fighters gather under the gaze of Klannoc Macleod, the chief warrior on the isle, awaiting whatever brutal trial he deems necessary.

quest:1719.text: The Affray. On Fray Island, warriors face a trial before Klannoc Macleod will train them. The Affray pits them against island challengers and their champion.
