Fray Island lies apart from the mainland, drawing brawlers, outcasts, and combat instructors. Klannoc Macleod does not teach every wanderer who arrives by boat. Aspiring warriors must first enter the Affray, where stamina and awareness in battle prove who can fight beyond mere boasting. A warrior begins the Affray by stepping onto the central iron grate among the spectators. Ringmaster Twiggy Flathead then sends challengers into the ring one after another. Those who survive face the island's heavyweight champion, Big Will. Defeating him is the only way to earn Klannoc's respect.

quest:173.text: Worgen in the Woods. Calor, a disillusioned former guardsman stationed in Darkshire, tasks adventurers with culling the sinister Nightbane Shadow Weavers prowling Duskwood. By taking the hunt to Brightwood Grove and the Rotting Orchard, outsiders can prove their mettle to Master Jonathan Carevin's monster hunters. The Night Watch struggles constantly against the undead, spiders, and outlaws pressing against Darkshire's borders. For some, like Calor, the official guard proved too slow and complacent to cleanse the land. Leaving the Watch behind, Calor threw in his lot with Master Jonathan Carevin, dedicating his blade to the total eradication of heresy and corruption. But Carevin does not accept just anyone into his circle; those seeking to aid their cause must first prove they can survive against the woods' most ferocious horrors. The proving ground lies in Brightwood Grove and the blighted Rotting Orchard, where feral lupine beasts known as worgen hold dominion. Among them, the Nightbane Shadow Weavers harness dark magics to blind and ensnare their victims before tearing them apart. Calor sends aspiring hunters to cut down these spell-weaving beasts, both to test an outsider's resolve and to thin out a threat whose origins remain deeply unsettling to Darkshire's defenders.

quest:1738.text: Heartswood. In the years since the Third War, Heartswood draws warlocks toward an old night elf tragedy. Takar the Seer sends them into Ashenvale for Gakin the Darkbinder, who needs the wood to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind. Takar the Seer says Heartswood grew where the night elf lovers Anathera and Latherion fell during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Their last breaths and devotion nourished the tree. To mortal eyes, it marks a tragic love; to practitioners of the dark arts, its concentrated emotion is potent magical fuel. Succubi feed on mortal passion, desire, and torment. Takar knows ordinary temptations cannot match an artifact filled with thousands of years of devotion. A piece of Heartswood gives Gakin the Darkbinder the catalyst he needs to draw a cunning demon through the Nether and into a summoning circle in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

quest:1739.text: The Binding. Stormwind warlocks seek to bind a succubus to their will. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb, an initiate uses the enchanted core from the Heartswood to summon the demon and defeat it in combat. A crypt beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter shelters the city's warlocks. There, away from the city watch and the Cathedral of Light, they practice forbidden arts. Stone summoning circles channel the Nether's power and let initiates reach across the veil between worlds. A warlock needs the prepared Heartswood Core to summon a succubus. The ritual opens a breach at the summoning circle, but the demon can corrupt and overwhelm even a fortified mind. To master it, the warlock must defeat it in single combat. Its physical form returns to the Twisting Nether, while its true tether is secured.

quest:174.text: Look To The Stars. Look To The Stars begins Viktori Prism'Antras's endeavor to gaze past the eerie canopy of Duskwood. Believing that a scientific answer beyond arcane superstition explains the forest's dark curse, Viktori recruits you to gather components for a telescope designed by his gnomish associate. Amid the gloom and fear shrouding Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras takes a distinctly unconventional view of Duskwood's misfortune. Rather than attributing the land's corruption purely to black magic, curses, or restless dead, Viktori suspects that greater truths await high above the canopy. With the aid of blueprints drawn up by his gnomish partner, Cog, he sets out to build an optical device capable of peering into the heavens. To commence assembly on the stargazing apparatus, Viktori needs a sturdy frame. Following Cog's specifications, he asks travelers to procure a machined bronze tube. This first step relies directly on the ingenuity of mortal mechanics rather than spellcraft, highlighting Viktori's stubborn insistence that practical craft and observation might shed light where mysticism has failed.

quest:1740.text: The Orb of Soran'ruk. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan sets warlocks to gather the scattered pieces of Soran'ruk. They seek to rebuild an orb that holds a disgraced demon's essence. Failure within the Burning Legion brings an eternal sentence. When lesser demons lose favor with their masters, their spirits are bound inside crystal orbs. The Legion gives these prisons to mortal conjurers and warlocks as vessels for power under demonic control. Shattering an orb does not free its captive; even the shards hold potent magic. Soran'ruk's orb lies in pieces across two continents. Twilight's Hammer cultists hold smaller fragments in the damp caverns of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale. A sorcerer in the haunted ruins of Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest claimed the larger, mostly intact half. Doan Karhan has spent his life studying Legion orbs and assembled the Orb of Zargain before. With the recovered pieces, he can restore Soran'ruk as a working implement.

quest:175.text: Look To The Stars. Following the blueprints provided by the tinker Cog, Viktori Prism'Antras seeks a reflective surface to assemble his observatory telescope in Darkshire. He directs travelers to southern Duskwood to locate Mary, a local woman remembered for carrying a looking glass. Having secured a bronze tube for his telescope, Viktori Prism'Antras turns to the next requirement outlined in Cog's blueprints: a reliable mirror to direct and reflect light through the device. Rather than forging fine silvered glass from scratch amidst the shortages plaguing Darkshire, Viktori recalls Mary, a local resident known across the region for always carrying a looking glass. Mary's former residence lies deep in southern Duskwood, just north of the haunted Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Seeking her out takes adventurers past the safe patrol borders of the Night Watch and into blighted groves teeming with ravenous wolves, feral spiders, and wandering undead.

quest:1758.text: Tome of the Cabal. Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan sends an aspiring Alliance warlock to the Library of Ironforge. A felhunter’s hunger can overwhelm an unprepared summoner, and the Tome of the Cabal holds the knowledge needed to summon and bind the demon. An imp, a voidwalker, or a succubus can be subdued through ritual, but a felhunter brings a different hazard. Felhunters serve the Burning Legion and hunt down arcane energy to devour it. A standard summoning circle will crumble before one, draining the summoner’s magic before a binding can take hold. From his redoubt in the Barrens, Strahad Farsan watches over Ratchet and knows an amateur must not attempt the binding unprepared. An acolyte needs the arcane formulas in the Tome of the Cabal to draw forth and bind a felhunter safely. The earliest mortal cabal of warlocks who successfully broke a felhunter without outside aid authored the manuscript. Its pages detail the geomancy, materials, and binding runes needed to withstand the creature’s hunger. The copy was lost long ago, leaving Strahad and his circle without the masterwork. Strahad sends Alliance warlocks across the Great Sea to the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, since he cannot provide the text himself. Krom Stoutarm, an itinerant dwarven warlock, resides there and spends his twilight years combing through ancient manuscripts and library records. If any trace of the lost grimoire remains recorded in the Eastern Kingdoms, it rests buried in Krom’s meticulous catalogs.

quest:177.text: Look To The Stars. This quest sends adventurers to recover Blind Mary's discarded looking glass for the astronomer Viktori Prism'Antras. The fragile mirror fell into the hands of an Insane Ghoul that wanders the desolate Tranquil Gardens Cemetery in southern Duskwood. Before the creeping gloom overran Duskwood and turned her into a weeping spirit, Blind Mary treasured an ornate looking glass. Following the horrific incident that claimed her sight and sanity, she cast the keepsake into the dirt behind her family barn. The reflective mirror is exactly what Viktori Prism'Antras needs to build his grand telescope in Darkshire, but it was snatched away into the shadows long before the astronomer dreamed of studying the heavens. The mirror was scavenged by an Insane Ghoul that prowled behind the ruined farmsteads. Driven south by restless hunger, the wretched undead creature carried the looking glass into the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, haunting an abandoned chapel amid the overgrown tombstones. Reclaiming the delicate lens means navigating the flesh-eating horrors that infest the southern woods to pry Mary's lost treasure from rotting claws.

quest:178.text: Theocritus' Retrieval. Theocritus' Retrieval begins when an adventurer in Redridge finds a magical trinket carried by the local gnolls, only to hear a distant voice echoing through it. The speaker is Theocritus, High Mage of Tower of Azora, who has successfully intercepted the gnolls' mystical network and urgently requests the pendant be brought to him for study. While fighting off the savage Shadowhide gnolls across the Redridge Mountains, travelers sometimes stumble across an enchanted trinket known as a Shadowhide Pendant. Instead of guttural barking or curses, touching the object triggers a calm, disembodied voice belonging to Theocritus, a human mage residing in Tower of Azora across the border in Elwynn Forest. The transmission is the result of long, painstaking research aimed at breaking into the dark sorceries directing the gnoll packs.

quest:1782.text: Furen's Armor. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard seeks help testing new armor. An aspiring warrior gathers spider fangs, chimaera horns, and phlogiston so the master smith can forge fire-hardened mail. Furen gives the finished armor to the warrior and promises to share what he learned with Alliance smiths. Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorer in Stormwind, works to improve how Alliance armor withstands heat and crushing blows. He asks an aspiring warrior to gather rare materials for his tests. The resulting mail proves a success and strengthens Furen's standing among Alliance armorers. Furen gives the finished fire-hardened mail to the warrior who gathered the materials, grateful for their help. The experiments also deepen his knowledge of protective smithing. He plans to send his notes and findings to other Alliance smiths, so they can put the new methods to use.

quest:1791.text: The Windwatcher. Warriors who have mastered the berserker stance are sent north to find The Windwatcher. After the Affray on Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod points them toward a weapon worthy of their fury. You have survived the Affray on Fray Island and learned the berserker stance from Klannoc Macleod. Now Klannoc sends you far from the Barrens coast, across continents, to find a solitary craftsman who can forge an exceptional weapon. Bath'rah the Windwatcher lives beside the river that runs north past Tarren Mill. His camp rests among stone ruins in the contested land between the Alterac Mountains and the blighted Western Plaguelands. The troll hermit crafts weapons and commands potent elemental shamanism. He waits for warriors determined to forge a weapon of great power.

quest:1793.text: The Tome of Valor. The Tome of Valor is a foundational trial for Alliance paladins coming into their own. Directed by paladin mentors in Stormwind and Ironforge, initiates are challenged to prove that their courage and devotion to protecting the innocent match their martial prowess. To wield the Holy Light in battle requires more than heavy armor and martial discipline. As young paladins reach greater heights in their training, instructors in the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries demand proof of their inner resolve. The lessons of the Tome of Valor test an initiate's readiness to confront terrifying evils—from dragons to demons—without faltering or abandoning those who cannot defend themselves. Bravery under mortal threat is considered as essential to a holy warrior as their weapon and shield. Through the trials laid out in the Tome of Valor, paladins learn that raw strength is hollow without an unwavering vow to shelter the helpless. Facing genuine peril ensures that when darkness falls upon the Alliance, its defenders will stand firm rather than break.

quest:1795.text: The Binding. Above Ratchet, warlocks face the rite that binds a felhunter to their will. Strahad Farsan oversees the summoning with the restored Tome of the Cabal, drawing an aggressive demon from the Nether to be subdued in combat. On Kalimdor's bluffs above Ratchet, the goblin port, Strahad Farsan conducts dangerous trials in demon summoning. After a warlock gathers the fragments and reagents needed to restore the ancient Tome of the Cabal, Strahad prepares the binding grounds. He lays an inner glyph of containment while his acolytes channel power through enchanted rods to complete the outer circle. The circles keep whatever emerges isolated from the settlement below. The Tome of the Cabal holds the incantations that open a bridge into the Twisting Nether. Felhunters are ravenous demonic hounds that hunger for arcane power and feast on magical energy. No gentle enthrallment or persuasion will bind one. The warlock must violently subdue and break the summoned beast in combat before it recognizes its rightful master. Surviving the clash proves the summoner can wield the hound against enemy spellcasters.

quest:1796.text: Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender asks warlocks to find Robes of Arcana for a garment meant to bear powerful enchantments. Menara Voidrender asks warlocks seeking greater power to bring her a set of Robes of Arcana. She wants a garment strong enough to hold dark magic. The strength of a magical relic depends on the skill, rarity, and effort put into its materials. Ordinary rags would fail under deep enchantments, so the robe must be finely made and ready to receive them. Menara admires warlocks who can weave the robe themselves, but ambition matters more to her than pride. You can sew the silk, commission a skilled artisan, or buy the robe at market. However you obtain it, the finished garment is ready to become a specialized tool of fel mastery.

quest:1798.text: Seeking Strahad. Warlocks leave Stormwind City for Ratchet, where Strahad Farsan can teach them to summon felhunters. Beneath the goblin port, his knowledge offers a path into more dangerous demon summoning. Gakin the Darkbinder sends you from Stormwind to seek help with summoning a felhunter. He guides warlocks in the Slaughtered Lamb, below the Mage Quarter, but the rites call for knowledge beyond what he can offer there. Your journey carries you across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, where another warlock may know the way. Strahad Farsan lives in the arid hills above Ratchet, the goblin harbor. He is a human warlock and a peer of Gakin's in their secret cabal. From neutral territory, Strahad can work beyond the notice of Alliance magistrates, church inquisitors, and Horde sentries. Warlocks come to him hoping to master demons that drain mana.

quest:180.text: Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore. Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore is a local bounty posted in Lakeshire by Magistrate Solomon. It calls on adventurers to hunt down Lieutenant Fangore, the vicious chieftain of the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching upon the Redridge Mountains. Eliminating him strikes a direct blow against the renegade sorcerer Morganth, whom the gnolls serve. Lakeshire sits in a desperate position. With Stormwind's army stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn mysteriously absent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon has left frontier settlements like Redridge to look after themselves. The Shadowhide clan has grown increasingly bold, raiding trade routes, burning farmsteads, and pressing right up against the town's perimeter. Magistrate Solomon relies on posted bounties to draw mercenary blades where royal soldiers will not march. Lieutenant Fangore is not merely a marauding beast; he operates as an enforcer for Morganth, a rogue dark wizard lurking in the hills of Redridge. Under Fangore's command, the Shadowhide gnolls coordinate their strikes rather than fighting as disjointed scavengers, threatening to completely sever Lakeshire from Elwynn Forest. Striking off Fangore's paw provides Magistrate Solomon with proof that Morganth's brute vanguard has been broken.

quest:1801.text: Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan sends Horde warlocks east in search of a lost grimoire. The Tome of the Cabal holds rites for summoning and binding a felhunter, and the search begins with cartographer Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Strahad Farsan says a felhunter takes more than ordinary fel magic to summon. These predators feed on magical energies and resist standard summoning circles. An initiate needs specialized circles and an ancient grimoire called the Tome of the Cabal. The first order of warlocks to bind a felhunter without outside aid wrote the book. Its rites and seals show how to enslave such a dangerous demon. Copies of the Tome of the Cabal have long been lost to warlocks in Kalimdor, so Strahad sends his student across the sea to Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Annison works as a royal cartographer, mapping Lordaeron, but knows a great deal about ancient and obscure texts. He admits that he despises mapmaking and hungers for rare histories, occult narratives, and treatises on dark magic.

quest:1802.text: Tome of the Cabal. This quest tasks an Alliance warlock with tracking down the scattered, ruined halves of a singular grimoire known as the Tome of the Cabal. Recovering the missing pages from distant lands is essential for deciphering the dark rites necessary to bind a felhunter. Only a single copy of the Tome of the Cabal was ever scribed, and its violent history ensured it did not stay intact. Torn apart and vandalized, its remnants were scattered to entirely different corners of the world. One portion, a tattered manuscript ripped straight from the binding, somehow found its way across the sea into the rugged canyons of Kalimdor, falling into the hands of the centaur clans. The remaining section was intended for transport by sea from the shores of Lordaeron down to Khaz Modan, but the vessel foundered before reaching its port. Reassembling the grimoire demands surviving two treacherous perils. The sea-lost pages washed ashore off the Hillsbrad coast west of Southshore, where scavenged debris and waterlogged relics fell into the grasp of shoreline murlocs near Azurelode Mine. Meanwhile, recovering the arid half requires infiltrating Splithoof Hold in Thousand Needles, delving deep into centaur caverns to reclaim the manuscript from an ancient chest. Only by uniting these disparate halves can Krom Stoutarm inspect the lost text before it returns to Strahad Farsan.

quest:1803.text: Tome of the Cabal. This quest tasks Horde warlocks with reuniting the severed halves of the ancient Tome of the Cabal for Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Once kept within the kingdom of Lordaeron, the grimoire was torn apart and scattered across the world before being lost entirely. Tracking down its damp and tattered remnants requires braving hostile waters in the Eastern Kingdoms and deep centaur territory in Kalimdor. The Tome of the Cabal was once preserved within the library walls of the old kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point, the sinister grimoire was deliberately vandalized, stripped of nearly half its pages, and sundered into two pieces. The remaining formal text was slated for transit south to the dwarven halls of Ironforge, but fate intervened: the transport wrecked along the rocky coastline west of Southshore, leaving the pages to rot in the shallows under the watchful eyes of scavenging murlocs.

quest:1804.text: Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan waits for a warlock to bring him the Tome of the Cabal and channeling rods. Together, they prepare the way to bind a felhunter. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Krom Stoutarm binds the Tome of the Cabal's tattered, mouldering remnants back together. The dwarf scholar reluctantly parts with this rare work of dark scholarship, but first secures a promise of a copy. He also passes along a fresh missive from Strahad Farsan. The tome holds the rites for breaching the Nether, though parchment alone cannot conduct the ritual. Strahad's acolytes need focus implements to steady the energies summoned to bind a felhunter. Krom sends the warlock to the Wetlands, where Dragonmaw spellcasters carry rods of channeling. Taking the rods from the hostile orcs gives Strahad's circle the conduit it needs to control the rift and stabilize the summoned energies.

quest:1805.text: Tome of the Cabal. A warlock's work with the Tome of the Cabal now leads into hostile territory. After helping Jorah Annison restore the tome, you must claim three Rods of Channeling and bring them to Strahad Farsan in Ratchet. In the Undercity, Jorah Annison studies the recovered fragments of the Tome of the Cabal. The Forsaken scholar pieces together its eldritch passages and welcomes the rare knowledge they offer. Then Jorah delivers an urgent directive from Strahad Farsan. Knowledge alone cannot bind a felhunter. A warlock needs precise instruments to focus demonic power into a binding circle. Strahad needs three Rods of Channeling, carried by renegade orcs of the Dragonmaw clan. They dwell among the ruins of Angerfang Encampment in the Wetlands, far from Horde lands. You must enter contested territory and face clan remnants who hate the modern Horde as much as they butcher Alliance explorers.

quest:1806.text: The Test of Righteousness. The Test of Righteousness culminates at Jordan Stilwell's forge outside Ironforge in Dun Morogh. After gathering perilous components from across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, a paladin waits while the smith crafts a mighty warhammer. It marks the transition of an apprentice into a recognized champion of the Light. Master smith Jordan Stilwell plies his craft outside the gates of Ironforge. While he admits to a touch of envy toward wandering paladins, he takes profound pride in supporting the cause through his hammer and anvil. Once presented with rare materials gathered from shadowy crypts, sunken ruins, and dangerous mines, Stilwell fulfills his promise to forge a weapon worthy of a true defender. The finished warhammer is christened Verigan's Fist in honor of Bosch Verigan, an honored dwarven paladin and dear personal friend of Jordan Stilwell. By passing this sacred weapon into a young champion's hands on behalf of himself and his wife, Stilwell ensures that the memory and valor of his fallen friend endure against the darkness threatening Azeroth.

quest:181.text: Look To The Stars. This quest marks the final chapter in Viktori Prism'Antras's endeavor to assemble a stargazing device in Darkshire. With the telescope structure otherwise built, Viktori sends travelers to the dangerous Vul'Gol Ogre Mound to retrieve a lens large enough for his contraption: a monocle worn by the ogre Zzarc'Vul. Throughout the construction of his stargazing telescope, Viktori Prism'Antras has relied on plans drafted by the gnome engineer Cog Glitzspinner. While brass tubes and sturdy mountings could be scavenged or assembled from local supplies, the apparatus required an exceptionally massive focusing lens. Standard magnifying glasses and optical components from Stormwind traders simply lacked the diameter called for by Cog's ambitious design, leading Viktori to look toward an unlikely and perilous alternative.

quest:1824.text: Trial at the Field of Giants. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem sends warrior aspirants south to face an unfamiliar foe. They must slay silithid in the Field of Giants and return with several twitching antennae within half an hour. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem challenges growing warriors to prove themselves against an unfamiliar adversary. The Horde's warrior trainers test more than combat skill: aspirants must slay the creatures and bring back fresh antennae within half an hour. The run across the southern Barrens tests their speed and resolve, while the antennae must still twitch when they reach Taurajo. Silithid hives rise in the Field of Giants, beneath massive fossilized ribcages. The bizarre, crawling insects are recent arrivals in the Barrens, disturbing tauren hunters and shamans who watch the savannas. Ruga says their presence bodes ill for Kalimdor. The trial tests a young warrior's instincts in combat and gathers intelligence on a growing threat to the land.

quest:1825.text: Speak with Thun'grim. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thun'grim Firegaze, an acclaimed orc blacksmith camping in the Barrens. Having proved themselves through demanding physical trials, warriors are invited to have custom armor forged in recognition of their valor. The quest serves as the crucial bridge connecting general warrior testing with the crafting of Brutal Armor. After proving their mettle against the silithid hives during the Trial at the Field of Giants, Horde warriors earn more than simple praise from Ruga Ragetotem. Word of their endurance and martial prowess quickly reaches Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned orc smith who maintains a camp perched on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Recognizing a warrior worthy of his craft, Thun'grim sends word that he wishes to fashion them an exceptional suit of battle mail. Thun'grim Firegaze does not forge for ordinary soldiers. For an armorsmith of his reputation, steel must match the spirit of the one who carries it into battle. Reaching his camp signifies that a warrior has advanced past simple militia drills and is ready to undertake the grueling, specialized tasks required to gather rare crafting reagents across Kalimdor.

quest:1838.text: Brutal Armor. A warrior in the northern Barrens faces Thun'grim Firegaze's test. The near-blind smith sends seasoned Horde warriors across distant lands for rare ingredients and smelting agents. Fulfilling his scroll begins the forging of a full set of brutal battle gear. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze listens for news of war. The veteran orc smith's eyesight is failing, but his skill at the forge remains unmatched. Rumors reach him of a warrior whose strength and valor exceed those of ordinary soldiers. Thun'grim sets out to craft mail that can withstand the fiercest battles across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Thun'grim's armor calls for more than common ore. By firelight, his failing eyes guide him as he writes a precise scroll for the core chestpiece. Its ingredients include refined iron, smoky iron ingots carried by burrowing kobolds, powdered azurite worked by miners across the sea, and a volatile vial of phlogiston. Only a warrior ready to face trials across distant lands can bring the required materials together.

quest:1839.text: Ula'elek and the Brutal Gauntlets. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you from the Barrens to Sen'jin Village for the Brutal Gauntlets. There, Darkspear craftsman Ula'elek will forge them. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east after you prove your valor in the Barrens and begin assembling the Brutal Armor set. The veteran orc smith relies on skilled artisans across Horde lands instead of forging every piece at his mountain perch. For the heavy mail gauntlets, he directs you to Durotar's rocky southern shores. In Sen'jin Village, troll armorsmith Ula'elek works among his Darkspear kin. Thun'grim has already told him of your deeds, and Ula'elek says the spirits have watched your triumphs in battle. For a warrior earning a place among the Horde's elite, fine craft and spiritual acknowledgement go hand in hand.

quest:1840.text: Orm Stonehoof and the Brutal Helm. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thunder Bluff to consult with Orm Stonehoof, an artisan smith. Recommended by Thun'grim Firegaze, Orm possesses the specialized craft required to forge the Brutal Helm. After proving their mettle and assembling pieces of the Brutal Armor in the Barrens, warriors are directed higher into the mesa city of Thunder Bluff. Thun'grim Firegaze, an accomplished armorsmith himself, recognizes his limits and refers his champions to Orm Stonehoof. Orm's craft is renowned throughout Kalimdor, specifically his ability to mold resilient battlefield helms from rare, savage trophies. Orm makes his home and workplace on the high bluffs of Mulgore, standing near the tranquil waters beneath the city's towering central totem. When a warrior arrives carrying word from Thun'grim, Orm steps away from routine work to discuss the demanding components needed to forge headgear truly worthy of the Horde's front lines.

quest:1841.text: Velora Nitely and the Brutal Legguards. Thun'grim Firegaze sends Horde warriors across the Great Sea for Velora Nitely's Brutal Legguards. In the Undercity, the Forsaken smith draws on the craft she kept from her mortal life to forge the armor. Her work helps assemble a durable suit for the Horde's warriors. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east across the Great Sea to find a smith for the Brutal Legguards. You've proved your mettle to the veteran smith at his vigil in the Barrens, and now he points you toward the fabled Brutal Armor. Thun'grim cannot make the whole suit alone, so he relies on skilled allies across the Horde. The greaves call for an artisan whose work was revered before northern humanity fell, in the Forsaken's underground kingdom. Velora Nitely works in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, where her old craft still serves the Horde. Before the Scourging of the north ended her mortal life, she was one of the Kingdom of Lordaeron's foremost armorsmiths. Her homeland was corrupted, and she became one of the Forsaken, but death did not take her mastery of metal. She now turns her human skill toward the Horde's warriors, with a dry, macabre wit about being undead.

quest:1842.text: Satyr Hooves. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek sends warriors north for Satyr Hooves. He needs their strange power to forge brutal gauntlets. Ula'elek sends you into Ashenvale's ancient woods to gather what his craft requires. Demonic corruption still clings to the satyr covens there, and he seeks more than iron and leather for armor meant to rival Kalimdor's fiercest forces. In northeastern Ashenvale, satyrs feed on the forest's lingering purity and twist it into foul power. Those that take in the most develop swollen hooves without the usual cloven split. Ula'elek plans to draw out that concentrated magic and weave it into the gauntlets he makes.

quest:1843.text: Brutal Gauntlets. Ula'elek has finished a pair of Brutal Gauntlets for a seasoned Horde warrior. Rare materials gathered across distant lands have gone into the work, meant to honor both maker and bearer. Ula'elek brings his lineage and skill to the forging of armor for a seasoned frontline warrior. In Durotar, the Horde craftsman shapes brutal gauntlets from hardened trophies taken from dangerous foes. The finished armor is made to withstand fierce blows and strengthen the wearer's attacks. For orcs and trolls, fine arms and armor carry the forge's prestige and the maker's spirit into battle. When Ula'elek presents the finished gauntlets, he entrusts a warrior with his ancestors' legacy. A champion who wears them is expected to meet that craft with courage, martial discipline, and strength.

quest:1844.text: Chimaeric Horn. As part of the warrior rite to craft the Brutal Helm, Orm Stonehoof tasks an aspiring champion with journeying into the ruined Charred Vale. There, the warrior must hunt a maddened chimaera matriarch to claim her galvanized horn as both an act of mercy and proof of strength. Orm Stonehoof is willing to forge the legendary Brutal Helm for Horde warriors, but martial tradition demands that the wearer prove their mettle first. Orm does not simply ask for raw metal or coin; he demands proof of martial prowess and a willingness to confront the grim scars left behind by devastating conflict. The quest directs warriors to the southwestern reaches of the Stonetalon Mountains, into the ashen desolation known as the Charred Vale. Once lush and green, the valley was burned into a smoking wasteland. The surviving beasts wandering its soot-covered craters are twisted by agony and fury, particularly the mighty chimaeras that make their nests amid the dead trees and searing steam vents. Slaying a chimaera matriarch serves two purposes in the tauren smith's eyes. It claims the hardened, galvanized horn required for crafting the headpiece, but it also ends the creature's torment. By felling the matriarch, the warrior acts both as an executioner and an instrument of mercy for a wild spirit driven mad by the destruction of its home.

quest:1845.text: Brutal Helm. Brutal Helm marks the culmination of an arduous warrior trial overseen by Orm Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff. Having collected rare beast trophies across Kalimdor, an aspiring warrior is recognized with a formidable horned helm as a testament to their strength. Orm Stonehoof serves as a stern smith in Thunder Bluff, guiding Horde warriors through grueling rites of passage. These trials demand proof of martial capability, pushing initiates into treacherous territory to hunt ferocious creatures and claim rare trophies. Only those who have met Orm's exacting standards are granted audience for the completion of their armor. By bringing the rare chimaeric horn to Orm Stonehoof, the warrior proves their resolve against the wilderness. In recognition, Orm presents the Brutal Helm—a heavy, menacing piece of mail crafted to honor the beast and bolster the wearer in frontline combat. As he bestows it, Orm invokes the blessings of the Earthmother, looking forward to the greater deeds the warrior is bound to undertake across Azeroth.

quest:1846.text: Dragonmaw Shinbones. Dragonmaw Shinbones is a Horde warrior quest directed by the armorer Velora Nitely in the Undercity. To craft the resilient Brutal Legguards, warriors are dispatched into the southern Wetlands to harvest exceptionally thick shinbones from the hostile Dragonmaw orcs. Forging armor fit for a seasoned frontline warrior demands unorthodox materials. When tasked with fashioning Brutal Legguards, the Forsaken armorer Velora Nitely specifies a structural brace constructed from thick, resilient bone. Rather than utilizing common beasts, she directs aspiring warriors toward the Dragonmaw orcs of the Wetlands, whose dense skeletal builds provide the necessary resilience to withstand heavy blows in combat. Harvesting bone from the Dragonmaw is only half the ordeal. Velora instructs warriors to manually test every bone taken in the field; any specimen brittle enough to snap in bare hands is utterly useless for the forge. Warriors must scour the renegade encampments along the Wetlands' crags, breaking weak bones until eight genuinely sturdy examples survive the test of strength.

quest:1848.text: Brutal Hauberk. Across the Barrens, Horde warriors face a trial before Thun'grim Firegaze will forge their mail. They gather rare materials and prove themselves against dangerous foes across the lands, then bring their bounty to the reclusive smith. He hammers it into armor built for battle. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze forges armor only for warriors who meet his demands. The reclusive orc sends them far and wide to gather tough beast parts, rare metal, and alchemical reagents before he lights his bellows. The finished hauberk offers protection and marks the endurance and grit its wearer has shown, earning recognition from veteran fighters throughout the Horde. Thun'grim makes his demands punishing by design. Horde arms and armor are expected to carry the sweat and blood of their wearer from the moment they are made. When you hand over the finished Brutal Hauberk, the smith offers no praise. He expects you to prove the armor in brutal combat and return with stories of blood and honor.

quest:185.text: Tiger Mastery. At the northern safari camp in Stranglethorn Vale, the hunter Ajeck Rouack offers to train adventurers in the discipline of big cat stalking. She starts newcomers against the younger tigers prowling near the camp to test basic hunting and tracking prowess. Having learned the art of hunting tigers from her father when she was a girl, Ajeck Rouack shares his craft with travelers who reach Nesingwary's Expedition following Welcome to the Jungle. She insists that tracking and slaying the youngest felines is the essential foundation before any hunter can advance to greater quarry. Young Stranglethorn tigers are often found in the jungle close to the expedition camp. Rouack demands that ten of these beasts be hunted down to prove sufficient skill before she agrees to provide any further training.

quest:186.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Ajeck Rouack escalates her hunting trials. Having seen your early promise with young stalkers, he now sends you into the jungle to fell mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Following your initial success against younger predators, Ajeck Rouack seeks to test your growing skills against more seasoned beasts. She directs you back out into the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale to hunt down ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers before you can pursue even greater challenges.

quest:187.text: Tiger Mastery. Deep in the jungle at Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack raises the stakes of his hunting trials. He demands the death of ten elder Stranglethorn tigers to prove your prowess before the final test. Following the earlier hunts, Ajeck Rouack asks you to pursue ten elder Stranglethorn tigers across the wilds. He considers these beasts both the most elusive to track and the fiercest to overcome. Felling ten of them serves as the prelude to a concluding trial, after which he promises to proclaim you a master tiger hunter before Master Nesingwary.

quest:188.text: Tiger Mastery. Ajeck Rouack offers the ultimate challenge in his series of hunts within northern Stranglethorn Vale. After weeks of tracking an elusive beast, he challenges you to seek out the tiger Sin'Dall and bring back her paw. Having completed the earlier trials against Stranglethorn's tigers, you are offered one last challenge by Ajeck Rouack at Nesingwary's Expedition. The hunting camp has tracked an extraordinarily elusive tiger known as Sin'Dall across the jungle for weeks. Ajeck challenges you to track her down, fell the beast, and claim her paw as indisputable proof.

quest:189.text: Bloodscalp Ears. Kebok in Booty Bay is losing guards and agents to jungle clashes with the Bloodscalp tribe. Worried about climbing expenses and answering to Baron Revilgaz, he offers coin to any adventurer willing to hunt down the trolls and return with proof of the kill. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Kebok faces a serious operational dilemma. The local trolls in Stranglethorn Vale have been killing his agents in the jungle, and he has lost many of his best guards in skirmishes with them. With the casualties mounting, so too are the costs, leaving him frantic over how to explain them to Baron Revilgaz. Rather than allowing the losses to accumulate further, Kebok turns to outside help. He offers monetary compensation to travelers who head into the jungle, cull the Bloodscalp trolls, and bring back fifteen of their severed ears as undeniable confirmation of their demise.

quest:19.text: Tharil'zun. Marshal Marris places a bounty on Tharil'zun, the cunning leader of the Blackrock outrunners harassing the roads near Stonewatch Keep. Striking him down serves as a critical step in breaking the Blackrock clan's hold over northern Redridge. Bringing his severed head back to Lakeshire marks a hard-fought victory for the embattled town watch. The winding pass between Lakeshire and Stonewatch Keep has become a gauntlet of sudden ambushes. Blackrock outrunners and renegades prowl the rocky ridges, cutting off scouts and threatening any reinforcements attempting to push toward the fortress. Marshal Marris identifies Tharil'zun as the commander orchestrating these coordinated strikes, declaring his elimination necessary to prevent Lakeshire from being entirely hemmed in. Tharil'zun represents a dangerous breed of battlefield leader: vicious, crafty, and capable of coordinating the disparate orc raiders into an effective raiding force. Taking his head inside the shadow of Stonewatch requires cutting through entrenched Blackrock outposts. His death breaks the cohesion of the outrunner patrols, clearing a path for the Alliance to confront the garrison entrenched within the keep itself.

quest:190.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition offers a trial to those seeking to prove their prowess as big-game stalkers in Stranglethorn Vale. To join Hemet's hunting company, adventurers must first demonstrate their basic tracking ability by taking down ten young panthers. Within the wild expanse of northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary has assembled a seasoned band of big-game huntsmen. Sir S. J. Erlgadin tells anyone who wants a part of the hunt that they must first prove themselves an able panther hunter. Before Erlgadin entrusts anyone with greater game, he issues an entry test: finding and slaying ten young panthers. Simply finding the beasts is only half the challenge.

quest:191.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin demands that you prove yourself worthy of the big game hunters at Nesingwary's Expedition. Following your initial cull of younger beasts, he challenges you to track down and slay ten fully grown panthers in the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale. After dispatching the young panthers around the jungle, Sir S. J. Erlgadin asks you to raise your sights. To show that you deserve to keep company with seasoned big game hunters, you are sent out to hunt ten mature panthers, which are far tougher and more dangerous than their younger kin.

quest:192.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition challenges big game hunters to track and bring down the deadliest panthers in Stranglethorn Vale. Following your earlier trials, you must now seek out and slay ten Shadowmaw Panthers. Sir S. J. Erlgadin considers Shadowmaw Panthers to be the most dangerous cats prowling the jungles of Stranglethorn. Proving your mettle as a true stalker requires crawling through the dense underbrush to track down ten of these elusive beasts, whose ferocity makes them far harder to kill than to find.

quest:1938.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. In Stormwind, High Sorcerer Andromath seeks the forbidden tome Morganth stole and carried to the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Three promising mages once studied together in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum. Morganth turned to dark arts and shadow magic, despite his peers' desperate warnings to abandon those corrupting powers. The city's magical order formally banished him. Before leaving, he stole a dangerous work by Ur, an infamous archmage whose studies reached beyond orthodox arcana. Morganth seized the Tower of Ilgalar in the heights of the Redridge Mountains, far from Stormwind's scrutiny. High Sorcerer Andromath considers the tome's knowledge hazardous in the hands of an outcast practicing forbidden sorcery. He sends Alliance adventurers to breach the tower and recover it before its wards fall.

quest:1939.text: High Sorcerer Andromath. At Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, a summons calls promising Alliance mages to the tower's summit. Andromath works among the kingdom's foremost archmages beyond ruined Dalaran. Jennea Cannon, the apprentice coordinator in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, sends promising casters up to the Wizard's Sanctum summit. High Sorcerer Andromath, among the southern kingdoms' most senior active practitioners of the arcane, has asked to meet magi ready for greater responsibilities. Dalaran's magocracy was ruined in the Third War, and its surviving wizards are occupied with rebuilding. Without easy access to the Violet Citadel's libraries, the Alliance depends on senior archmages in Stormwind to study ancient threats and guide research into shadowy, forbidden arts.

quest:194.text: Raptor Mastery. At his expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges travelers to prove their prowess in the wilderness. The famed hunter demands ten Stranglethorn Raptors slain to test whether you possess genuine hunting talent. Following your arrival in the jungle after Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary offers to test your tracking and hunting capabilities. Rather than handing out maps or directions, he insists that finding the Stranglethorn Raptors yourself is half the test, challenging you to venture out into the brush and bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

quest:1940.text: Pristine Spider Silk. In Stormwind, High Sorcerer Andromath sends rising Alliance mages to Duskwood for pristine spider silk. They bring eight samples to Wynne Larson in the Mage Quarter, where she makes a robe for an adept. High Sorcerer Andromath marks a mage’s passage beyond apprenticeship with vestments fit for an adept. In the Wizard’s Sanctum, arcane mastery is matched by the robes its practitioners wear. Rather than buy finished garments, the mage must show field skill and discernment by taking pristine, unblemished silk from dangerous spiders. Venomous carrion recluse spiders haunt Duskwood’s gloomy woods, and their silk is not sold at ordinary stalls. You gather eight prime samples and carry them across Stormwind to Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. There, Wynne Larson uses the delicate threads to weave a robe with arcane significance.

quest:1942.text: Astral Knot Garment. Wynne Larson works fine spider silk into a garment in Stormwind City. An adventurer brings her rare silk gathered from the wilds, and she tailors it into a magical weave for dangerous journeys and high-society gatherings. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, tailors serve arcane elites and visiting nobles. Wynne Larson is known for weaving pristine spider silk into durable, enchanted garments. Her playful humor comes through when she jokes about saving a few precious scraps for her own wardrobe before handing over her finished work. Spellcasters who wear cloth prize the Astral Knot Garment for its resilience and refinement. Its silk comes from dangerous spiders, and its weave is made to endure combat while keeping the polished look expected at formal banquets in Stormwind Keep.

quest:1943.text: Speak with Deino. In Orgrimmar, Deino calls promising Horde mages to aid their craft. The troll mage works from the Valley of Spirits and seeks an adept for important work. Her summons opens a path to deeper study and duties across Kalimdor. Horde mages hone their arcane abilities under the guidance of instructors. When a student is ready for harder work, mentors such as Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity point the way to Orgrimmar. In its troll quarter, specialized knowledge and dangerous work await. Deino lives in Darkbriar Lodge in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Among the Darkspear, few study arcane magic compared with the many witch doctors and priests, which makes Deino an authority in the capital. Her work serves Horde mages beyond local concerns, and she seeks ambitious spellcasters willing to face dangers far from home.

quest:1944.text: Waters of Xavian. Waters of Xavian is a Horde mage quest offered by Deino in Orgrimmar. Seeking to plumb ancient elven secrets, she tasks her apprentice with traveling to the ruins of Xavian in Ashenvale to draw a sample from its highest waterfall. Within the dark crevices of the Valley of Spirits, the troll mage Deino seeks out lingering reservoirs of primal arcane energy across Kalimdor. Her gaze turns to Xavian, an ancient night elf city hidden deep in the eastern canopy of Ashenvale. Legends among scholars whisper that the city was steeped in magical knowledge before the Sundering, and its waters are said to retain potent arcane properties that modern casters yearn to dissect. Reaching the source of these waters is no simple errand. Xavian no longer belongs to peaceful elven sages; it has fallen into ruin and is now overrun by feral, corrupt satyrs who fiercely guard their territory from outsiders. Prying mages must navigate past Satyrnaar and tread through dangerous waterways, avoiding both prowling beasts and demonic sentinels to fill Deino's flask at the base of the city's towering waterfall.

quest:1945.text: Laughing Sisters. Laughing Sisters is a Horde quest that sends mages into the heart of Ashenvale to gather enchanted locks of hair from wild dryads. The material is destined for Kil'hala, an experienced troll tailor at the Crossroads, to spin into an empowered mage robe. Hunting the daughters of Cenarius underscores the relentless friction between Horde spellcasters and the native defenders of the ancient woodland. Following their efforts to secure water from Xavian, rising mages are directed by Deino in Orgrimmar to assist in crafting their own enchanted vestments. Arcane tailoring of this nature demands materials imbued with raw magical essence. Dryad locks, naturally suffused with the primeval vitality of the forest, hold the necessary qualities to thread intricate magical garments capable of shielding and augmenting a caster's powers. To harvest these locks, mages must venture south toward Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale. The laughing sisters—nimble, woodland dryads allied with the night elves—guard these groves fiercely against encroaching woodsmen and outsiders alike. Because these woodland fey would never willingly surrender their hair to Horde spellcasters, the harvest is inevitably paid in blood beneath the canopy of ancient trees. Once gathered, the locks are carried south across the border to the dusty settlement of the Crossroads in the Barrens. There, the troll tailor Kil'hala receives the tribute without remorse. While acknowledging the loss of the woodland creatures with a touch of irony, Kil'hala wastes no time putting the enchanted strands to practical use, recognizing that power in the Horde often requires unyielding resolve.

quest:1946.text: Nether-lace Garment. At the Crossroads, Kil'hala weaves dryad hair into enchanted cloth for spellcasters. The finished garment marks the end of his specialized work in the Barrens. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala weaves nether-lace from the locks of laughing sisters. The dryads live in Ashenvale, and their hair is harvested for this work. Kil'hala binds the woodland enchantment in those rare, magically resonant locks into cloth that is comfortable and durable. Kil'hala wants more than fine work from his trade. He hopes to win favor with Deino, a respected troll mage who lives in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. By making exceptional garb for aspiring practitioners, he hopes to earn and keep Deino's good graces.

quest:195.text: Raptor Mastery. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges hunters to step up their game against more dangerous quarry. Following an earlier raptor hunt, he directs adventurers to pursue and bring down ten Lashtail Raptors. After proving an initial measure of hunting prowess, Hemet Nesingwary expects more than idly passing time by the camp's fire. To prove true focus and skill, hunters are dispatched into the dense jungle brush just north of Grom'gol Base Camp to track down and slay ten fierce Lashtail Raptors.

quest:1950.text: Get the Scoop. Magus Tirth has locked a crucial spellbook inside his magically sealed strongbox, but he cannot recall the activation phrase to open it. To retrieve the tome, you must locate his missing apprentice somewhere around the Shimmering Flats racetrack and pry the forgotten words from him. Magus Tirth is an eccentric spellcaster dwelling on the cracked salt bed of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. While he possesses the esoteric knowledge and tomes that advancing mages desperately seek, dealing with him requires patience. Tirth relies heavily on an assistant to manage mundane details, including the spoken passwords guarding his arcane repositories. When tasked with retrieving a book of power, visiting practitioners quickly learn that Tirth has locked the volume away behind magic words that have slipped his mind entirely.

quest:198.text: Supplies to Private Thorsen. Krazek in Booty Bay hires a courier to haul miscellaneous goblin supplies north to Lieutenant Doren's camp. Local troll aggression has halted routine shipments, requiring an outside hand to ensure the goods reach Private Thorsen near the northern border. Lieutenant Doren and his outfit stationed near the border between Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood rely on regular shipments arranged through Krazek. Persistent attacks from local trolls have made standard delivery hazardous, prompting the goblin merchant to contract an independent courier. The package must travel all the way up the jungle road, with Private Thorsen designated to receive it either in their camp northwest of the road or along his patrol route to the south.

quest:1999.text: Tools of the Trade. Tools of the Trade is an initiation mission for Horde rogues given by Mennet Carkad in the Undercity. Ordered by Lord Varimathras, agents must obtain lockpicking gear and infiltrate Ambermill to recover sensitive Kirin Tor reports detailing Dalaran's current state. Following the interrogation of one of their prisoners, the Deathstalkers learned that vital intelligence concerning the ruins of Dalaran lies hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and the human mages guarding the village guard their communications fiercely. Under the orders of Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad directs promising operatives to bypass Kirin Tor sentries and secure the Dalaran Status Report. Unlike straightforward assassinations, this mission serves as a practical proving ground in infiltration and lockpicking. Operatives are outfitted with specialized thieves' tools from Estelle Gendry before marching into hostile Kirin Tor territory. Cracking the secured chest in Ambermill demonstrates that an operative has progressed beyond raw street brutality into an indispensable espionage asset for the Forsaken.

quest:2.text: Sharptalon's Claw. Sharptalon's Claw is a trophy quest representing the defeat of the ferocious hippogryph Sharptalon in Ashenvale. Taking the creature's severed talon back to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post proves your skill and protects Horde supply lines through the ancient forest. As the Horde attempts to carve out resources in Ashenvale, the native fauna proves just as perilous as the night elven sentinels. Sharptalon, a notoriously aggressive hippogryph, haunted the canopies and paths winding toward Splintertree Post. The beast preyed upon vulnerable peons and couriers traveling between the forward logging camps and the outpost, severely hampering Horde operations in the region. Under the guidance of the tauren huntress Senani Thunderheart, Horde stalkers are tasked with clearing out the deadlier predators lurking beneath Ashenvale's canopy. Carving the massive talon from Sharptalon serves as undeniable evidence that the sky-terror has fallen. Delivering the trophy to Splintertree Post earns honor among the outpost's defenders and brings relief to the frightened laborers who must walk the woods.

quest:20.text: Blackrock Menace. Marshal Marris of Lakeshire tasks adventurers with culling the aggressive Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. By seizing their battleworn axes, the town's defenders hope to break the siege tightening around the settlement. Lakeshire finds itself hemmed in on multiple fronts, but none pose so dire a threat as the Blackrock orcs spilling over from the fiery Burning Steppes. Having pushed south into Redridge, these veteran raiders have seized strongholds and roam the craggy passes. Their presence keeps the townspeople effectively penned inside the settlement, cutting off trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads. Marshal Marris, commander of the beleaguered Lakeshire guard, cannot spare a detachment to assault their positions outright. Instead, he enlists roaming adventurers to bleed the invaders' forward scouts and foot soldiers. By demanding their crude, battleworn axes as proof of death, Marris seeks to thin the invaders' numbers both around Stonewatch to the north and in the rugged pockets of southeastern Redridge.

quest:200.text: Bookie Herod. Lieutenant Doren fears a spy among his own men after Kurzen discovered Thorsen's secret. To uncover how the secret slipped out, an investigator must infiltrate Kurzen's Compound and recover the records kept by Kurzen's logistics officer. Following the discovery of Thorsen's secret, Lieutenant Doren suspects that a traitor operates within their midst. The intelligence leak threatens their operations, and finding the traitor has become an urgent concern. Thorsen maintained a line of communication directly into Kurzen's Compound through Bookie Herod, the colonel's logistics officer. Because Herod knows how Kurzen's Compound is run from day to day, Doren believes the officer's written records hold the truth about how the operation was exposed. Reaching Bookie Herod's paperwork requires venturing into Kurzen's Compound. During Doren's time serving under Kurzen, Herod kept his office on the top floor of the compound's lone two-story house. There, among supply requisitions and missives from Colonel Kurzen himself, lie the documents that could trace how the secret was betrayed.

quest:201.text: Investigate the Camp. Investigate the Camp is an expedition task originating in Booty Bay to scout a newly established hunters' campsite in Stranglethorn Vale. Commissioned by Krazek, it tasks travelers with confirming rumors that the legendary dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary has arrived near Lake Nazferiti. Reports circulating through the docks of Booty Bay speak of an expedition of big-game hunters encamped in the northern jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Word has reached Krazek that the camp lies along the river just past the Venture Company's busy mining claim near Lake Nazferiti. In a lawless jungle teeming with dangers and competing interests, unexplained armed encampments always demand a watchful eye. What makes this particular expedition notable is the rumored presence of Hemet Nesingwary himself. The renowned dwarven marksman is known throughout the lands as an elite explorer with influential ties. Krazek prefers to take no chances with powerful figures operating in the hinterlands, sending scouts upriver to confirm whether the legendary hunter has truly arrived.

quest:203.text: The Second Rebellion. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks help against the overwhelming forces of Colonel Kurzen. Outnumbered ten to one by a cunning tactician, the rebels must rely on swift, covert strikes to survive. Cutting down Kurzen's jungle fighters is the first step toward relieving the relentless pressure on their refuge. The soldiers at the Rebel Camp face dire odds against Colonel Kurzen. Yohwa explains that the Colonel is a brilliant military tactician whose force outnumbers the rebellion by at least ten to one. Unable to wage an open war of attrition, the rebels have no choice but to adopt the Colonel's own covert tactics, launching quick incursions into his encampment to thin his ranks and escaping before heavy reinforcements can retaliate. To stem the tide, Yohwa asks you to push east into Kurzen's stronghold and eliminate a sizable contingent of his jungle fighters. Thinning out these foot soldiers eases the pressure bearing down on the Rebel Camp.

quest:204.text: Bad Medicine. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks to blunt Colonel Kurzen's military advantage by targeting his medical support. The renegades rely on powerful remedies and toxins concocted by their practitioners, leaving the resistance fighters desperate to turn those same concoctions to their own advantage. Colonel Kurzen has bolstered his jungle force with numerous medicine men who heal his forces and poison Yohwa's fighters with venom fern extracts. To turn the tide of the conflict, Sergeant Yohwa directs adventurers into the Kurzen Compound to scavenge those vital supplies. Securing their jungle remedies will help treat wounded fighters at the Rebel Camp, while capturing a sample of their venom fern extract will enable the resistance to study the toxin and manufacture their own cures.

quest:2040.text: Underground Assault. Underground Assault is an Alliance quest offered by Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. Tasked with aiding the displaced gnomes, adventurers venture into the Deadmines to salvage an intact power core from a goblin shredder. This stolen component is destined to power drilling machines intended to spearhead the liberation of Gnomeregan. Following the catastrophic fall of Gnomeregan to the primitive troggs, surviving gnomish tinkerers have been forced into exile across Khaz Modan and Stormwind. Rather than wallowing in defeat, engineers like Shoni the Shilent are already devising mechanical operations to breach their lost home. The primary obstacle is the dense, subterranean rock surrounding the technocratic city, requiring massive tunneling engines known as gyrodrillmatic excavationators. Lacking the necessary localized power grids in human lands, the gnomes have turned their sights to an unlikely and volatile alternative: goblin heavy machinery operating in the criminal underworld. Deep within the twisting shafts of the Deadmines in Westfall, Edwin VanCleef's Defias Brotherhood employs goblin engineers to manufacture war machines, including a fully operational goblin shredder. Shoni directs Alliance operatives to infiltrate this foundry, destroy or dismantle the lumbering automaton, and recover its specialized heart—the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. By commandeering the potent goblin power supply, the exiled gnomes gain the raw mechanical output needed to bore through the subterranean perimeter and launch a counteroffensive to reclaim Gnomeregan.

quest:2078.text: Gyromast's Revenge. Along Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast seeks payback from the murlocs who plundered his wrecked ship. He sends you to reactivate his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100. Gelkak Gyromast is stranded on Darkshore, but he will not accept defeat by the shore-dwelling murlocs. He has salvaged the pieces needed for his scheme and now seeks revenge on the tribe and its chief. Rather than take up his cutlass and wade into the surf, the eccentric captain turns to engineering. He entrusts you with a winding key and asks you to handle his mechanical subordinate.

quest:2098.text: Gyromast's Retrieval. On Darkshore's coast, Gelkak Gyromast needs help restoring his mechanical first mate. His winding key shattered on the rocks, and wildlife and murlocs scavenged the three pieces. Recovering them is the first step toward setting his crew right. Gelkak Gyromast is a gnome pirate stranded on Darkshore, far from the South Seas. He says aggressive threshadons attacked and sank his vessel just off the coast. The wreck cast him ashore among the flotsam, marooned and separated from his crew. Gelkak's first concern is his first mate, not provisions or gold. The companion needs a specialized key to operate, but the key shattered into three pieces when Gelkak crashed on the rocky shoals. Before he could gather them, reef crawlers on the beach, foreststriders near the woods, and scavengers from the Greymist murloc tribe carried the shiny pieces away.

quest:213.text: Hostile Takeover. Gelriz has been muscling out the moguls appointed by the trade princes and now makes a move on the most notorious pirate of all, and Baron Revilgaz will not stand for it. In response, Kebok in Booty Bay directs adventurers to steal strange blue crystals that Venture Company geologists have been finding near Lake Nazferiti. Gelriz has stepped over the line by shoving aside moguls chosen by the trade princes and making a move on the most notorious pirate of all. Baron Revilgaz refuses to permit such insolence, instructing Kebok to handle the intrusion however he sees fit. Kebok's chosen response is outright theft, targeting the strange blue stones that Venture Company mining crews have been unearthing. Venture Company geologists operating around Lake Nazferiti have taken a keen interest in these unusual crystals. Kebok wants eight samples brought back to Booty Bay, unconcerned with how they are acquired so long as they end up in his hands.

quest:215.text: Jungle Secrets. After being rescued from an ambush in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he re-enlisted with Kurzen's men. He directs you back to the Rebel Camp so his commander can verify his covert intentions. Following his rescue, Private Thorsen admits the scene looks bad and asks to explain. He claims Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men to gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. What seemed to be an opportunity to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound quickly turned disastrous, forcing Thorsen to refer you directly to Doren at the Rebel Camp for official confirmation while begging for complete discretion.

quest:2158.text: Rest and Relaxation. Rest and Relaxation is an introductory Alliance quest directing newly trained adventurers from Northshire south along the road to the Lion's Pride Inn. Run by Innkeeper Farley, the bustling Goldshire tavern offers food, drink, and a warm hearth for those seeking a reprieve from the road. After cutting their teeth in Northshire, weary travelers are pointed south toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. The road south leads directly to the beloved tavern, run by Innkeeper Farley. For new adventurers stepping out into the wider forest, it represents the first major outpost offering hearth, shelter, and hot meals away from the Abbey. Innkeeper Farley takes pride in his establishment's hospitality, operating under the motto of providing rest and relaxation for the tired and cold. Adventurers who mention their referral can take advantage of Farley's good graces, settling by the open fire to enjoy a warm meal, sturdy ale, and a much-needed respite before journeying further into Elwynn.

quest:219.text: Missing In Action. Missing In Action is an Alliance escort mission in the Redridge Mountains to rescue Corporal Keeshan from Blackrock orc captivity. After his regiment was wiped out in the hills, Keeshan was knocked unconscious and dragged into a cave fortress. Guiding the wounded soldier safely back to Lakeshire helps the local garrison confirm the grim fate of their missing men. The Redridge Mountains have grown increasingly perilous as Blackrock orcs descend from the northern peaks. Patrols sent out by the town guard frequently run into ambushes, and Corporal Keeshan's unit suffered the worst of it. Outnumbered and overwhelmed, most of the soldiers in his regiment were cut down on the spot. Keeshan survived only because a crushing blow knocked him cold before he could be executed, allowing the orcs to drag him back to their cave as a prisoner. Battered, concussed, and held deep within enemy territory, Keeshan could not make the trek back down the mountain alone. Escorting him down to the safety of Lakeshire takes him past swarming orc warbands that occupy the ridgelines. Reaching Lakeshire alive brings sorely needed relief to Marshal Marris, who has been trying to piece together what happened to the missing regiment while bracing Lakeshire for further attacks.

quest:220.text: Call of Water. Brine's water reaches Islen Waterseer on the eastern Barrens coast, where the next part of the shamanic trial begins. The vial holds water Brine prepared and blessed, the base for a sapta that lets an initiate see water spirits in Silverpine Forest. After the trials in the southern Barrens, Brine gives the shaman initiate a Vial of Purest Water. The water comes from pure springs and has been consecrated by Brine's rites. The initiate carries it back to the eastern coast, where Islen Waterseer keeps watch. The water links Brine's teachings with the rites of the totem. Islen explains that mortal eyes cannot easily see water spirits. To meet them, an initiate drinks a brew called a sapta. The water from Brine will form the base of that draught and open the shaman's senses to what ordinary sight cannot find. Seeing the spirits is only part of the journey; they will test the initiate.

quest:221.text: Worgen in the Woods. As the Nightbane pack encroaches further upon Darkshire, Calor tasks adventurers with striking down the pack's primary rank-and-file stalkers. These ferocious Dark Runners have overrun the nearby Rotting Orchard, threatening to completely surround the besieged town. While scouts first encountered lone worgen weaving shadowy magic on the fringes of the forest, Calor's rangings revealed a far more urgent tactical threat. Larger, swifter beasts known as Nightbane Dark Runners have massed in the Rotting Orchard just southwest of Darkshire. Rather than merely lurking beneath the canopy, these predators form the bulk of the pack's numbers, establishing a staging ground within striking distance of the village gates.

quest:222.text: Worgen in the Woods. As the Nightbane pack tightens its grip on Duskwood, Calor directs adventurers to strike against their deadliest ranks. Taking the fight directly to their southern dens and mines, defenders push back the feral threat encroaching on Darkshire. The worgen infestation haunting Duskwood is far from mindless chaos. Having carved out territory in the dark expanse south of Darkshire, the beasts known as the Nightbane have begun establishing fortified camps. Calor watches their bonfires flicker in the distance with growing dread, noting that the creatures have occupied deep caves and abandoned mining shafts. Among them, the Vile Fangs and Tainted Ones represent the most vicious breeds, displaying ferocious savagery and a tenacity that threatens to overwhelm the town's perimeter.

quest:223.text: Worgen in the Woods. This errand delivers Calor's letter of recommendation to Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, concluding your pursuit of the savage worgen haunting Duskwood. Impressed by your prowess against the beastly invaders, Calor points you directly to a man fighting deeper threats among the shadows. Having culled the Nightbane pack stalking Roland's Doom and the shadowed glades, you earn the hard-won respect of Calor. Stationed on the darkened frontiers of the woods, Calor is rarely eager to hand out compliments, let alone formal introductions. Handing over a faded scrap of parchment, he directs you to deliver his word directly to Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, remarking that if they had more fighters of your caliber, their small cohort might finally eclipse the town's beleaguered Night Watch. Jonathan Carevin operates within Darkshire under tremendous strain, wary of outsiders and perpetually pressed for time. The town faces onslaughts not only from slavering worgen, but also from unresting undead, shadowy demonic forces, and traitorous cultists aiding the corruption from within. Receiving Calor's glowing endorsement breaks Carevin's cold demeanor, confirming you as a trustworthy blade dedicated to preserving the Light against the suffocating terrors of Duskwood.

quest:226.text: Wolves at Our Heels. Wolves at Our Heels is an Alliance quest offered by Lars at Sven's Camp in western Duskwood. Tasked with hunting the rabid and starving dire wolves stalking the surrounding woods, travelers help clear immediate wilderness threats so Sven and Lars can focus on their vendetta against the necromancer Morbent Fel. Tucked away along the western hills of Duskwood near the Westfall border, Sven Yorgen and his companion Lars maintain an isolated outpost. Living away from Darkshire leaves them entirely reliant on their own foraging and hunting to survive. However, carrying fresh game through these dark woods makes Lars an irresistible target for the ravenous predators stalking the shadowed riverbanks and underbrush. The local packs of starving and rabid dire wolves roam primarily to the north and east of the camp toward the river. By culling these frenzied beasts, travelers lift an immediate siege on Lars's hunting efforts. Thinning out the wolves frees both men from constantly fighting for their daily bread, allowing them to turn their full attention toward the necromancer Morbent Fel, who lurks further east.

quest:2282.text: Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a pivotal training assignment given to Alliance rogues by Lucius in Lakeshire. Dispatched to the nearby mill with a set of thieves' tools, initiates are tasked with infiltrating an area under Blackrock orc scrutiny to crack a locked chest and retrieve a token of thievery. In Lakeshire, rogue instructors do not bother with abstract lectures when a locked chest can teach the lesson faster. Lucius sends promising operatives northeast along the road to Alther's Mill, equipping them with their first set of thieves' tools. To earn their formal Certificate of Thievery, novices must slip into the abandoned mill, pick open Lucius's personal lockbox, and bring back the token cached within. While Alther's Mill was once an ordinary lumber outpost, it has recently drawn the dangerous attention of the Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. Lucius gleefully treats the encroaching warmongers as an added layer of practical examination. Prowling through enemy-held territory to pick locks undetected is precisely the kind of trial SI:7 expects its agents to survive.

quest:23.text: Ursangous's Paw. This quest represents the proof of felling Ursangous, one of the most ferocious and legendary predators prowling Ashenvale. Bringing the beast's severed paw to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post earns honor among the Horde's trackers. As part of the Ashenvale Hunt, trackers operating out of Splintertree Post are tasked with pursuing the ancient beasts that dominate the dense forest canopy. Ursangous ranks among the fiercest of these apex predators, known for killing numerous travelers and warriors who crossed his path. Taking down such a beast is no small feat, and claiming his paw serves as undeniable physical proof that the mighty creature has finally met his match.

quest:230.text: Sven's Camp. Sven's Camp is an Alliance quest in Duskwood that uncovers a crucial clue regarding the tragedy at the Yorgen homestead. By unearthing a buried, untitled journal from a mound of loose dirt on the abandoned farm, adventurers piece together who witnessed the slaughter of Sven Yorgen's family. Sven Yorgen was away when dark riders struck his farm, returning only to find his family murdered and his farm in ruins. Consumed by grief and vengeance, he sent allies to search the wreckage of the homestead. Hidden beneath a mound of freshly turned earth, a small, dirt-stained book lay buried where a shadowy figure had hastily hidden it.

quest:235.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. Warcaller Gorlach sends the Horde north into Ashenvale to join the hunt. Report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post, where the Horde is pushing its frontier into the ancient forest. Orgrimmar needs timber, meat, and safe trade routes to keep growing. Warcaller Gorlach carries orders from the Horde's high command, sending seasoned wanderers and new adventurers toward active campaigns. For those coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, Ashenvale is the next test of skill and survival. North of the Barrens, Ashenvale holds two Horde strongholds. Splintertree Post lies in the eastern woods, while Zoram'gar Outpost stands along the western coast. Senani Thunderheart coordinates operations from Splintertree Post, organizing trackers and hunters to face the beasts beneath the canopy and night elven sentinels who contest the Horde's claims.

quest:2359.text: Klaven's Tower. Agent Kearnen watches Klaven's Tower from a camp in Westfall. Strange shipments and altered guards point to a threat inside the Defias Brotherhood. Near the river at Westfall's southeastern edge, Klaven's Tower rises north of the Dagger Hills. The Defias Brotherhood claims the stone spire, though its human thieves and brigands are common across the plains. Agent Kearnen has watched it alone for weeks and noticed strange developments. A bizarre shipment recently came straight from Duskwood's shadowed woods. Monstrous, deformed sentries escorted it, unlike any ordinary highwaymen.

quest:24.text: Shadumbra's Head. This quest represents the proof of victory over Shadumbra, a notoriously ferocious nightsaber stalking the western paths of Ashenvale. Taking the beast's severed head back to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post fulfills a key trial of the Ashenvale Hunt and secures travel routes toward the Zoram Strand. Shadumbra is no ordinary predator among the towering trees of Ashenvale. The great nightsaber stalked the wilderness west of Splintertree Post, preying upon Horde scouts and couriers attempting to journey toward the Zoram Strand. Her speed, stealth, and sheer savagery made travel on foot perilous, leaving Splintertree's defenders on edge whenever patrols moved west. As part of the Ashenvale Hunt, the tauren huntress Senani Thunderheart challenges Horde champions to track and fell the forest's apex beasts. Presenting Shadumbra's head is not merely a grim display of prowess; it serves as undeniable proof that the roads have been made safer and that the hunter has mastered one of Kalimdor's deadliest native stalkers.

quest:240.text: Return to Jitters. Return to Jitters concludes Chef Grual's culinary errand in Duskwood. Having prepared his infamous 'crab' cakes using the gooey legs of the local venom web spiders, Grual sends you back to the starving, terrified hermit at Raven Hill. Delivering the meal finally satisfies Jitters' desperate hunger. Duskwood is short on conventional livestock and sea life, leaving Chef Grual at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to improvise with whatever the blighted forest provides. His renowned 'Dusky Crab Cakes' contain no actual crab meat at all, relying instead on gooey legs harvested from the venom web spiders creeping through the wood. Grual considers this resourceful cooking; anyone with a delicate stomach might view it with horror. Jitters spends his days huddled at Raven Hill, utterly consumed by fright and paralyzed by whatever horrors drove him out of the woods. Weak with terror and unable to muster the courage to hunt or forage for himself, his empty stomach only amplifies his distress. Receiving the warm cakes brings a rare moment of relief to the trembling vagrant, who is far too hungry to question what kind of 'crab' Chef Grual used.
