His recipe dries quickly and resists smearing, but the ink can dry in its pot if left too long. To make more, he needs raw Rethban iron ore, mined in the rocky Redridge Mountains. Lakeshire has little room for a distant scribe’s request. Foreman Oslow oversees laborers busy strengthening barricades, rebuilding ruined structures, and defending the town from ongoing Blackrock orc raids. With no workers to spare for mining, travelers must seek the ore in the perilous Rethban Caverns themselves.

quest:346.text: Return to Kristoff. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Stormwind for a borrowed book to return. After a long search and a delay in Northshire, you bring The Stresses of Iron back to the Cathedral of Light. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Cathedral Square for The Stresses of Iron, a book on metallurgy. Its trail led from Stormwind Keep's Royal Library to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton was copying the text by hand. Paxton ran short of Rethban ore for the scribe's ink, so the work stalled. With the ore retrieved and the copy complete, you bring the original book back to Stormwind. Northshire's copyists preserve civic and spiritual lore through patient work. Brother Paxton asks you to apologize to Librarian Milton Sheaf, a sign of how thin the abbey's resources have worn. Scribes must copy valuable books stroke by stroke with mineral-rich ink before returning them to Stormwind's care, making a book request a long undertaking.

quest:347.text: Rethban Ore. Foreman Oslow sends you into Rethban Caverns in Redridge for a dark mineral the scribes of Northshire Abbey need for ink. It is too soft for strong weapons or armor, but its color makes it useful for their work. Scribes at Northshire Abbey prize Rethban Ore for its dark, flat color. Bart Rethban discovered the mineral, but it has little use at an armorer’s anvil. Smelted metal from the ore lacks the strength needed for sturdy weapons or plate. Its raw color instead makes a valued base for manuscript dyes. The main deposits lie in the northern mountains of Redridge, inside Rethban Caverns. Lakeshire’s stoneworkers have left the cavern, driven out by a fierce band of Redridge gnolls. The gnolls put drudgers to work chipping ore from the rocky veins for their own crude purposes. Brother Paxton, a monk at Northshire Abbey, needs the pigment to copy historic texts. His work on The Stresses of Iron has stopped without the proper dye. Messengers and adventurers now travel into gnoll-held territory to bring him the raw stone.

quest:349.text: Stranglethorn Fever. Deep within Stranglethorn Vale, Witch Doctor Unbagwa claims to know how to draw out the beast known as Mokk the Savage. Before communion with the spirits can begin, the witch doctor requires a Gorilla Fang as an offering. Once the ritual commences, defending the troll from agitated jungle beasts is necessary to lure the creature forth. Witch Doctor Unbagwa possesses the ritual knowledge needed to summon Mokk the Savage out of the surrounding jungle. To begin the incantation, the witch doctor demands a Gorilla Fang. Communing with the spirits carries a heavy risk, as the ritual chant draws the attention of other gorilla beasts in the vicinity, demanding protection while the magic does its work.

quest:350.text: Look to an Old Friend. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to seek an unusual contact in Stormwind's Trade District. Noble corruption shields traitors from ordinary justice, so Shaw turns to the city's finest cheesemonger and his intelligence network.

quest:3513.text: The Runed Scroll. A silvery ribbon marks the Runed Scroll found in Kalimdor's wilds as a formal message from across the border. Finding it sends Horde scouts to the Mor'shan Rampart to warn its guards of activity to the north. A fine silvery ribbon binds the scroll, unlike the rough leathers and parchment common in the Barrens. Its craft and script point to the night elves beneath Ashenvale's canopies to the north. With every ridge and road contested, a message taken from the enemy could matter greatly to the Horde's front lines. The scroll belongs with local command, not at the Warchief's hall in Orgrimmar. Kadrak, an orc warrior, watches the border from the Mor'shan Rampart, where the Barrens' red earth meets Ashenvale's forests. Bringing the scroll to this outpost gives its guards word of night elf troop movements.

quest:3514.text: Horde Presence. At the Barrens border, Kadrak sends a Horde champion into Stonetalon Peak after a missive is intercepted. The champion is to kill the dryad Rynthariel and plant a Horde banner inside the Talon Den. Kadrak watches the Barrens' northern boundary for Alliance and night elf incursions. After a messenger carrying a runed scroll is cut down, he decodes the missive and traces it to Rynthariel the Keymaster, an influential dryad in Stonetalon Peak. Kadrak chooses to strike rather than simply guard the mountain passes, hoping to deter future scouts from probing Horde territory. Horde warriors enter the Talon Den, a cavern overlooking Stonetalon Peak. Killing Rynthariel deals a blow to local night elf coordination. Kadrak's banner is planted inside the cave, its red standard marking the heart of dryad territory with a warning: incursions into the Barrens will meet decisive violence.

quest:359.text: Forsaken Duties. Forsaken Duties is a reconnaissance mission assigned by Magistrate Sevren in Brill to assess Scourge activity along the eastern perimeter of Tirisfal Glades. It establishes the constant threat posed by the Scourge slipping past The Bulwark and endangering local settlements. Magistrate Sevren oversees the security of Brill and the surrounding countryside, keeping a nervous eye on the eastern borders of Tirisfal Glades. With the Scourge swarming across the Western Plaguelands, Sevren requires constant reconnaissance from frontline sentries to ensure undead horrors do not slip past the perimeter unnoticed. Travelers willing to assist are dispatched south and east down the main thoroughfare to gather an urgent tactical assessment from Deathguard Linnea. Stationed at an eastern outpost along the road, Deathguard Linnea observes the frontier firsthand. Her findings confirm the magistrates fears: while the fortified position at The Bulwark successfully holds off the main Scourge host, small groups of undead manage to bypass the defenses on occasion. These stray forces have begun congregating around the nearby Balnir Farmstead, posing a localized but dangerous threat to Tirisfal Glades.

quest:373.text: The Unsent Letter. In the Deadmines, The Unsent Letter waits to be carried to Stormwind. Its delivery reveals the grievances and shared history binding Edwin VanCleef to the city's master builders. Edwin VanCleef falls aboard his juggernaut beneath Moonbrook, leaving behind more than a broken rebellion. A newly penned, sealed letter is tucked into his clothing. He addressed it not to a criminal lieutenant or financier, but to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect.

quest:3765.text: The Corruption Abroad. Argos Nightwhisper, a night elf envoy visiting Stormwind, seeks capable adventurers to cross the Great Sea and aid his brother in northern Kalimdor. His brother Gershala studies spreading ecological decay in Darkshore, where fresh hands are desperately needed. While Stormwind contends with internal turmoil and regional unrest, representatives from the distant kaldorei lands can be found wandering its stone streets. Argos Nightwhisper came seeking seasoned champions willing to look beyond human borders. The kaldorei are relatively new allies to the Eastern Kingdoms, and formal military aid is scarce, leaving family members and researchers to recruit whatever independent champions answer the call. The destination Argos points toward is Auberdine, a misty port town resting on the fog-shrouded coast of Darkshore. There, his brother Gershala conducts vital research into an ominous malaise afflicting the local wildlife and flora. Answering the summons means a long voyage from Stormwind Harbor across the Great Sea, marking a traveler's first real foray into the ancient wilderness of Kalimdor.

quest:377.text: Crime and Punishment. Crime and Punishment is an Alliance bounty originating in Darkshire that demands the extrajudicial execution of a grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Councilman Millstipe issues the contract after the House of Nobles overrides Duskwood's death sentence for Dextren Ward. Carrying out the hit satisfies local vengeance while delivering a sharp warning to the capital's negligent aristocracy. Duskwood already suffers beneath a shroud of creeping horrors and official indifference from the capital. When Dextren Ward was caught digging up fresh corpses from the Darkshire cemetery to sell to the necromancer Morbent Fel, the town's ruling council showed no mercy. Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced the grave robber to beheadment. However, before the axe could fall, the House of Nobles intervened, claiming Ward as an imperial prisoner and transferring him to the high-security cells of the Stormwind Stockade. To Councilman Millstipe and the grieving citizens of Darkshire, sparing Ward from the headsman's block was an intolerable insult. The nobles in their secure city showed complete disregard for the torment suffered by frontier families whose dead relatives were fed into Fel's dark craft. Frustrated by Stormwind's bureaucratic meddling, Millstipe recruits daring mercenaries to infiltrate the riotous Stockade, assassinate Ward in his cell, and sever his hand as proof of execution.

quest:378.text: The Fury Runs Deep. This quest represents Motley Garmason's bitter quest for vengeance against the Dark Iron dwarf Kam Deepfury. Deepfury masterminded the assault on the Thandol Span, which claimed the lives of Bronzebeard defenders, including the brother of Longbraid the Grim. Dissatisfied with Stormwind's political detention of the culprit, Motley enlists an adventurer to enact dwarven justice inside the Stockade. The northern reaches of the Wetlands bleed from perpetual clashes between the Bronzebeard defenders at Dun Modr and the insurgent Dark Iron dwarves. When the Thandol Span came under attack, the sabotage cost vital dwarven lives, including the brother of Longbraid the Grim. Intelligence gathered by Roggo revealed that Kam Deepfury planned the deceitful strike. Instead of facing execution on the front lines, however, Deepfury ended up secured inside the Stormwind Stockade—held as a political prisoner rather than executed for murder. Stationed at Dun Modr, Motley Garmason refuses to allow Stormwind's political calculations to shield a war criminal. To Motley, human bureaucracy has placed decorum above blood debts. Bound by duty to remain at Longbraid's side in the Wetlands, Motley tasks trusted champions to march deep beneath the human capital, brave the rioting Stockade, and claim Deepfury's severed head to settle the clan's score once and for all.

quest:386.text: What Comes Around.... What Comes Around... is an Alliance quest offered by Guard Berton in Lakeshire, who is infuriated by the political delays surrounding an orcish war criminal. Players are directed into the Stormwind Stockade to execute Targorr the Dread before corrupt nobility can arrange his escape. Targorr the Dread gained infamy in the Redridge Mountains serving as supreme executioner under General Gath'Ilzogg, chieftain of the Blackrock orcs entrenched at Stonewatch Keep. Renowned for savage cruelty even among the Blackrock invaders, Targorr personally oversaw the torture and execution of numerous defenders of Redridge. Following his eventual capture, he was transferred to the capital's high-security prison, the Stormwind Stockade, and condemned to death for his atrocities against the realm.

quest:387.text: Quell The Uprising. Deep beneath the cobblestones of Stormwind, the high-security Stockade has fallen into total chaos. Following a coordinated breakout led by incarcerated members of the Defias Brotherhood, Warden Thelwater is urgently commissioning adventurers to cut down the rioting inmates and restore order before the capital learns how compromised the facility truly is. The Stockade was built to contain the most dangerous criminals, conspirators, and outlaws threatening the Kingdom of Stormwind. However, a sudden, violent uprising orchestrated by imprisoned Defias operatives has wrested control of the cell blocks directly from the guards. With the prison thoroughly overrun and corridors choked with armed felons, normal protocol has collapsed entirely. Rather than mounting a structured retaking, prison authorities are relying on visiting champions to fight their way through the riots. Warden Thelwater's command to execute Defias prisoners on sight reflects both sheer desperation and an effort of self-preservation. Suspecting foul play behind the coordinated mutiny, the warden fears that if the broader nobility or the House of Nobles discovers the facility is out of hand, his post will be forfeit. By decreeing death as the immediate penalty for insurgency, Thelwater hopes brute force will break the inmates' spirits and quell the rebellion before word leaks past the canal gates.

quest:388.text: The Color of Blood. The Color of Blood is a personal task given by Nikova Raskol, a grieving grandmother living in Stormwind City. Consumed by anger over the murder of her young grandson inside the city's prison, she hires adventurers to venture into The Stockade and claim the Defias gang's trademark red bandanas as retribution. When Stormwind's regular military forces were deployed away to distant fronts, local defense fell upon volunteer recruits and the city's youth. Nikova Raskol's grandson, Mac, was only fourteen years old when he took up arms as a guard within The Stockade. Tasked with watching hardened criminals and mutinous members of the Defias Brotherhood, the young guard was thrust into an intensely dangerous environment far beyond his experience. Behind bars, the captured Defias inmates began ripping apart their provided wool prison blankets, fashioning the shredded fabric into makeshift red bandanas. These crude garments served as identifying gang colors, signaling their continued loyalty to the Brotherhood even inside prison walls. When young Mac reprimanded the prisoners and tried to enforce discipline, the inmates stabbed the boy in the back, leaving him dead on the stone floor. Devastated by Mac's pointless death, Nikova seeks cold revenge rather than official bureaucracy. She dispatches brave adventurers into the depths of The Stockade to cull the rioting prisoners and bring back ten of their cherished red bandanas—symbols dyed the color of her grandson's spilled blood. Presenting these blood-colored trophies offers a grim sense of closure to a broken family.

quest:389.text: Bazil Thredd. In Stormwind, Bazil Thredd holds insight into the Defias Brotherhood's lingering plots. After an unsent letter is recovered from the Deadmines, City Architect Baros Alexston directs you to the Defias leader's right-hand man, now locked beneath the streets in the high-security Stockade. Baros Alexston shares a bitter history with Edwin VanCleef. Both led the Stonemasons Guild, charged with rebuilding Stormwind from the ashes of the First and Second Wars. When the kingdom's magnificent white walls and towers were finished, the nobility refused to pay the masons their promised wages. Some senior members received bureaucratic posts to quiet them, but VanCleef refused to abandon the rank-and-file laborers. He led a violent riot out of the city and founded the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:391.text: The Stockade Riots. The Stockade Riots is an Alliance quest issued by Warden Thelwater at the gates of Stormwind's prison. To quell the ongoing uprising and prove your loyalty to the city guards, you are ordered to descend into the chaos and execute the riot's ringleader, Bazil Thredd. Deep beneath the cobblestones of the Mage Quarter, the Stockade has descended into utter lawlessness. Criminals, Defias insurgents, and violent cutthroats have broken containment and seized the cell blocks, turning the facility into an impenetrable war zone. Warden Thelwater and his guards are clinging desperately to the entrance, entirely unable to push inward and restore order through ordinary means.

quest:392.text: The Curious Visitor. After the Stockade uprising, Warden Thelwater has a troubling discovery about Bazil Thredd. For months before the riot, a man named Maelik visited Thredd with legitimate papers. Warden Thelwater learned that Bazil Thredd had not been abandoned by his former comrades, as the guards believed. Months before the riot, a quiet visitor began meeting with Thredd once or twice a week. He passed every inspection, carried authorized paperwork, and gave his name as Maelik. Thelwater suspects the visits helped coordinate the bloody uprising. He gathers a physical description and sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston to learn who the visitor was.

quest:393.text: Shadow of the Past. In Stormwind, the trail from a Stockade prisoner leads into the city’s hidden dealings. Baros Alexston sends you to Mathias Shaw after a mysterious visitor spoke with Bazil Thredd. Baros Alexston cannot identify the visitor who spoke with Bazil Thredd, the Stockade’s chief prisoner. Warden Thelwater’s account has brought investigators to the city architect, but he has no name to offer. Instead, Baros points you toward Master Mathias Shaw, who leads SI:7 and makes it his business to know Stormwind’s secrets.

quest:394.text: The Head of the Beast. In Stormwind, The Head of the Beast carries you from Elling Trias to Master Mathias Shaw in Old Town. Reporting Lord Gregor Lescovar’s death confirms your place in Stormwind’s covert intelligence network. Master Mathias Shaw directs Stormwind’s covert apparatus through SI:7 from hidden chambers in Old Town. When you report Lescovar’s death, Shaw recognizes your skill and ruthlessness, praises your efficiency, and thanks you for serving the people of Stormwind.

quest:395.text: Brotherhood's End. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Gregor Lescovar's killing leaves dangerous questions behind. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston and warns you to keep the killer's identity quiet. Baros Alexston, the City Architect who helped rebuild Stormwind as a stonemason, is relieved to hear that Lescovar is dead. Edwin VanCleef had marked Alexston and other prominent figures in the rebuilding effort for vengeance after the Stonemasons were cast out without pay. With Lescovar silenced and the conspiracy disrupted, Alexston believes the immediate threat to the kingdom's architects and nobility has passed.

quest:396.text: An Audience with the King. At Stormwind Keep, An Audience with the King brings the Defias report before the Crown. After the long investigation across Westfall and the Deadmines, the heroes carry City Architect Baros Alexston's findings to the capital. Edwin VanCleef has been defeated, and the conspiracy beneath Moonbrook has been dismantled. City Architect Baros Alexston prepares an official report for the Crown. He believes the adventurer who broke the guild's criminal enterprise should be honored before the monarch. You carry the detailed findings across Stormwind's grand canals to Stormwind Keep, expecting to meet the realm's sovereign.

quest:401.text: Wait for Sirra to Finish. This brief pause marks the moment Sirra Von'Indi deciphers the cryptic note delivered from the reclusive hermit Abercrombie. As he puts quill to paper in Darkshire's Town Hall, an ominous dread settles over the room, hinting that the hermit's words are far darker than expected. After receiving the mysterious note penned by the hermit Abercrombie, Sirra Von'Indi requires only a short spell to decipher its text. As a resident scholar aiding the Night Watch and town leadership, he undertakes the task without realizing immediately what horrors the message conceals.

quest:4021.text: Counterattack!. At Regthar Deathgate’s outpost west of the Crossroads, Kolkar warriors strike back after their leaders fall. They have crossed from Desolace, and Warlord Krom'zar leads their charge. The Kolkar have suffered a deep humiliation in the Barrens. Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark are dead, leaving the remaining centaur shattered and without direction. Word of their defeat travels west across the mountains to their ancestral homeland in Desolace. There, a fresh force of hardened Kolkar warriors rallies instead of scattering into the scrubland. Burning for blood and retribution, they cross into the Barrens and march against the young Horde encampments.

quest:442.text: Assault on Fenris Isle. Assault on Fenris Isle is the climactic military directive issued by High Executor Hadrec to eradicate the Scourge stronghold in Silverpine Forest. To break the Lich King's grip upon Lake Lordamere, Forsaken agents are sent to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. For weeks, Fenris Isle has stood as a poisonous blister in the heart of Lake Lordamere. While the Forsaken secured the western roads and established their presence at the Sepulcher, the Scourge entrenched themselves inside Fenris Keep. Commanded by the powerful necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, this island outpost threatened not only Silverpine Forest but the southern waterways leading toward the Undercity itself. High Executor Hadrec recognizes that the Forsaken will never truly hold Silverpine while a servant of the Lich King conducts vile experiments right off their eastern shores.

quest:4542.text: Message to Freewind Post. Message to Freewind Post is a Horde quest tasking travelers with carrying urgent dispatches from Brave Moonhorn near the border lifts down into Thousand Needles. The missive warns Cliffwatcher Longhorn of intensifying centaur raids against local caravans. It also raises early concerns regarding the suspicious, standoffish behavior of the neighboring Grimtotem clan. Standing watch near the canyon's western approaches, Brave Moonhorn keeps a vigil over the roads leading down into Thousand Needles. With centaur aggression abruptly spiking, communication between border sentries and the regional leadership is vital. Moonhorn entrusts passing Horde adventurers with carrying an urgent dispatch southeast to Cliffwatcher Longhorn, the commander stationed atop the mesa settlement of Freewind Post. Upon receiving the message, Longhorn confirms the dire situation: a recent supply caravan was intercepted and slaughtered by marauding centaur, leaving Freewind Post in desperate need of retaliation and defense. Just as concerning is Moonhorn's parting caution to avoid the local Grimtotem tauren, whose uncharacteristically bizarre and hostile demeanor hints at deeper rifts brewing across the arid flats.

quest:455.text: The Algaz Gauntlet. The Algaz Gauntlet is an urgent military mission to fight through Dun Algaz, a critical mountain pass linking Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Orcs of the Dragonmaw clan have entrenched themselves in the tunnels, threatening to sever Ironforge's vital lifeline to Menethil Harbor. Adventurers are tasked with cutting down the orcish vanguard and delivering word of the invasion to Valstag Ironjaw. Dun Algaz serves as the solitary overland mountain pass carving through the crags between Loch Modan and the marshy basin of the Wetlands. For the dwarves of Ironforge, this stone corridor is essential for trade, troop movements, and supplies heading to Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's primary coastal port in the region. Should the pass fall, Ironforge's connection to the western seas is effectively strangled, leaving isolated outposts cut off from dwarven reinforcements. While remnants of the Dragonmaw clan have long haunted the hills and ruins of the Wetlands following the Second War, their sudden, organized push into Dun Algaz marks an aggressive escalation. Instead of lingering in their marshland enclaves, Dragonmaw scouts and grunts have seized the tunnels and fortified the pass. Mountaineer Rockgar enlists brave Alliance travelers to shatter this blockade by slaying the encroaching orcs and carrying word of the assault directly to Valstag Ironjaw in Menethil Harbor.

quest:4581.text: Kayneth Stillwind. This quest sends an Alliance courier from Astranaar eastward to the ancient outpost of Forest Song. Carrying a scouting missive from Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire, travelers seek out the druid Kayneth Stillwind to help him monitor the spread of corruption across the ancient woods. In the town of Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire stands watch over the western half of the forest. Word reaches her from the druid Kayneth Stillwind, stationed far out in Forest Song near the eastern reaches of Ashenvale. Deeply concerned by shifting wildlife behaviors and dark omens stirring along the coasts and woodlands, Kayneth requested a formal appraisal of the region's security. Swiftfire drafts her observations into a sealed note, trusting an able-bodied traveler to convey the dispatch safely across the treacherous central forest. Reaching Forest Song requires enduring the wilderness of Nightsong Woods, an area threatened by encroaching satyrs, hostile wildlife, and Horde excursions from the south. At the shrine of Forest Song, Kayneth Stillwind studies the delicate balance of Ashenvale's natural spirits. Reading Swiftfire's reconnaissance confirms his grim suspicions: the tainted influence creeping through the forest is neither isolated nor fleeting, and the druids will require further aid to confront the wickedness taking root.

quest:463.text: The Greenwarden. "The Greenwarden" is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing travelers deeper into the marshes of the Wetlands. Sent by First Mate Fitzsimmons from Menethil Harbor, adventurers venture northeast into the swamp to seek out a mysterious entity rumored to dwell among the beasts. Around the docks of Menethil Harbor, sailors and wanderers trade breathless stories of a beast lurking out in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons paints the Greenwarden as an appetite with legs, warning gullible seekers that stepping off the dry road means being bitten in two by 'ol' Greenie.' To the dockside folk, anything massive lurking out in the murky waters is just another man-eating hazard of the marsh.

quest:464.text: War Banners. Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor tasks Alliance champions with striking an encampment of Dragonmaw orcs northeast of the town and claiming their war banners. The remnant orcs, broken and scattered after the Second War, have begun gathering strength once again in the bogs of the Wetlands. During the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan subjugated the red dragonflight from the mountain fortress of Grim Batol. When their foul control broke, the liberated dragons turned upon their captors with ferocious vengeance, hunting the orcs nearly to extinction. What few survived fled Grim Batol into the high mountains east of Whelgar's Excavation, hidden away from the red flight's wrath. Though long believed broken beyond repair, the Dragonmaw have resurfaced. Northeast of Menethil Harbor, these savage survivors have raised an active war camp and planted their crimson standards in the marsh. Recognizing the danger of an aggressive orc force so close to the harbor town, Captain Stoutfist wants their ranks culled and their proud war banners torn down as proof of their defeat.

quest:465.text: Nek'rosh's Gambit. Nek'rosh's Gambit is an urgent strike mission commissioned by Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor. Learning that Chieftain Nek'rosh has constructed siege engines to bombard the vulnerable port town while reinforcements remain cut off at Dun Algaz, the Alliance sends brave volunteers deep into the marshes to burn the Dragonmaw catapults before an assault can begin. While Alliance adventurers were clashing with Dragonmaw raiding parties, dwarven scouts uncovered the clan's true ambition. Chieftain Nek'rosh has overseen the construction of full-scale siege catapults in the wetlands encampments. His goal is bold and catastrophic: to march his war engines to Menethil Harbor and batter down the fortress walls, wiping out the Alliance's primary shipping hub on the western coast. Menethil Harbor's peril is magnified by the choke point at Dun Algaz. Heavy skirmishes and greenskin activity in the mountain pass effectively isolate the lowlands from Ironforge's main garrisons. Without immediate aid from Khaz Modan, Captain Stoutfist cannot spare a defensive detachment to guard the perimeter, making a preemptive sabotage of the catapults the harbor's sole chance for survival. Armed with Dwarven Tinder, scouts must push directly into the heart of the Dragonmaw encampment. Setting the bulky timber engines ablaze robs Nek'rosh of his artillery, leaving his warriors exposed and denying them the firepower needed to crack Menethil's defenses before the warlord himself can be confronted.

quest:466.text: Search for Incendicite. Pilot Stonegear at Steelgrill's Depot seeks samples of volatile incendicite ore discovered in the Wetlands. Believing its explosive properties could revolutionize artillery munitions, he tasks miners with venturing north to extract the dangerous mineral from a secluded cave. Word of a rare and unstable mineral known as incendicite has reached the siege engine pilots and mechanics at Steelgrill's Depot. Rumors place rich veins inside a cavern northwest of Algaz Gate in the sodden marshlands of the Wetlands. Highly reactive and hazardous to handle, incendicite has developed a reputation for detonating in the faces of careless miners. Where others see a mining hazard, Pilot Stonegear sees military potential. If refined properly, incendicite could serve as a devastating propellant or payload for dwarven artillery, producing cannon shells capable of shattering fortified defenses. Stonegear aims to procure raw samples so courageous, or foolhardy, researchers can begin testing smelting techniques without leveling the depot.

quest:467.text: Stonegear's Search. Stonegear's Search is an Alliance directive directing adventurous travelers to Pilot Stonegear at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. The enthusiastic siege engine operator has caught wind of an exotic mineral and seeks a daring explorer to track down fresh fuel for his tank's ordnance. Dwarven siege engines are legendary feats of engineering, but their operators are rarely content leaving well enough alone. Word around Ironforge and Loch Modan quickly spreads that Pilot Stonegear, stationed just outside the capital, is scheming to boost his war machine's punch. Whether pointed his way by Pilot Longbeard or Mountaineer Kadrell, travelers are recruited simply to meet the ambitious pilot and hear his proposal. Pilot Stonegear makes his workshop at Steelgrill's Depot, the proving ground and staging yard tucked along the road just east of Kharanos. Amid clanking gears and spewing steam, Stonegear keeps watch for prospectors brave enough to pursue a volatile, rare ore known to ignite his tank's firepower to devastating new heights.

quest:468.text: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. Report to Mountaineer Rockgar is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers north from the guard posts of Loch Modan toward Dun Algaz. Mountaineer Kadrell dispatches capable travelers to join Rockgar, who is organizing a vital expedition into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the gateway passage connecting the dwarven homeland to northern territories. Dun Algaz represents the crucial artery between Loch Modan and the marshy expanses of the Wetlands. Built into the northern mountain ridge, the fortified pass has long guaranteed safe passage for trade, messengers, and military detachments moving between Ironforge and Alliance settlements further north. With tensions rising along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps a close watch on travellers passing through, recruiting hardy volunteers to reinforce the northern outposts.

quest:469.text: Daily Delivery. Daily Delivery is an errand on behalf of the dwarven hunter Einar Stonegrip, who asks travelers heading toward Menethil Harbor to deliver cured crocolisk hides to the local tanner. Rather than facing domestic friction at home, Einar relies on passing adventurers to keep his supply line moving. Out in the marshlands, Einar Stonegrip makes his living hunting the local wildlife, particularly the aggressive crocolisks that lurk along the waterways. While he gathers plenty of valuable skins, delivering them requires a trip home to Menethil Harbor. Reluctant to confront his wife Sida during a rough patch in their marriage, Einar prefers to stay in the field and hand his parcels off to passing travelers instead. The destination for these hides is James Halloran, a tanner operating within Menethil Harbor. Halloran relies on regular deliveries from local hunters to craft boots and cure leather for merchants and sailors passing through the port. Having noticed Einar's week-long absence, the tanner easily deduces the marital spat behind the proxy delivery, musing that his own wife might need to intervene and smooth things over with Sida.

quest:470.text: Digging Through the Ooze. While paying her regular respects at Ironbeard's Tomb, Sida was startled by the foul oozes prowling the barrows and threw her bag to distract them. Unable to face the creeping sludge again, she asks brave adventurers in Menethil Harbor to track down the creature that swallowed her belongings. Sida, a traveler residing in Menethil Harbor, regularly ventures northeast into the Wetlands to pay homage at Ironbeard's Tomb. On her latest visit, she found the ancient barrow crawling with foul, dripping oozes. Panicking at the sight of the shapeless horrors, she hurled her satchel at one of them. The creature simply engulfed the bag whole, though the distraction gave Sida just enough time to flee back to the safety of the port town. The burial site of the storied dwarven hero Ironbeard rests near the contested stronghold of Dun Modr. Despite its historical reverence, the surrounding marshland is prone to corruption, drawing amorphous acidic slimes that consume anything unfortunate enough to cross their path. Sida cannot remember which specific monstrosity swallowed her prized belongings, leaving travelers to scour the tomb grounds and carve through the creeping blight to recover her drenched satchel.

quest:471.text: Apprentice's Duties. Apprentice's Duties is an Alliance contract offered by tanner James Halloran in Menethil Harbor. After sending his young apprentice into the marshes only for the boy to be mauled by giant crocolisks, Halloran hires a capable adventurer to finish the dangerous harvesting job and settle the score. Tradesmen in frontier ports like Menethil Harbor must rely on local raw materials, but the surrounding bogs are unforgiving. James Halloran sent his young apprentice into the marshes to skin giant Wetlands crocolisks. When the youth failed to return, Halloran tracked him down and found him horribly mauled by the predatory beasts. Although the local midwife believes the apprentice will survive, the boy was maimed and lost a leg in the attack. Needing his stock replenished and seeking a measure of retribution against the beasts that tore into someone he considers like a son, Halloran enlists traveling adventurers to venture north along the coast, clear past the murloc hovels, and hunt down the giant crocolisks.

quest:472.text: Fall of Dun Modr. Dun Modr, the northern dwarf fortress overlooking the Thandol Span, has succumbed to a violent assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. A severely wounded survivor in Menethil Harbor seeks an Alliance adventurer to venture north and discover if commander Longbraid the Grim and any remnant of the garrison survived. Dun Modr has long anchored northern Khaz Modan, guarding the vital road and bridge connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands across the Thandol Span. Following an ambush at the bridge itself, the garrison scrambled back to regroup within the fortress walls. Before defensive lines could be reestablished, Dark Iron forces struck in overwhelming numbers, slaughtering the defenders and forcing a desperate evacuation. Harlo Barnaby, a young soldier among the defenders, fell gravely injured when a stray axe struck his back during the chaotic retreat. Believing his wounds fatal, Longbraid the Grim and the remaining troops strapped Barnaby to their last surviving horse and dispatched him south to Menethil Harbor. Barnaby survived the ordeal, but awoke in the harbor tavern racked by survivor's guilt, entirely unaware of whether any of his comrades made it out of the massacre alive.

quest:473.text: Report to Captain Stoutfist. Report to Captain Stoutfist is an Alliance military directive in Menethil Harbor. Following initial skirmishes against the Dragonmaw clan at Dun Algaz, Valstag Ironjaw sends proven combatants inside the harbor's keep to coordinate deeper defense efforts. Captain Stoutfist commands the local garrison and is organizing direct strikes against the entrenched orcs across the Wetlands. While dwarven mountaineers have long monitored the narrow mountain passes of Dun Algaz, the resurgence of the Dragonmaw clan cannot be contained to the borders of Loch Modan alone. Valstag Ironjaw recognizes that these orcs are pressing outward, establishing encampments and threatening the entirety of the marshlands. Securing the pass is merely the opening move in a larger campaign to safeguard the road to Ironforge. Deep inside Menethil Keep sits the war room, where Captain Stoutfist oversees the defenses of the Alliance port. Facing attacks from Dark Iron saboteurs, local beasts, and marsh murlocs, the captain relies on capable volunteers to counter external military threats. Valstag's recommendation confirms that you are hardened enough to take on direct orders against the Dragonmaw war machine.

quest:4736.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Across the sea, Alliance warlocks seek Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. From Strahad Farsan's tower above Ratchet, she teaches seasoned practitioners to craft tools and garments that strengthen their control of demons. Briarthorn sees when a warlock has moved beyond basic demonology and resisted corruption. He sends those pupils beyond Ironforge, across the sea to Kalimdor, instead of keeping them beneath the mountain. There, they can learn practical felcraft from an artisan with greater skill. Strahad Farsan keeps a solitary tower on the bluffs above Ratchet. Warlocks often set aside racial and political borders to survive in a world wary of dark magic. Menara Voidrender stays at Strahad's sanctuary and works with warlocks of every allegiance, helping them sharpen their craft and keep their summoned fiends bound.

quest:4737.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Zevrost sends warlocks from Orgrimmar to seek Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. He warns that fel magic leads to demonic enslavement, yet points them toward a mentor who can help fashion powerful arcane vestments. Warlocks gather beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, where their presence is tolerated uneasily. Zevrost, one of their bitter tutors, sneers at acolytes who seek mastery of the dark arts. He believes those who delve deeper into fel magic only hasten their own enslavement. In his view, demonic addiction will eventually overtake every practitioner, turning even the most disciplined scholar into a thrall of the Twisting Nether. Zevrost admits that other warlocks do not share his bleak view. Word has reached Orgrimmar of Menara Voidrender, a skilled warlock on the bluffs overlooking Ratchet, the neutral goblin port. Menara seeks promising disciples to help craft specialized implements for wielding their arcane might. For warlocks eager to advance their craft, her summons begins the forging of the legendary Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. Menara waits high above Ratchet, where the realities of warlock society are plain. Warlocks must set aside racial and cultural rivalries and support one another. The demons they bargain with show no prejudice and no mercy to anyone who falters. Sharing knowledge and crafting protective vestments comes from practical need, not noble charity: warlocks must survive the hostile entities they bind to their service.

quest:4738.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. An Alliance warlock seeking to craft powerful vestments is directed by the Mage Quarter's covert practitioners to seek out Menara Voidrender across the Great Sea. Stationed high above the neutral port of Ratchet, Menara trains dark spellcasters across faction divides in the dangerous arts of binding and artifact creation. Within the dark crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, warlock trainer Demisette Cloyce is known for her strict, unsparing standards. When an aspiring warlock reaches the threshold of weaving significant items of power, Demisette rarely believes they are truly ready. Nevertheless, higher authorities within the cabal mandate the student's advancement, dispatching them far from the safety of the capital to prove their mettle. The destination is the arid hills overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. There, Menara Voidrender maintains her laboratory in a stone tower. Isolated from the strict laws of Stormwind and the watchful eyes of Orgrimmar, Menara accepts apprentices regardless of race or political allegiance, knowing that the fiends and demonic entities warlocks contend with harbor equal malice toward every mortal soul.

quest:4739.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Menara Voidrender awaits Horde warlocks ready for deeper study in Ratchet. From the Undercity, they cross the Great Sea to her hilltop refuge above the port. Kaal Soulreaper watches warlocks grow more skilled in the Undercity. When one outgrows simple hexes and impish thralls, he sends them across the Great Sea for specialized instruction. Demonic control leaves little room for error. A skilled mentor can help a warlock survive the volatile powers of the Nether. Strahad Farsan’s tower rises from a high bluff above Ratchet. Away from the scrutiny of city guards, practitioners such as Menara Voidrender teach younger initiates. Warlocks from different backgrounds set aside tribal and political rivalries. The demons they bargain with will consume human, orc, or Forsaken alike if their summoner’s will falters.

quest:474.text: Defeat Nek'rosh. Defeat Nek'rosh marks the culmination of the Alliance campaign against the Dragonmaw clan in the Wetlands. With their siege engines sabotaged, adventurers are ordered to strike down Chieftain Nek'rosh directly to secure Menethil Harbor. Bringing his severed head back to Captain Stoutfist shatters the orcish threat to the coastal port. The Dragonmaw orcs have long plagued the marshlands of Khaz Modan, entrenched within their fortified encampments and threatening the sea lanes of Menethil Harbor. After discovering and burning the clan's catapults, the defenders of the marsh strike straight at the head of the serpent. Chieftain Nek'rosh, commander of the local warband, stands as the final obstacle to breaking the siege. His demise strips the remaining Dragonmaw raiders of their tactical coordination. Returning Nek'rosh's severed head to Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor marks an enormous victory for Ironforge's garrison. Deprived of both their heavy siege weaponry and their chieftain, the Dragonmaw are dealt a blow from which they are unlikely to quickly recover. For the beleaguered port, which serves as the Alliance's primary lifeline between Lordaeron and Khaz Modan, the chieftain's fall ensures the docks and trade vessels remain safe from sudden assault.

quest:4767.text: Wind Rider. Wind Rider is a Horde quest offered by Elu atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Aspiring to become a wind rider himself, Elu tasks adventurers with climbing into the craggy heights of Highperch to gather wild wyvern eggs to bolster the Horde's aerial mount reserves. Across Kalimdor, the Horde relies heavily on wind riders to ferry couriers, scouts, and warriors across vast distances. At Freewind Post, a young tauren named Elu aspires to join their esteemed ranks. With the demands of the expanding Horde outpacing the availability of mounts, Elu has been charged with helping procure new wyverns to supply the master wind riders, offering eager travelers a chance to assist in this vital effort. Highperch rises atop the towering mesas of Thousand Needles, serving as a prime nesting ground for wild wyverns. Gathering viable eggs requires braving the cliffs and facing the fiercely protective adults that patrol the roosts. By securing these clutches, Elu hopes to prove his dedication and begin the rigorous process of hand-raising and training wyverns for the Horde's flight masters.

quest:4770.text: Homeward Bound. Homeward Bound is a Horde quest that tasks adventurers with rescuing Pao'ka Swiftmountain, a young tauren naturalist stranded in the wyvern nesting grounds of Highperch. After getting separated and lost while studying the dangerous beasts, Pao'ka must be escorted safely down the cliffs back toward Whitereach Post. Pao'ka Swiftmountain accompanied the elder Motega Firemane to Thousand Needles to study the unique wildlife of the canyon floor and its towering stone pillars. Driven by curiosity and overconfidence, Pao'ka crept alone into the heights of Highperch to observe the local wyverns firsthand. The territorial beasts drove him off, leaving the young scholar stranded, terrified, and hiding among the crags for days. Highperch is thick with aggressive wyverns fiercely guarding their clutches and high roosts. Escorting Pao'ka back to level ground requires carving a path straight through the nesting predators. Unprepared for open combat, the panicked youth relies entirely on passing Horde travelers to fend off the swarming wyverns until he reaches the relative safety of the canyon path leading east.

quest:480.text: The Weaver. The Weaver is a strike mission assigned by Shadow Priest Allister in the Sepulcher to halt Dalaran's magical operations in Silverpine Forest. A Dalaran archmage, Ataeric, is directing efforts to reactivate a powerful ley energy node in the region. By slaying the archmage and claiming his staff, the Forsaken disrupt Dalaran's occult ambitions and secure their grip on the surrounding lands. Following preliminary investigations into Ambermill and Dalaran's movements in Silverpine Forest, the Forsaken learned of a hazardous development: the wizards are attempting to harness and reactivate a dormant ley energy node. Left unchecked, access to such concentrated arcane power would allow Dalaran to fortify their position and threaten the Undercity's dominion over the southern reaches of Lordaeron.

quest:4821.text: Alien Egg. Rumors among the tauren of Freewind Post speak of a bizarre, foreign egg guarded fiercely by wild serpents on the canyon floor. Hagar Lightninghoof tasks Horde adventurers with tracking down and retrieving the specimen before whatever lurks inside breaks free. Word reached Freewind Post of an unusual egg spotted deep in the serpent dens that dot the canyon floor beneath the towering stone needles. The serpents native to the canyon watch over the egg as though it were their own brood, striking out at any traveler who ventures too close. Intrigued and wary of what might threaten the local hunting grounds, Hagar Lightninghoof asks brave scouts to locate the clutch, bypass the slithering sentries, and secure the oddity for study.

quest:484.text: Young Crocolisk Skins. James Halloran, a prominent tanner based in Menethil Harbor, contracts travelers to supply fresh skins from the marsh's juvenile crocolisks. His cured hides enjoy international maritime demand, making reliable hunting essential to his trade. Supplying these softer materials earns his trust and opens the way to further leatherworking chores. Menethil Harbor is an essential maritime hub connecting the Eastern Kingdoms to distant continents, but it also supports a bustling local economy built around the resources of the surrounding marshland. James Halloran has established an international trade by tanning and curing the tough hides of the region's abundant reptilian predators. Merchants and ships sailing out of Menethil carry Halloran's leather goods to distant ports, creating constant pressure on his workshop to maintain a steady inventory. While veteran trappers like Einar provide regular hauls of mature hides, tanning specialized luxury goods requires far softer leather than fully grown marsh crocolisks can yield. To fill this shortage, Halloran relies on passing adventurers to wade into the shallow bogs right outside Menethil's palisades. Sourcing intact skins from juvenile beasts requires careful hunting, ensuring the hides remain intact enough to endure Halloran's meticulous curing process.

quest:4841.text: Pacify The Centaur. Pacify the Centaur is a retaliatory hunting mission issued by Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post. Charged with clearing the threat gathering beneath the canyon spires, Horde adventurers strike deep into the Galak centaur encampments of Splithoof Crag. Perched upon its precarious desert mesa, Freewind Post grants the tauren a commanding vantage over the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. However, that high ground offers little peace when hostile enemies mass directly beneath the ropes and elevators. The Galak centaur have established a sprawling war camp nestled directly north along the canyon wall at Splithoof Crag, directly menacing supply lines and tauren movement through the needles. To counter the growing danger, Cliffwatcher Longhorn sends capable Horde travelers to thin the Galak ranks through unsparing violence. Rather than merely defending the access lifts, the tauren believe the only way to safeguard Freewind Post is to break the centaur vanguard in their own camp. Taking down their scouts, beast-wranglers, and windchaser mystics is meant to blunt any concerted assault on the post before it can begin.

quest:4865.text: Serpent Wild. Serpent Wild is a Horde quest in Thousand Needles that connects the discovery of strange alien eggs to ancient tauren legends. Following an unsettling revelation at Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof dispatches adventurers northwest to Motega Firemane at Whitereach Post to confront the awakening of Arikara. When strange, unnatural eggs began appearing in Thousand Needles, local tauren feared an ecological disaster. However, inspecting the artifacts reveals something far older and more ominous than ordinary predators: signs pointing to the vengeance spirit Arikara. Stunned by the horrifying confirmation, Hagar Lightninghoof realizes the canyon faces a mythical threat long thought relegated to fireside lore. Recognizing that the threat surpasses simple physical defense, Hagar urges immediate council with Motega Firemane. Stationed northwest along the canyon floor at Whitereach Post, Motega serves as a watcher and spiritual guide versed in the traditional omens of the Needles. His guidance is essential if the Horde hopes to understand and appease or destroy the rising vengeance spirit.

quest:4881.text: Assassination Plot. Assassination Plot is a Horde quest initiated by recovering intercepted centaur orders in Thousand Needles. The orders reveal an impending strike targeting the tauren Kanati Greycloud at his hunting camp by Whitereach Post. Thousand Needles has long been contested terrain dominated by warring centaur clans and dangerous wildlife. When the tauren brave Kanati Greycloud set up a hunting camp at Whitereach Post, the small post southwest of the Great Lift, the local centaur viewed it as an audacious intrusion into their territory. Rather than merely driving game away, the centaur resolved to eliminate Greycloud entirely to discourage any further Horde expansion through the canyon.

quest:490.text: Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg. Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg is an Alliance quest authorized by the Sentinels to curb the aggressive furbolg population corrupting Teldrassil. Shayla Nightbreeze recruits adventurers outside Darnassus to hunt the corrupted beasts and collect their fangs as proof of deed. On the road outside Darnassus, Shayla Nightbreeze acts on direct orders from the Sentinels to place a bounty on the Gnarlpine furbolg. Once peaceful inhabitants of the ancient forests, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading corruption that stripped away their reason, turning them into vicious threats to the safety of travelers and the natural sanctity of Teldrassil. To curb the Gnarlpine aggression, hunters are dispatched across the boughs of the World Tree to cull their ranks and collect their fangs as proof. The bulk of their corrupted population resides in two major strongholds: Ban'ethil Hollow, set south of the road west of Dolanaar, and the ruins of Starbreeze Village toward the east.

quest:4904.text: Free At Last. Free at Last is a rescue mission atop the windswept spires of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Lakota Windsong, a tauren woman held captive by Arnak Grimtotem, needs protection as she flees her captor's stronghold and returns to her friend Thalia Amberhide at Freewind Post. The Grimtotem clan's aggressive presence in Thousand Needles is not limited to skirmishes over land. Arnak Grimtotem sought to take Lakota Windsong as his bride, but when she refused his advances, he chose violence. Arnak returned in the night, struck down Lakota's brother when he tried to defend her, and dragged her away to Darkcloud Pinnacle. Perched across the high wooden suspension bridges above Thousand Needles, Darkcloud Pinnacle is swarming with hostile Grimtotem warriors. Escorting Lakota requires navigating the descent while fighting off waves of Grimtotem bandits intent on recapturing her before she reaches the canyon floor. Once safely down from the pinnacle, Lakota makes her way back to the safety of Freewind Post. Her companion, Thalia Amberhide, receives the news with immense relief but deep mourning for Lakota's fallen brother, offering his remaining belongings as a token of gratitude to those who brought her home alive.

quest:493.text: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills is a Horde courier task connecting the Forsaken research efforts in Silverpine Forest with their outpost in Tarren Mill. Entrusted with sensitive notes from Apothecary Renferrel, the traveler journeys south into the disputed Hillsbrad Foothills to deliver vital biological research to Apothecary Lydon. This dispatch reflects the intense pressure Lady Sylvanas Windrunner places upon the Royal Apothecary Society to produce a weapon of mass devastation. Since breaking free from the Lich King's iron grip, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has harbored a single-minded ambition: the development of a New Plague engineered to eradicate both living enemies and the Scourge. To achieve this, the Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from the Banshee Queen. Because distance isolates their laboratories, researchers scattered across Lordaeron must continuously share raw chemical data and test findings to accelerate their sinister breakthrough. Apothecary Renferrel, operating out of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, directs couriers to deliver his recent findings to his colleague, Apothecary Lydon. The trek winds south through the shadowed pine woods and down into the open, rolling pastures of Hillsbrad Foothills. There, nestled beneath the Alterac Mountains, lies Tarren Mill—a vital Forsaken hub and laboratory staging ground.

quest:494.text: Time to Strike. "Time to Strike" is a Horde reconnaissance mission that transitions scouts across the Hillsbrad Foothills border to the military hub of Tarren Mill. Delivering Deathstalker Lesh's coded signal to High Executor Darthalia marks the transition from quiet surveillance to coordinated offensive operations against the local human populace. Perched along the high ground near the border between Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the movements of human settlers and militia in the valley below. The Deathstalkers operate as the eyes and ears of the Undercity, surveying enemy settlements before any military deployment. Rather than risk abandoning her watchpost, Lesh entrusts passing Horde travelers to relay her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

quest:496.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon pursues the Royal Apothecary Society's grim mandate to engineer lethal concoctions against the living. To advance his morbid experiments, he enlists travelers to harvest animal reagents from the surrounding foothills. While Tarren Mill serves as a military stronghold for the Forsaken in the Hillsbrad Foothills, it also functions as an active research station for the Royal Apothecary Society. Stationed amidst the scenic greenery, Apothecary Lydon despises the pristine countryside and yearns to see the human settlements poisoned and conquered. To manufacture his experimental 'Elixir of Suffering', he requires local biological agents known for their potency and virulence. Developing alchemical plagues demands precise ingredients. Lydon directs hunters into the wilds surrounding Tarren Mill to collect the tongues of native Gray Bears alongside rare ichor secreted by Moss Creepers. Once refined through unholy alchemy, these organic fluids form the foundation for a lethal mixture intended to eradicate living trespassers across Hillsbrad.

quest:4966.text: Protect Kanati Greycloud. Protect Kanati Greycloud is a Horde quest at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Warned that centaur assassins have targeted the tauren Kanati Greycloud, adventurers must make a stand beside him and repel a squad of Galak assassins. While stationed among the towering sandstone spires of Whitereach Post, the tauren Kanati Greycloud learns from intercepted centaur orders of an assassination plot directed squarely at his life. The Galak tribe of centaur, relentless in their hostility toward the nomadic tauren and their Horde allies, are not content merely raiding supply paths; they seek to eliminate those who settle in their canyons. Realizing the attack is imminent and suspecting the enemy forces might outnumber his initial estimates, Kanati asks travelers at the post to fight alongside him. When the Galak assassins strike, Kanati stands his ground, relying on allied blades and spells to break the ambush before the centaur can claim their prize.

quest:499.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon brews a venomous concoction intended to further the Royal Apothecary Society's sinister work. To confirm its lethality, he orders an immediate live trial on his unfortunate companion nearby. Apothecary Lydon works tirelessly out of Tarren Mill to develop chemical weapons capable of fulfilling the Dark Lady's grand ambitions: a blight that will annihilate both the living humans of the Alliance and the undead horrors of the Scourge. Once the necessary reagents are gathered and steeped, Lydon mixes the foul brew into what he dubs the Elixir of Suffering, eager to witness its raw potency before deploying it on a broader scale.

quest:5.text: Jitters' Growling Gut. Stranded and terrified in the ruins of Raven Hill, the paranoid vagrant Jitters is desperate for real sustenance after subsisting on weeds and insects. He begs passing adventurers to travel east to Darkshire and convince Chef Grual to prepare a hot batch of his famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill has become a den of ravenous undead and lurking beasts, leaving the eccentric hermit Jitters trapped in hiding for weeks. Prowling through dilapidated shanties under perpetual gloom, he has survived solely on dirt-dwelling grubs and wild weeds. Starved of civilized comfort, his nerves and stomach are pushed to their absolute limits. Desperate for any reminder of safety, Jitters dreams of the seasoned patties crafted at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He sends travelers across the haunted road to seek out Chef Grual, hoping Grual will agree to whip up a batch of Dusky Crab Cakes to quiet his violently growling gut.

quest:501.text: Elixir of Pain. Commissioned by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, this assignment tasks Horde adventurers with harvesting mountain lion blood to brew a lethal new concoction. It highlights the Royal Apothecary Society's grim dedication to perfecting their New Plague while despising the natural vitality of the Hillsbrad Foothills. While stationed inside Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon finds little joy in the surrounding landscape. Looking out past his window at the blooming meadows and brisk mountain air of Hillsbrad, he views the region's enduring life as an offense. Like many within the Royal Apothecary Society, his personal devotion is bound to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the perfection of the New Plague, an engineered scourge intended to bring death to the living and retribution to their enemies. To engineer his latest poisonous mixture, Lydon turns to the local fauna prowling the foothills and the slopes toward the Alterac Mountains. Believing that mountain lion blood possesses specific properties vital for crafting what he calls an Elixir of Pain, he sends agents into the wilds to claim ten vials. The collection serves as the foundation for the Society's ongoing chemical trials along the contested southern front.

quest:502.text: Elixir of Pain. Commissioned by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, this quest tasks Horde agents with testing a newly brewed biological concoction known as the Elixir of Pain. The Forsaken apothecary selects Stanley, a pet dog belonging to Farmer Ray in the Hillsbrad Fields, as an unsuspecting test subject. Operating out of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon conducts experiments on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Utilizing fresh blood gathered from the local wildlife, Lydon concocts a volatile mixture he dubs the Elixir of Pain. Rather than relying purely on theoretical alchemy, the society requires empirical field data to observe the physiological effects of their experimental poisons and mutagens. To evaluate the draught without alarming the human defenders of Hillsbrad, Lydon directs his agents to target the northern farm in Hillsbrad Fields. There lives Stanley, a seemingly harmless pet dog kept by Farmer Ray. Approaching the unsuspecting canine with the draft poured into an open hand, the agent administers the dose under the guise of an ordinary treat.

quest:503.text: Gol'dir. Krusk has gone through the documents you procured and concludes that Gol'dir is kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Gol'dir has languished in captivity far too long and needs to be freed. Krusk, in Tarren Mill, has gone through the documents you brought back after Infiltration. They point to Gol'dir being kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Krusk says the captivity has dragged on far too long and Gol'dir needs to be freed. Gol'dir is held in the top room of the inn at Strahnbrad, and the inn is packed with Syndicate. A Rusted Iron Key opens the lock, and Jailor Borhuin carries it; Borhuin may be in any building of the town.

quest:5042.text: Agamaggan's Strength. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde travelers Agamaggan's Strength in return for Blood Shards. The captive Razormane shaman draws on his people's reverence for the ancient boar demigod and his hatred of the rival Bristleback tribe. The quilboar honor Agamaggan, an ancient boar demigod whose spilled blood is said to have formed the red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. They treat the crystals as sacred, drawing on their power to strengthen their front-line fighters. Mangletooth, an elder Razormane shaman held captive in Camp Taurajo, offers this strength to Horde champions. He claims your foes will cower as they do before the Razormane's mightiest champions. Mangletooth offers his strength out of spite. The orcs and tauren captured and caged the old quilboar, whose Razormane tribe is at war with the rival Bristleback. Unable to break his chains and slaughter them himself, he trades Agamaggan's gifts for help against them. He rewards those who destroy Bristleback tribes and take the sacred Blood Shards from their lands.

quest:5043.text: Agamaggan's Agility. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a blood shard ritual. The captive quilboar channels the power of his ancient boar god, blessing those who bring him shards from the Barrens with swift movement and sure aim. Crimson blood shards jut from the Barrens soil, especially near quilboar encampments and colossal brambles. Quilboar tradition says the crystals formed from Agamaggan's spilled blood. The Great Boar Ancient fell fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Even locked in a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo, the elder quilboar Mangletooth knows how to channel the stones' dormant divine power for anyone who brings them. Quilboar hunters and scouts prize ruthless accuracy and blinding quickness in the scrublands. For four blood shards, Mangletooth calls on the fallen demi-god's latent energy, lending the petitioner the instincts and supple grace of his people's best stalkers. He grunts with disdain at outsiders, yet honors his pact and weaves Agamaggan's power into a temporary mantle of agility.

quest:5044.text: Wisdom of Agamaggan. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth trades the wisdom of Agamaggan for blood shards. The captive quilboar offers Horde spellcasters a ritual drawn from the ancient boar god’s power. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth is held prisoner by the Horde. The quilboar trades his people’s magical secrets for blood shards, crimson crystals said to have formed from Agamaggan’s spilled blood. The towering boar Demigod died in the War of the Ancients. Mangletooth says the geomancers and shaman of his tribes use the shards to channel divine power in their rituals. Other shard offerings bring physical resilience or swiftness. Mangletooth’s Wisdom ritual instead sharpens intellect and arcane ability. For four blood shards, he calls on Agamaggan’s spirit to grant you cunning in your confrontations, then reminds you of your mortality.

quest:5045.text: Rising Spirit. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers a ritual blessing drawn from Agamaggan's ancient power. Bring blood shards taken from his Bristleback rivals, and he strengthens your will and spirit. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth knows the geomancy and ancestral magic of the quilboar. He takes pride in his people's devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. To Mangletooth, an unbroken spirit carries a warrior onward when strength fails and defeat seems near. Mangletooth asks for blood shards to raise your spirit. These crystals hold Agamaggan's ancient blood, which seeped into the red earth ten thousand years ago. Bring him shards gathered across the Barrens, especially from his Bristleback enemies, and he can channel their power into a blessing that bolsters your will.

quest:5046.text: Razorhide. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Razorhide to those who bring him blood shards. The captive quilboar trades Agamaggan’s life essence for a blessing that hardens the skin before battle. The quilboar trace their power to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who died fighting the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood sank into the Barrens and hardened into crystalline shards, still alive with ancient power. The Horde and quilboar remain sworn enemies, yet Mangletooth, held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, will share sacred knowledge for these fragments. Quilboar are born with thick hides and protective quills, but their warriors call on Agamaggan to harden their skin against blades and claws. Mangletooth can perform the rite for outsiders, channeling four blood shards to strengthen their defenses and help keep their bones unbroken in the wilds.

quest:5052.text: Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Across the Barrens, blood shards carry the power of the fallen boar god Agamaggan. Quilboar say his blood sank into the earth and hardened into red stones. At Camp Taurajo, the captive Mangletooth trades their power to the Horde for his own reasons. Quilboar lore tells how Agamaggan fell ten thousand years ago in the War of the Ancients. His blood raised giant thorn mazes across the plains, then sank beneath the soil and seeped into minerals. In time, it hardened into blood-red stones. The quilboar honor the shards as sacred remnants of their creator. They gather them from mineral seams and holy grounds, then use them as totems for battle and sorcery. Mangletooth is held in a cage at Camp Taurajo by the tauren. He bears a bitter grudge against his own kind, saying his tribe betrayed and cast him out. Without freedom or the magic of his people, he bargains with adventurers for blood shards. Their power lets him reach Agamaggan's magic despite his captivity and channel it to Horde champions. He takes pleasure in turning that power against the quilboar who rejected him. Mangletooth speaks with reverence of Razorfen, the quilboar's holiest sanctuary to the south. The tribes say the vast briars of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs grew from Agamaggan's colossal skeleton and tusks. They believe Razorfen Downs lies within the demigod's gaping maw, a holy threshold that devours and crushes any who enter without the Boar God's favor.

quest:506.text: Blackmoore's Legacy. Gol'dir, freed from the Syndicate, has information for Krusk in Tarren Mill. The Syndicate's leader, Aliden Perenolde, visited Gol'dir and spoke of making slaves of the orcs who stand against him, and brought a girl named Elysa who wore the pendant the Warchief desires. A day or two ago, the head of the Syndicate paid Gol'dir a visit. His name was Aliden Perenolde, and he styled himself lord of the land. He confided that he meant to enslave the orcs who resisted him, just as his father and the despised Blackmoore, his mentor, once planned. Gol'dir sends you to bring this to Krusk in Tarren Mill, and will make his own way after settling his business where he is. More important, Perenolde brought his mistress, a slight girl named Elysa. Around her neck hung the pendant the Warchief desires.

quest:5062.text: Sacred Fire. Sacred Fire is a Horde rite of passage that bridges the jagged canyons of Thousand Needles with the heights of Thunder Bluff. To summon and banish the vengeful wind serpent Arikara, hunters must gather rare Incendia Agave from the Boiling Pool so that Magatha Grimtotem can enchant it into ritual powder. The monstrous wind serpent Arikara cannot simply be tracked across the canyon floor; she must be called. Motega Firemane instructs hunters to prepare the sacred fire of life, an ancient ritual flame that acts as a beacon to the spirit beast. Feeding this fire requires more than ordinary kindling, calling for the rare Incendia Agave that sprouts only around the scalding waters of Thousand Needles. Incendia Agave thrives near the Boiling Pool, a geothermally heated lake tucked below Darkcloud Pinnacle. Harvesting the spiky succulent requires braving the blistering waters and the volatile steam elementals that drift through the mists. Many bushels grow submerged beneath the surface, demanding resilience from any hunter sent to gather them.

quest:5064.text: Grimtotem Spying. Cliffwatcher Longhorn tasks Horde champions with infiltrating Darkcloud Pinnacle to discover what the elusive Grimtotem clan is plotting. Three unknown couriers were spotted visiting the mesa, leaving guarded correspondence scattered across their mountaintop village. Uncovering these secret notes exposes a brewing scheme that threatens the tauren settlements of Thousand Needles. Freewind Post sits precariously on high spires, but its defenders must constantly look over their shoulders at their hostile cousins. The Grimtotem clan has long maintained a tense, resentful stance toward the Horde, clinging to their isolationist strongholds atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn noticed a shift in their behavior when three mysterious agents arrived over successive weeks, conferring with clan leadership in secret. Longhorn suspects these emissaries carried marching orders or alliances meant to undermine Thunder Bluff's presence in the canyon. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified network of sheer mesas connected by wooden rope bridges. Penetrating the village requires braving dense patrols of hostile Grimtotem warriors and shamans. Longhorn's scouts confirmed that the mysterious messages were locked away in separate chests spread across the outpost's central dwellings and outer bluffs. Securing the three secret notes requires sneaking or fighting across the entire settlement to snatch the clan's private communications from under their watchful eyes.

quest:5088.text: Arikara. "Arikara" is the culmination of an ominous task given by Magatha Grimtotem in Thunder Bluff. Warning that an ancient wind serpent may be stalking High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the elder shaman sends Horde adventurers to summon and slay the beast upon the burial spires of Thousand Needles. After securing refined Incendia powder, Magatha Grimtotem enchants the reagent to serve as a summoning catalyst. She warns that ancient tauren traditions have shifted too rapidly under the new Horde alliance, provoking the vengeance of Arikara, a ferocious wind serpent spirit. Magatha directs heroes southward into the windswept canyon of Thousand Needles, instructing them to throw the powder onto a ritual pyre situated among the elevated burial sites of Darkcloud Pinnacle.

quest:509.text: Elixir of Agony. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon enlists Horde adventurers to gather toxic fungi from an overrun farmstead in Hillsbrad Foothills. These virulent Mudsnout Blossoms serve as vital raw material for the Royal Apothecary Society's grim chemical experimentation. The resulting concoction is meant to aid Lady Sylvanas's long-term design to eradicate both the living and the Scourge. While the Scourge ravages the north and the Alliance clings to towns like Southshore, the Forsaken pursue their own calculated solution: the development of a tailored, lethal plague. Operating out of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon labors under the mandate of the Dark Lady. Though personally cynical about the tedious toil of alchemy, Lydon diligently gathers potent organic toxins from the surrounding countryside to brew elixirs capable of speeding along the mutual destruction of Sylvanas's enemies. South of Tarren Mill and east of the river lies Nethander Stead, an abandoned human farmstead now overrun by the vicious Mudsnout gnolls. Amid the filth and neglected soil, strange and foul-smelling mushrooms known as Mudsnout Blossoms flourish. These large, pungent growths hold concentrated organic poisons prized by the Royal Apothecary Society. Procuring them requires cutting through gnoll packs or quietly weaving past their ramshackle camps.

quest:513.text: Elixir of Agony. This errand carries Apothecary Lydon's freshly mashed Mudsnout Composite from Tarren Mill straight to the heart of the Royal Apothecary Society in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell requires the plant mash to treat it with a colloid of decay, furthering the Forsaken's development of a new plague. In the ongoing efforts of the Royal Apothecary Society, regional researchers frequently send their raw discoveries back to Undercity for specialized refinement. Apothecary Lydon has mashed down local Mudsnout Blossoms into a composite, but bringing it to lethal fruition requires the advanced reagents kept only in the capital's laboratory. Master Apothecary Faranell works under tremendous pressure within the Apothecarium. Caught between the ever-present shadow of the Scourge in the north and aggressive human populations to the south, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has demanded a potent new plague to defend their people. Receiving Lydon's composite provides Faranell with exactly the kind of toxic breakthrough the Dark Lady expects.

quest:5147.text: Wanted - Arnak Grimtotem. Wanted: Arnak Grimtotem is a Horde bounty posted at Freewind Post demanding the execution of a violent Grimtotem exile. Arnak is targeted by the local authorities for murder and kidnapping on the mesas above the canyon. While tensions between the mainstream tauren of the Horde and the reclusive Grimtotem tribe are perpetually strained, Arnak took matters far beyond political friction. Branded an outcast, Arnak murdered a tauren and abducted the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong. In response to these heinous acts, Cliffwatcher Longhorn of Freewind Post sanctioned an open bounty calling for the rogue tauren's death. Arnak took refuge upon the high crags of Darkcloud Pinnacle, an extensive network of rope bridges and mesa encampments occupied by the Grimtotem clan near the entrance to Razorfen Downs. Trapped upon these windswept heights alongside Arnak is his captive, Lakota Windsong, awaiting rescue from anyone brave enough to fight across the Grimtotem bridges.

quest:515.text: Elixir of Agony. This errand continues the development of the Royal Apothecary Society's new plague, dispatching a courier from Undercity back to Tarren Mill. Master Apothecary Faranell enriches Lydon's Mudsnout mixture with his own decaying compounds, demanding coastal reagents and alchemical draughts to catalyze the lethal brew. When Apothecary Lydon's field work produced a potent composite from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered at gnoll-held Nethander Stead, he sent it straight to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell, head of the Royal Apothecary Society, immediately recognized the concoction's grim potential. Delighted by its toxic properties, Faranell added his own specialized colloid of decay to the mixture before outlining the catalysts required to weaponize it fully. Activating the volatile contaminating agents requires precise reagents that Lydon must assemble in Tarren Mill. In addition to a restorative draught of Strong Troll's Blood to feed and stabilize the chemical reaction, Faranell requires organic components harvested from the southern shoreline of Hillsbrad: scales stripped from the serpentine Daggerspine naga and eyes carved from the coastal Torn Fin murlocs.

quest:5151.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Following a deadly centaur ambush on a merchant caravan in Thousand Needles, the goblin tinkerer Wizlo Bearingshiner was left as the sole survivor. Desperate to reclaim his prized invention, he hires adventurers to breach the wreckage, unlock an iron cage, and wrest the gizmo from the neck of a fearsome caged predator. Caravans venturing beneath the towering sandstone spires of Thousand Needles run a perilous gauntlet. Hostile centaur prowl the canyon floor, fiercely guarding their territory and raiding any travelers bold enough to pass through. When one such trade caravan was overrun just north of Whitereach Post, the centaur slaughtered the travelers and plundered the wagons, leaving only the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner to limp back to safety. In the chaos of the raid, the centaur looted nearly every valuable scrap, but they gave one ruined wagon a wide berth. Bound inside a sturdy transport cage was a ferocious, enraged panther with Wizlo's prized hypercapacitor gizmo fastened directly around its neck. Daunted by the predator's snarling fury, the centaur abandoned the cage intact, forcing Wizlo to entrust its key to brave mercenaries capable of slaying the beast and reclaiming his gadget.
