Culling lesser harpies along the edge of the Charred Vale provides only temporary relief for Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder believes that the only lasting way to curb their aggression is to eliminate their matriarch, Bloodfury Ripper. Revering her as something akin to a queen, the flock draws its ruthless coordination and boldness directly from her leadership along the craggy western ridge. Once Bloodfury Ripper falls and her remains are presented as proof, the immediate threat to the retreat subsides. With their brood queen destroyed, the disorganized harpies become far easier to keep at bay. The victory also lifts a spiritual burden from Maggran himself, freeing his thoughts from bitter vigilance so he can return to the customary tauren pursuit of harmony and balance.

quest:6284.text: Arachnophobia. Arachnophobia is a Horde bounty quest targeting Besseleth, an ancient and colossal predator haunting southern Stonetalon Mountains. Posted on a roadside notice near Windshear Crag, the bounty directs adventurers into Sishir Canyon to claim the spider matriarch's fang for Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat. Putting an end to her reign makes the mountain roads safer for night travelers. Travelers along the main thoroughfare south of Windshear Crag will spot a weathered wanted poster warning of the dangers to the west. Sishir Canyon and Webwinder Path have been completely overrun by eight-legged predators. At the heart of this webbed menace sits Besseleth, an unusually large, orange-hued spider who commands her brood and ambushes anyone daring to stray off the path after sunset. The bounty on Besseleth is offered by Maggran Earthbinder, a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran has a personal score to settle with the matriarch: during a previous encounter, he was nearly killed when struck by Besseleth's massive two-foot fang. Though he managed to fight her off and limp to safety, the lingering wound serves as a constant reminder of the danger lurking in the canyon shadows. By having an adventurer claim Besseleth's Fang, Maggran hopes to secure the passes so trade and travel to Sun Rock Retreat can flourish without fear.

quest:629.text: The Vile Reef. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp seeks a piece of an ancient stone tablet resting deep beneath the Savage Coast. The sunken city, known as the Vile Reef, is infested with aggressive murlocs and holds the legendary history of Gri'lek, which the Darkspear tribe wishes to preserve in Orgrimmar. Northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp, an ancient troll city slipped beneath the waters along the Savage Coast when a violent earthquake shattered the land long ago. Now referred to as the Vile Reef, its flooded ruins crawl with hostile murlocs that assault anyone venturing near. Resting on the sea floor among the ruins is a massive stone tablet carved with the story of Gri'lek, a legendary troll hero whose memory remains sacred to the Darkspear. Because the full monument is far too massive to carry away from the depths, Kin'weelay asks you to break off a shard from the stone. He intends to carry this fragment back to Orgrimmar, enshrining it in a sacred place so the Darkspear will never forget the strength and honor of Gri'lek.

quest:63.text: Call of Water. Across the sea, Call of Water carries Barrens shamans to Silverpine Forest. There, an initiate faces the blight on an ancient coastal shrine to earn communion with water spirits. After gathering drops of pure water with help from the hermit Brine, you return to Islen Waterseer on the Barrens coast. She sends you across the sea with the purified essence to Silverpine Forest's haunted shore, just west of the Forsaken refuge called the Sepulcher.

quest:6301.text: Cycle of Rebirth. Cycle of Rebirth is a Horde task assigned by Tammra Windfield at Sun Rock Retreat to gather rare Gaea seeds from the shores of Mirkfallon Lake. Distressed by the toll of industrial greed and ongoing warfare across Stonetalon, Tammra seeks to bless these resilient kernels with shamanic power to revive the mountain's ravaged soil. It forms the essential first step in a restoration effort aimed at healing the scarred wilderness. The peaks of Stonetalon bear deep wounds from both commercial exploitation and relentless regional conflict. Between aggressive logging operations and clashes between rival factions, entire swaths of forest have been scorched, clear-cut, or reduced to ash. For the tauren stationed at Sun Rock Retreat, witnessing this rapid destruction of the natural world is a grievous wound. Rather than merely fighting to hold ground, shamans like Tammra Windfield look toward the ancient natural order, striving to enact the Earthmother's restorative cycle. Restoring life to barren ground demands extraordinary vitality, which Tammra finds in the rare Gaea seeds found around Mirkfallon Lake. Situated to the north of Sun Rock Retreat, the lake's banks nurture these sturdy seed pods along the water's edge. Though the surrounding region is steeped in danger, these seeds hold an innate resilience unique to Stonetalon. Once retrieved, Tammra channels ancestral shamanistic blessings into each kernel, awakening their latent power to accelerate their growth for the work ahead.

quest:631.text: The Thandol Span. Following a devastating explosion that rocked northern Wetlands, Rhag Garmason asks travelers to search the ruined bridges of the Thandol Span for a missing dwarf scout. The Dark Iron clan has launched a brutal assault against Dun Modr, cutting off communication and leaving local defenders stranded without reinforcements. Finding Ol' Rustlocke is the first step toward uncovering the full scale of the sabotage. A catastrophic blast recently tore through the Thandol Span, shattering the massive stone bridge connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands. Bronzebeard soldiers stationed at the border were caught in the devastation as Dark Iron dwarves ambushed Dun Modr. With their ranks thinned and their strongholds besieged, the survivors under Longbraid the Grim have been forced into a desperate defensive holdout against the attackers. Hoping to salvage a crossing and determine whether any path northward remains usable, Longbraid dispatched the veteran scout Ebenezer Rustlocke to inspect the eastern span. Days passed without a single report, but with Dun Modr actively under siege, Rhag Garmason and the garrison lack the soldiers to launch a rescue expedition into enemy-controlled rubble.

quest:633.text: The Thandol Span. This critical Alliance mission tasks champions with defending the sole surviving bridge across the Thandol Span. Following the tragic murder of Ebenezer Rustlocke, Rhag Garmason discovers a plot by the traitorous Kam Deepfury to detonate hidden explosives and sever Ironforge's vital connection to the north. After discovering the grim fate of Ebenezer Rustlocke within the Thandol Span's substructure, a recovered document brings darker intentions to light. The Dark Iron agitator Kam Deepfury, architect of the bridge's initial destruction, was not finished. Having already collapsed one of the grand stone crossings, his sabotage network planted a second cache of heavy munitions just across the northern border in the Arathi Highlands, poised to finish the job.

quest:634.text: Plea To The Alliance. Plea to the Alliance carries a desperate request for reinforcements from the surviving dwarven defenders of Dun Modr across the Thandol Span into Arathi. Faced with the slaughter of their garrison by Dark Iron infiltrators, the dwarves seek aid from the human forces stationed at Refuge Pointe, only to find the Alliance stretched beyond its limits. Following the devastation of Dun Modr and the sabotage of the Thandol Span by Dark Iron dwarves, the dwarven survivors hold a precarious foothold at the northern rim of the Wetlands. With Ironforge's main reserves yet to arrive, Rhag Garmason and Longbraid the Grim look north toward the Arathi Highlands. Learning of an Alliance encampment established at Refuge Pointe, Garmason dispatches an emissary across the shattered bridge to appeal to Captain Nials for urgent military aid. Upon reaching Refuge Pointe, the grim reality of the northern Alliance becomes apparent. Captain Nials offers heartfelt sympathies to Longbraid's soldiers, but he cannot spare a single fighter. Stromgarde itself has fallen into ruin, overwhelmed by Syndicate rogues, Boulderfist ogres, and Witherbark trolls. The surviving Stromgarde defenders are entirely committed to reclaiming their ancestral capital. Bound by honor and desperate circumstances of their own, Nials is forced to send word back that the dwarves at the Span must stand alone.

quest:635.text: Crystal in the Mountains. The Pendant of Myzrael pulses in your hand and a pleading reaches you, as if someone desperately needs help. A vision shows a gleaming crystal rising out of the ground in the northern mountains of Arathi, and you feel drawn to that place. The pendant pulses as you hold it. From it comes a sense of pleading, as if someone is trying to reach you and badly needs your help. Then a vision opens before you: the mountains in the north of Arathi, and a gleaming crystal thrusting up out of the ground. You feel drawn to that place.

quest:637.text: Sully Balloo's Letter. Recovered from a drowned skeleton beneath the shattered arches of the Thandol Span, this waterlogged letter contains the dying words of a dwarven soldier named Sully Balloo. Addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge, it carries the final thoughts of a defender lost beneath the icy river waters during the battles for the bridge. Beneath the massive stone pilings supporting the Thandol Span—the crucial land bridge linking the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands—rests the drowned skeleton of a fallen dwarf. Still clutched in his skeletal grasp is a water-damaged envelope that barely survives handling. Written with painstaking care amid the fires of battle, the pages open with the tender phrase, 'My dear Sara...', preserving the soldier's voice long after the tides claimed him. The Thandol Span has seen fierce fighting between Alliance forces and their enemies, from Dark Iron saboteurs to marauding warbands contesting the borderlands. Sully Balloo was one of the many dwarven soldiers sent north to defend the vital thoroughfare. When he perished beneath the waves, his fate remained unknown to his family in the mountains until a diver finally retrieved his farewell testament.

quest:638.text: Trollbane. Vol'jin has ordered the Darkspear trolls to recover the ancient sword Trol'kalar from the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. With King Thoras Trollbane fallen, the blade is meant to serve the Horde in future conflicts against the trolls of Zul'Gurub. Following the death of King Thoras Trollbane and the collapse of Stromgarde into ruin, Chieftain Vol'jin has ordered that every effort be made to spirit Trol'kalar away. This storied blade has long rested in human hands, but the Darkspear tribe hopes to claim it for the battles looming against the jungle trolls dwelling within Zul'Gurub. To carry out Vol'jin's directive, a seasoned hunter named Zengu was sent to the Horde outpost of Hammerfall, situated in the northeastern reaches of the Arathi Highlands. Nimboya directs travelers from Stranglethorn Vale to seek out Zengu and assist in securing the legendary weapon.

quest:6381.text: New Life. New Life is a restorative Horde quest offered by Tammra Windfield in Sun Rock Retreat. Following the collection of enchanted seeds, the player journeys west into the ashen ruins of the Charred Vale to sow them into fertile earth. This ritual effort aims to spark the land's recovery amidst hostile elementals and harpies. The Charred Vale stands as a tragic testament to recent devastation, choked by soot, furious fire elementals, and scavenging harpies. Tammra Windfield refuses to let the region surrender to ruin. Relying on the ancient resilience of the Earth Mother, she dispatches travelers into the heart of the blackened valley to seek out Gaea Dirt Mounds—patches of fertile topsoil that survived the inferno. The enchanted Gaea seeds planted in the scorched soil are bred to withstand lingering elemental corruption. By taking root, they begin weaving a vital ecological anchor that can resist decay and invite flora back into the valley. Tammra envisions a long-term healing process: as living roots slowly reclaim the basin, the agitated fire spirits will settle, the harpies will lose their desolate roost, and the Venture Company's rapacious logging operations will eventually be driven out.

quest:639.text: Sigil of Strom. Zengu in Hammerfall wants the sigils that guard Trol'kalar, the sword of Lord Ignaeus Trollbane. The first, the Sigil of Strom, was taken by the Syndicate, and a Syndicate agent in Stromgarde is likely to hold it. In ancient times the trolls fought the Arathorian Empire, and their ablest foe was Lord Ignaeus of Strom, called Trollbane. He went into battle wielding Trol'kalar, a name that means troll slayer in the trolls' old tongue. Now Trollbane's sons are weakened and their stronghold lies in ruins. Several sigils protect the sword, and the survivors of Stromgarde each took a share of them. Zengu says they must all be retrieved. The Syndicate seized the first, and Zengu reckons one of their agents in Stromgarde has it. Bring it back to him at Hammerfall.

quest:6393.text: Elemental War. Elemental War is a task undertaken for Tsunaman, an envoy of the water elementals residing at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon Mountains. Guided by the will of Neptulon the Tidehunter, adventurers are sent into the scorched depths of the Charred Vale to extinguish blazing fire elementals and collect their smoldering Incendrite cores. It provides a rare glimpse into the ancient, perpetual rivalry that divides the elemental planes. In the rugged reaches of Stonetalon Mountains, an envoy named Tsunaman has arrived at Sun Rock Retreat on behalf of the Tribunal of the Tides. Acting under the supreme will of Neptulon the Tidehunter, the lord of water elementals, Tsunaman seeks to carry out an ancient vendetta against their fiery kin. Rather than a dispute over mortal borders, this conflict represents the unending clash of Azeroth's primal forces. The primary battleground for this struggle is the Charred Vale, a scarred wasteland smoldering in southern Stonetalon Mountains. Fire elementals thrive amidst the ashes, threatening the surrounding regions. Adventurers are enlisted to descend into the vale, snuff out these flame-wreathed entities, and gather Incendrites—blazing remnants left behind upon an elemental's defeat—to prove their destruction to the Tribunal.

quest:6394.text: Thazz'ril's Pick. Foreman Thazz'ril accidentally left his favorite enchanted mining pick deep inside the northern cavern during a mineral survey. Now overrun by dangerous beasts, the cave known as the Burning Blade Coven holds the glowing tool awaiting recovery. Foreman Thazz'ril, the supervisor overseeing work details in the Valley of Trials, previously ventured into the northern cavern to prospect for mineral veins. While surveying the rocky interior, he accidentally left behind his prized mining pick. By the time he realized his mistake and returned to fetch it, vicious beasts and hostile inhabitants had overtaken the cavern, forcing the foreman to seek assistance from capable recruits to recover his lost tool. To make his prized pick easier to use in dim subterranean depths, Thazz'ril enchanted it with a spell that causes it to glow in the dark. This magical illumination allows adventurers to easily spot the implement resting inside a waterfall chamber within the Burning Blade Coven, though retrieving it requires facing whatever dangerous creatures prowl the cavern shadows. Once returned, Thazz'ril hopes to put the pick back to work uncovering new mining opportunities across the valley.

quest:642.text: The Princess Trapped. The Princess Trapped begins when adventurers uncover an iridescent crystal shard in the Arathi Highlands and hear the plea of Myzrael, a self-styled princess of the earth imprisoned deep underground. Claiming she was trapped by hostile giants, she begs travelers to confront their kobold allies in Drywhisker Gorge and restore power to her crystalline communication network. Scattered across the rolling plains of the Arathi Highlands, strange crystal shards hum with distant power. Approaching them reveals a desperate voice echoing from deep subterranean caverns: Myzrael, a self-proclaimed princess of the earth. She claims that ancient giants cast her down and bound her far beneath the soil, cutting her off from the sunlit lands above. The crystals embedded in the earth represent her sole means of contacting the surface, carrying her pleas for salvation to any adventurer willing to listen. To maintain her tenuous contact and begin breaking through her subterranean isolation, Myzrael directs travelers eastward toward Drywhisker Gorge. The gorge is infested with Drywhisker kobolds, creatures she identifies as allies of her giant captors. These kobolds carry resonant Motes of Myzrael and guard a prominent cluster of iridescent shards. By wresting these motes from the kobolds and applying their energy to the formation, rescuers can empower the crystal cluster and deepen their communication with the trapped princess.

quest:647.text: MacKreel's Moonshine. MacKreel's Moonshine is a fast-paced errand run on behalf of Foggy MacKreel, a dwarf stranded on the broken part of the Thandol Span. Having overindulged on his own potent brew and slept through his watch, Foggy entrusts an Alliance traveler with rushing a fresh batch to Hillsbrad to settle a lingering debt with Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore. Life on watch atop the shattered Thandol Span is wet, cold, and notoriously dull. Foggy MacKreel manages the damp chill by imbibing his own homemade moonshine, a concoction so fierce he compares its aftermath to an entire brigade of siege engines rolling across his skull. Unfortunately for Foggy, one drink too many caused him to pass out during his shift. With Longbraid the Grim commanding the dwarves defending the Span, Foggy cannot afford any further lapses in discipline. Compounding Foggy's troubles is a longstanding debt owed to Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore. Foggy promised Bilger a batch of his personal brew to balance the books, but between his hangover and his shift duties, he finds himself minutes away from default. Relying on gryphons and swift feet, travelers must race across the Arathi Highlands to Southshore to deliver the jug before Bilger decides Foggy has skipped out on his tab once again.

quest:6481.text: Earthen Arise. Deep within Boulderslide Ravine, the shaman Mor'rogal discovers a slumbering Earthen named Goggeroc sealed inside a Resonite cask. Fearing the raw destructive power an ancient being of stone could unleash upon Kalimdor, he sends a champion to shatter the cask and strike Goggeroc down before the creature can recover its full strength. While investigating the vermin infestation in Boulderslide Ravine, scouts discovered a strange relic nestled among the kobolds: a Resonite cask radiating unearthly force. Mor'rogal, a tauren shaman stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, recognized the container for what it truly was—a prison and sanctuary housing Goggeroc, a dormant Earthen. These primordial creations of stone possess strength that outmatches mortal warriors, making the prospect of Goggeroc roaming free an existential threat to the region.

quest:6503.text: Ashenvale Outrunners. Ashenvale Outrunners is a Horde patrol-interception mission issued by Kuray'bin in Ashenvale. Night elf scouts have fanned out from Silverwing Outpost to gather intelligence on nearby Horde encampments, prompting a preemptive strike to keep the outpost's defenses hidden. By hunting down these stealthy scouts, the Horde blinds the local Alliance forces and discourages future incursions. The forests of Ashenvale remain a contested frontier where every path and ridge is fiercely watched. Intelligence is as deadly as an axe, and reports reaching Kuray'bin confirm that night elf scouts known as Ashenvale Outrunners have slipped out from the Alliance stronghold at Silverwing Outpost. Operating in the dense wilderness east of their base and south of local Horde holdings, these scouts stalk the woodland paths to map out fortifications and track troop movements. To prevent an organized assault, the Horde relies on eliminating enemy reconnaissance before it can return home. By hunting down the outrunners, Horde champions deny the commanders at Silverwing Outpost vital knowledge about troop strength and outpost perimeter defenses. Stripped of their forward eyes, the night elves are left disoriented and far less willing to risk aggressive maneuvers through the contested woodlands.

quest:6504.text: The Lost Pages. While transporting a newly acquired goblin shredder from Ratchet to the Warsong Lumber Camp, the orc Gurda Ragescar lost the machine's operating manual to a sudden gust of wind. Stranded near Splintertree Post, she cannot run the complex engineering marvel without recovering the scattered pages. The Warsong Clan relies heavily on steam-powered shredders bought from the goblins of the port of Ratchet to clear lumber across Ashenvale. Operating these delicate, noisy contraptions is far from intuitive for an ordinary orc warrior. When Gurda Ragescar made the journey north with a freshly purchased shredder, a sudden blast of wind tore the instruction booklet from her hands, scattering twelve fragile parchment leaves across the forest floor. Because the wild winds swept the manual over the canopy, individual pages have drifted into the hands of wandering creatures, cultists, and forest denizens across the entire region. Without all three gathered chapters, the complex machine remains an inert block of steel and whirring sawblades, leaving Gurda stranded along the road to Splintertree Post unable to report for logging duty.

quest:6546.text: Warsong Outrider Update. Warsong Outrider Update is a Horde delivery quest originating along the perilous paths of eastern Ashenvale. A lone Warsong scout entrusts an adventurer with vital intelligence detailing threats from the nearby Alliance, entrenched satyr, and encroaching naga in neighboring Azshara. Eastern Ashenvale is a contested border zone where Horde supply lines face constant harassment. The Warsong Outriders maintain a vigilant screen across the woods, scouting enemy movements long before raiding parties can strike outposts like the Mor'shan Rampart or Splintertree Post. Encountering an outrider on patrol means stepping directly into an active theater of reconnaissance, where information can mean the difference between holding a fortification or losing it to ambush. The report compiled by the outrider paints a grim tactical picture for the Horde in Kalimdor's central forests. Beyond the ever-present skirmishes with the night elves and the broader Alliance, eastern Ashenvale crawls with cunning, demonic satyr. Compounding the danger, scouts have uncovered a massive naga presence spreading across the ruined coastal lands of neighboring Azshara, warning commanders that the Horde is hemmed in by hostile powers from almost every direction.

quest:6547.text: Warsong Scout Update. Warsong Scout Update is a Horde communication task connecting the outpost commanders along the borders of Ashenvale with forward scouts watching the contested forest. Carrying strategic orders from Kadrak, couriers ensure the Warsong Clan maintains tight surveillance against ambushing night elves. It highlights the tenuous, hostile grip the Horde strives to maintain over their newly claimed territory. The borderlands of Ashenvale remain a powder keg where neither side yields an inch. Horde forces under Kadrak rely heavily on dispersed Warsong scouts stationed in high-risk outposts to track night elf movements and secure contested supply lines. Because the forest itself provides natural cover to the stealthy sentinels of the Alliance, regular reports and written updates are critical to keeping isolated scouts from being cut off and overwhelmed. For the Warsong clan, every stretch of forest cleared or occupied has been paid for in blood. The scouts watch constantly for retaliatory night elf raids aiming to reclaim the woodlands. Delivering Kadrak's orders reassures the vanguard that reinforcements and coordination remain active, allowing the scouts to report back that their defensive measures are succeeding despite continuous elven resistance.

quest:655.text: Hammerfall. Hammerfall recounts the tragic fall of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer during the liberation of an Alliance internment camp in the Arathi Highlands. Through the grief-stricken memories of Gor'mul, travelers learn how the camp was freed and why the stronghold bears its solemn name. Hammerfall was once a grim Alliance internment camp where captive orcs were kept behind wood and steel after the Second War. That changed when young Thrall and Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer launched an assault to shatter the enclosures and free their kin. Though the raid succeeded in freeing many captives and bringing down the camp's defenses, it ended in tragedy when Doomhammer was struck from behind by a mounted lance, dying on the very soil where the Horde settlement now stands. Not every captive found freedom on that fateful day. In the chaos of battle and the tremors of the earth, an orc named Gor'mul watched the legendary Warchief fall and lost all will to fight. Left behind as his brethren fled, Gor'mul spent years wandering the highlands in directionless grief. Even now that the Horde has reclaimed the site as a fortified base, the memory of that cowardly strike continues to haunt those who survived it.

quest:6561.text: Blackfathom Villainy. Blackfathom Villainy is an urgent plea delivered by a dying Argent Dawn crusader trapped inside Blackfathom Deeps. Horde adventurers are charged with putting an end to Twilight Lord Kelris, the cult leader orchestrating horrific blood sacrifices to an ancient monstrosity in the ruins below. Drawn to the subterranean temple along the Ashenvale coast, the Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid discovered horrors far worse than simple naga incursions. Wounded and stripped of strength within the caverns, the night elf realizes he cannot finish his mission alone. Rather than letting his reconnaissance die with him, he turns to any passing Horde champions willing to strike at the dark leadership presiding over the sunken halls. The target of the task is Twilight Lord Kelris, the head of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who have entrenched themselves within the ruined Temple of the Moon. Allied with the local naga, Kelris conducts dark rituals over the defiled Moon Well, feeding living captives to Aku'mai—a ravenous hydra and beast of the Old Gods—in a mad pursuit of cosmic power and primordial chaos.

quest:6562.text: Trouble in the Deeps. Trouble in the Deeps is a call for assistance sent from Stonetalon Mountains to the remote shores of Ashenvale. Tsunaman directs Horde adventurers to seek out the troll scholar Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost, warning that dangerous forces lurk along the coast. In the arid crags of Stonetalon Mountains, Tsunaman recognizes that dark rumblings to the north demand attention. He charges capable Horde travelers with crossing into Ashenvale—the ancestral woodland of the night elves—to make contact with Je'neu Sancrea. Stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the far western edge known as the Zoram Strand, Je'neu has found himself confronted by mounting peril that requires outside intervention. Reaching the western shore of Ashenvale is no trivial journey for Horde travelers. Whether cutting through the goblin-disturbed passes of Windshear Crag or moving north out of the Barrens, travelers must cross into hostile forest guarded fiercely by night elf sentinels. Far past the dense canopies, on the storm-washed coast of Zoram Strand, the lone outpost clings to survival while peering into the shadowed waters nearby.

quest:6563.text: The Essence of Aku'Mai. Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost has noticed the naga of Blackfathom Deeps harvesting potent sapphire clusters from the caverns. Concerned by their magical properties and elemental water energies, the shaman tasks Horde adventurers with recovering the gems before they can be misused. On the mist-shrouded shores of the Zoram Strand, the Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea keeps watch over ancient Kaldorei ruins now overrun by sinister forces. Deep within the submerged chambers of Blackfathom Deeps, naga have begun mining vibrant sapphire formations that sprout along the damp cavern walls. Sensing that the serpentine invaders seek to harness this volatile power, Sancrea seeks to intercept the harvest before their designs can come to fruition. The Sapphires of Aku'mai are far more than ordinary gemstones; they thrum with elemental resonance and harbor clinging water spirits. In the hands of adept sorcerers, such conduits could fuel dangerous arcane rituals or amplify the influence of the shadowy hydra, Aku'mai, whose dark presence permeates the subterranean temple. Recovering these clusters deprives the naga of an invaluable reagent and safeguards the coastline from runaway elemental magic.

quest:6564.text: Allegiance to the Old Gods. Allegiance to the Old Gods is a Horde quest initiated by recovering a waterlogged message from the naga inside Blackfathom Deeps. Delivering the note to Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost uncovers a sinister ritual plot unfolding deep within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. While battling the naga of Blackfathom Deeps, Horde scouts discover a damp, crumpled note bearing frantic handwriting. The scribbled parchment details instructions directed toward the naga priestesses, ordering them to gather elemental water crystals. Far from random pillaging, these crystals are being collected to fuel the summonings of naga aquamancers, marshaling elemental forces for a far darker objective.

quest:6565.text: Allegiance to the Old Gods. Allegiance to the Old Gods is a Horde quest tasking adventurers with eliminating Lorgus Jett within the depths of Blackfathom Deeps. Directed by the Darkspear seer Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost, the mission aims to disrupt the Twilight's Hammer cultists who seek to awaken ancient forces of destruction. Striking down Lorgus deals a direct blow to the cult's subversive operations beneath Ashenvale's coast. Perched on the strand of Ashenvale, the Horde outpost at Zoram'gar keeps a nervous watch over Blackfathom Deeps. The submerged temple complex has become a breeding ground for dark sorcery, overrun by naga, corrupted beasts, and the cloaked fanatics of the Twilight's Hammer. Je'neu Sancrea, an earthen ring seer stationed on the coast, recognizes that the cultists do not revere the natural balance or spirits of the land. Instead, they pledge their servitude to the Old Gods—monstrous beings of chaos defeated in ancient eras whose malign touch still lingers in Azeroth's forgotten places. Je'neu tasks champions of the Horde with penetrating the subterranean ruins to hunt down Lorgus Jett, a crucial leader among the cultist ranks. Lorgus operates deep within the stone passageways spanning the chambers between the giant turtle Ghamoo-ra and the water elemental Baron Aquanis. Je'neu himself is too frail to march into the damp darkness, making the execution of Lorgus vital to severing whatever dark rituals the cultist sought to orchestrate beneath Ashenvale's waves.

quest:657.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Quae has gone through the folder and learned that Apothecary Jorell is running deadly experiments at Go'Shek Farm. Quae is in poor shape after clashing with orcs and cannot help Kinelory, who will need your protection when she heads for the farm to steal any of Jorell's research not yet sent to Tarren Mill. Quae reads through the folder and finds that Apothecary Jorell is running deadly experiments at Go'Shek Farm. How that touches Hillsbrad is unclear to Quae, yet Phin would not want it to go on. Some of Jorell's research has already been sent to Tarren Mill. While you were away, Quae clashed with some orcs and is in no shape to help Kinelory. Kinelory means to go down to the farm and steal the research Jorell has not yet sent to Tarren Mill, and she will need protection. You are to speak to Kinelory.

quest:6571.text: Warsong Supplies. Warsong Supplies is an expansive Horde logistics quest issued by Locke Okarr at Splintertree Post. Keeping the Warsong Lumber Camp operational demands reclaiming vital logging gear scattered across hostile furbolg and satyr territories, alongside imports arriving from distant goblin ports. The Warsong Clan's campaign to harvest Ashenvale's ancient timber requires an endless flow of heavy tools. From their outpost at Splintertree Post, Horde quartermasters face constant supply disruptions. Locke Okarr is charged with keeping the lumber camp fully outfitted, but local shipments have disintegrated under raids from indigenous wildlife and demonic cultists, leaving the operation starved for vital gear. Securing the needed equipment is an ordeal spanning much of Kalimdor and extending even across the sea. While circular saw blades await collection from the goblin courier Pixel right in Splintertree Post, the crate of heavy axes requires picking up a delivery from Wharfmaster Lozgil down in Booty Bay. The remaining essential goods must be ripped directly from enemy hands: sturdy logging ropes seized by hostile Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolgs, and barrels of Warsong machinery oil stolen by the satyrs of Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian to fuel their profane rituals.

quest:658.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Quae and Kin have been watching Go'Shek Farm for days. Kin saw a courier come out of a small house to the south, and they suspect the courier carries notes bound for Tarren Mill. Quae wants those documents and asks whether you are a skilled tracker. Quae is not surprised that Phin Odelic sent you to check on them, since Phin worries too much. Quae and Kin have been watching the farm for days. Not long ago Kin saw a courier come out of a small house to the south. Kin talks a lot, but Quae can always trust Kin's senses in dangerous areas. Quae asks whether you are a skilled tracker. The courier may carry notes bound for Tarren Mill, and getting hold of those documents could shed some light on what is happening in Hillsbrad. You are to find the Forsaken Courier and bring her Sealed Folder back to Quae near Go'Shek Farm. While you search, Kin spots an apothecary leaving that same house. Quae is confident the apothecary is up to no good, but needs proof before anyone does something rash.

quest:6581.text: Warsong Saw Blades. Warsong Saw Blades is a Horde errand undertaken at Splintertree Post on behalf of the Warsong Clan's logging campaign. To acquire heavy saw blades imported from Ratchet, adventurers must strike an under-the-table bargain with the courier Pixel, who demands personal protection before surrendering the shipment. Fulfilling her trade secures essential machinery needed to keep the Horde's lumber mills humming in Ashenvale. The Warsong loggers in Ashenvale rely entirely on imported heavy machinery to cut through the ancient timber of the deep forest. While Pixel has successfully brought a shipment of specialized saw blades straight from the goblin port of Ratchet to Splintertree Post, she has no intention of simply handing them over for free. Out in the perilous wilds of Ashenvale, coin is only worth so much; personal safety is worth far more. Rather than demanding gold, Pixel insists on bartering the heavy saw blades for a reliable Deadly Blunderbuss to keep herself safe during her dangerous travels through hostile territory. Ashenvale's dense canopy is prized by the Horde, which faces severe timber shortages across the arid plains of Durotar and the Barrens. However, logging ancient sentinel groves quickly dulls standard axes, making goblin-forged industrial blades a necessity. Securing Pixel's shipment directly fuels the operations of the Warsong lumber camps, ensuring the Horde can continue constructing outposts and war machines despite fierce resistance from the night elves.

quest:659.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Phin Odelic leads a band of adventurers looking into odd happenings in the area, and believes the undead are involved. Two companions, Quae and Kinelory, headed for Go'Shek Farm, in the Arathi Highlands. No word has come from them for days. Not long ago, a cousin of Phin's in Hillsbrad had to put down his dog, Stanley. The beast had mystically swollen to a huge size and savagely turned on anyone who came near. Phin believes the undead are involved in the odd happenings, and the group is looking for signs to prove it. Quae and Kinelory, two of Phin's companions, headed into the Arathi Highlands, to Go'Shek Farm, and have not checked in for days. Phin grows concerned and wants you to find them near the farm.

quest:66.text: The Legend of Stalvan. The Legend of Stalvan begins in Darkshire with a foreboding vision from the town diviner, Madame Eva. Disturbed by an omen portending death for her granddaughter Alyssa, Eva draws upon her cards and trance visions to divine a single lingering name: Stalvan. To untangle this thread of dread, she sends travelers to consult town records in the Darkshire Town Hall. In the perpetual gloom of Duskwood, Madame Eva serves as Darkshire's resident seer, interpreting portents and reading cards for troubled locals. After being jolted awake by a terrible disturbance, Eva consulted her divination deck, only to draw the Death card in connection to her young granddaughter, Alyssa. Falling into a deep, shadowy trance to pierce the gloom, she pulled forth only a single clue: the name Stalvan. Terrified of what this omen means for her family and the town, she turns to capable adventurers to follow the thread before tragedy strikes. Eva knows that uncovering the truth of Stalvan requires looking into Darkshire's written history. She directs adventurers across the square to the Darkshire Town Hall to speak with Clerk Daltry, the municipal keeper of ledgers and public archives. Daltry oversees the township's dusty documents, making him the only person capable of determining whether Stalvan was a former resident, a traveler passing through, or something far more sinister buried in Duskwood's past.

quest:660.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory is ready to head down to the farm and wants you at her side. She fears the undead may be doing harm back in Hillsbrad the longer they wait, and you are asked to see her safely back to Quae. After the earlier steps of the investigation, Kinelory is ready to act. She asks you to come with her down to the farm. You are to see her safely back to Quae, and anyone who cares about the people of Hillsbrad is urged to protect her.

quest:661.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory is back from the farm, none the worse for wear, and Quae has the items she brought. Quae and Kinelory mean to stay in Arathi a while longer, so it falls to you to carry word to Phin Odelic in Southshore. Quae is pleased with how well you looked after Kinelory, who has come back in better shape than after a night at the tavern. The items from the farm should give Phin Odelic some idea of what is happening out in Arathi. Since the farm was attacked, Quae and Kinelory plan to stay put a little longer in case of retaliation, and ask you to go back to Southshore and speak to Phin.

quest:6621.text: King of the Foulweald. King of the Foulweald is a Horde military strike commissioned by Karang Amakkar at Zoram'gar Outpost. Seeking to subdue the corrupted Foulweald furbolgs southeast of Astranaar, Horde champions plant a war banner directly atop the tribe's sacred totem mound, provoking and executing their chieftain, Chief Murgut. While the night elves struggle to contain Ashenvale's corrupted native tribes, the Horde approaches the threat with calculated aggression. Karang Amakkar at Zoram'gar Outpost recognizes that while the Foulweald tribe may not rival the vast numbers of the northern Thistlefur, their unchecked ferocity represents a lurking danger along the southern road. Rather than wait for ambushes on Horde patrols, Karang orders a preemptive demonstration of martial dominance to break the tribe's will. The strike targets Greenpaw Village, situated northeast of Mystral Lake. Karang crafts a tribal war banner intended to be driven directly into the center of the Foulweald totem mound—an unforgivable insult to the tribe's ancestral spirits and pride. Furbolg defenders rush the mound in desperation to tear down the offending standard, compelling Chief Murgut to emerge and defend his honor in open combat. Claiming Murgut's personal totem shatters their leadership and establishes Horde supremacy in the area.

quest:6627.text: Test of Lore. The Test of Lore is a trial of intellect and historical memory set by the hermit Braug Dimspirit in the Stonetalon Mountains. After retrieving the ancient tome Legacy of the Aspects, travelers must demonstrate their understanding of ancient history by answering Braug's inquiry. Those who fail to heed the text find themselves abruptly banished across Kalimdor. Part of a broader series of trials originating with Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, the Test of Lore shifts focus away from martial survival or blind trust toward understanding the world's ancient past. Braug Dimspirit, residing in the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, requires seekers to recover ancient texts and genuinely absorb the knowledge held within their pages. The lesson centers upon the creation and division of the Dragon Aspects, specifically the fateful pact made long before the Great Sundering. Braug tests the seeker's recall regarding the Earth Warder, Neltharion, whose descent into madness and betrayal reshaped the surface of Azeroth. Those who do not respect history are not allowed to proceed along the path of wisdom.

quest:6628.text: Test of Lore. This trial marks the intellectual examination in a broader series of spiritual tests originating in Thousand Needles. After scouring the world for historical texts, initiates present themselves to Parqual Fintallas in the Undercity to prove they understand the darker histories that shape Azeroth. While many trials among the Horde test martial strength or raw endurance, the Test of Lore demands scholarly dedication. Originating from Dorn Plainstalker's spiritual regimen at the Weathered Nook, the journey carries candidates far from the wind-carved canyons of Thousand Needles into the shadowed halls of the Undercity. Parqual Fintallas serves as the examiner, holding seekers to an exacting standard of historical literacy.

quest:663.text: Land Ho!. At Faldir's Cove, the lookout Lolo greets you with news that Captain O'Breen's stop here will last far longer than planned. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, are lost, and Lolo suggests you speak with the captain. Lolo, ever on the lookout, spots you arriving at Faldir's Cove. Captain O'Breen had promised the crew only a few hours here, time enough to collect the treasure and head back to Booty Bay. Lolo doubts it will be so quick. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, now rest on the bottom of the sea. Anyone who means to stay is told to talk to the captain.

quest:6661.text: Deeprun Rat Roundup. Deeprun Rat Roundup is an Alliance task in the Deeprun Tram where players assist Monty with pest control. Using a charming musical flute, players round up living Deeprun rats to supply Monty's brother with fresh meat for rat kabobs. Down in the subterranean tube of the Deeprun Tram, a colorful character named Monty struggles to keep the underground transit line clear of pests. Speaking in salty sea slang and treating the tramway like a ship's deck, Monty enlists passing travelers to help round up the scurrying vermin infesting the station.

quest:6662.text: Me Brother, Nipsy. Me Brother, Nipsy is an Alliance delivery quest that takes travelers across the Deeprun Tram between Ironforge and Stormwind. A gnome named Monty tasks commuters with transporting a crate of live rats to his brother Nipsy, who runs a rat kabob stall at the opposite terminal. Beneath the quirky errand lies a touching look at Monty's fractured mind following the tragedy of Gnomeregan. Me Brother, Nipsy is a brief courier errand that introduces commuters to the wonders—and hazards—of the Deeprun Tram. Stationed on the Ironforge side of the tramway, an odd gnome named Monty tasks travelers with ferrying a carton of fresh critters through the subterranean transit corridor to his brother Nipsy at the Stormwind depot. The delivery highlights the bizarre everyday commerce taking place beneath the mountains connecting the dwarven and human capitals. While labeled as a Carton of Mystery Meat, the parcel is actually packed with live, squirming Deeprun rats. Nipsy operates a rat kabob enterprise at the Stormwind terminal and requires his stock delivered before it goes bad. When the crate arrives intact and twitching, Nipsy is relieved to keep his culinary operation stocked for hungry travelers passing through the transit hub.

quest:67.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This errand begins the paper trail into the fate of Stalvan Mistmantle, sent by Clerk Daltry from the town hall of Darkshire. His oldest records point west to the abandoned Moonbrook Schoolhouse in Westfall, setting off a classic investigation into an ordinary man's unraveling. After the initial inquiries in Darkshire, Clerk Daltry pulls the town registry to locate Stalvan Mistmantle. To his surprise, the ledger hasn't been updated in years and lists Stalvan's last known residence far to the west, at the schoolhouse in Moonbrook. Unaware of the sinister nature of the investigation, Daltry treats it as routine bureaucratic upkeep, asking travelers to look into the address and gather whatever records might bring Darkshire's dusty archives up to date. Following the trail means venturing beyond the gloom of Duskwood into the lawless dust of Westfall. Moonbrook, once a thriving agricultural settlement, now crawls with Defias Brotherhood outlaws. Near the center of the derelict town stands its abandoned schoolhouse, standing quiet amid the bandit occupation. Inside, an old footlocker holds the first tangible clues to Stalvan's past life as an educator, as well as a lingering, restless sorrow bound to the chest.

quest:671.text: Foul Magics. Foul Magics is a Horde quest originating in Hammerfall within the Arathi Highlands. Tor'gan senses a disturbing demonic presence to the west and discovers traces of dark summoning rituals at Northfold Manor. He asks adventurers to venture into the manor and retrieve bloodstone amulets used in these summonings so he can study their dark magic. Tor'gan, an orc stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall, began noticing an unsettling disturbance drifting through the Arathi Highlands. For an orc, demonic energies are not merely an abstract threat; they evoke a visceral, biological reaction rooted in the history of the blood curse. As Tor'gan tracked the source of his agitation westward toward Northfold Manor, the ambient corruption caused his blood to boil and stoked an involuntary rage within him. Recognizing the telltale aftermath of demonic summoning, he retreated before the dark influence overwhelmed his senses, seeking outside help instead of returning himself. At Northfold Manor, Tor'gan discovered physical evidence of dark rituals: an amulet carved from bloodstone lying on the ground. These magical charms are actively employed to facilitate and stabilize demonic summoning rituals. The specific amulet Tor'gan managed to recover was already depleted of its magical reserves, making thorough magical analysis impossible. In order to investigate the full extent of the summoning and determine what entities were brought forth, he charges Horde travelers with heading into Northfold Manor to retrieve ten intact bloodstone amulets from the practitioners residing there.

quest:672.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands where Tor'gan seeks to lift the spirits of a despondent orc named Gor'mul. When tales of Orgrimmar and Warchief Thrall fail, Tor'gan turns to newly rediscovered shamanic traditions to craft a revitalizing amulet from highland raptor eyes. At the remote outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, the orcs face enemies from without and quiet battles within. One of their own, Gor'mul, has fallen into a deep, unshakable melancholy. His companions attempted to rally him with proud tales of Kalimdor, the mighty fortress city of Orgrimmar, and the visionary leadership of young Warchief Thrall. Yet none of these grand victories or distant wonders could pierce Gor'mul's gloom or give him reason to hope. Recognizing that mere words are powerless against Gor'mul's despondency, Tor'gan turns to the Horde's revived spiritual heritage. By gathering the eyes of fierce highland raptors roaming Arathi, Tor'gan crafts an amulet blessed with the predators' spirits. Rather than relying on brute force or fel power, this ritual invokes the restorative strength of newly embraced shamanistic traditions, hoping the beast's vital flame can awaken a brother's dormant will to live.

quest:674.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest aimed at rekindling the fighting will of Gor'mul, a broken warrior consumed by despair. An emissary delivers a Raptor Talon Amulet in hopes of awakening the fierce spirit he once possessed. However, Gor'mul remains bitter, questioning whether any simple trinket could ever mend his sorrow or restore glory to the Horde. Raising Spirits involves delivering a Raptor Talon Amulet to an orc named Gor'mul. His allies hope that the wild strength and ferocity of raptors, channeled through the talisman, will reawaken the warrior's flame that once burned fiercely within his veins.

quest:675.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest that addresses the lingering emotional trauma of an old orc veteran. Through the guidance of Tor'gan, a shaman attempts to reach the embittered Gor'mul using ancestral magic to restore his lost pride and will to live. In the wake of past wars, many orcish veterans struggle with the burdens of survival and perceived dishonor. Gor'mul is one such warrior, languishing in bitter despondency because he was denied what he considers an honorable death alongside his fallen Warchief. Tor'gan, an empathetic shaman, seeks to alleviate Gor'mul's suffering by reminding him of his people's spiritual strength. Believing that ancestral energies can heal emotional wounds, Tor'gan prepares an enchanted amulet intended to rekindle the old fighter's pride.

quest:676.text: The Hammer May Fall. Dispatched by Tallow from Tarren Mill, Horde champions are directed across the mountains into the Arathi Highlands to relieve the embattled settlement of Hammerfall. Before reporting to Drum Fel, adventurers must prove their battle readiness against the brutish Boulderfist ogres lurking near the ruins of Stromgarde. In Tarren Mill, Tallow harbors little patience for untested adventurers wandering through the Foothills. Seeing undisciplined recruits standing idle while distant allies bleed, he directs capable fighters east through Thoradin's Wall into the Arathi Highlands. The Horde outpost of Hammerfall stands besieged on multiple fronts, but Tallow refuses to send warm bodies unless they have proven their worth against substantial opposition first. Rather than allowing recruits to stumble blindly into Hammerfall, Tallow demands a demonstration of martial strength at the ogre mound northeast of Stromgarde. The Boulderfist tribe maintains a heavy presence in Arathi, their hulking ogres and enforcers posing an immediate threat to anyone traveling the highland trails. Slaying these brutes serves both to thin the hostile forces flanking the road and to ensure that only capable warriors arrive at the outpost.

quest:677.text: Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde military initiative directed by Drum Fel from the outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Threatened by an alliance between the local Witherbark forest trolls and Boulderfist ogres, the Horde launches a preemptive campaign against the Witherbark to secure their foothold in the region. From the fortified sanctuary of Hammerfall, Drum Fel organizes a preemptive military strike against the hostile native powers of the Arathi Highlands. Surrounded by old human ruins and aggressive local factions, the Horde settlement faces an imminent threat from a cooperative pact formed between the indigenous Witherbark forest trolls and the brute Boulderfist ogres. Rather than allowing their enemies to dictate the terms of survival, Drum Fel calls on champions to take the offensive. The initial offensive focuses south of Hammerfall, targeting the heart of Witherbark territory. The Witherbark have turned their backs on any diplomacy, choosing instead to conspire with the Boulderfist ogres to purge the Horde from the highlands. By culling their specialized axe throwers, headhunters, and witch doctors, Hammerfall seeks to shatter their martial leadership and demonstrate that the Horde is here to stay.

quest:678.text: Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde martial trial issued by Drum Fel at the Hammerfall outpost in the Arathi Highlands. Having proven their basic combat readiness, adventurers are ordered southwest toward the dwarven bridge to engage the dangerous Boulderfist ogres. Eliminating both front-line brutes and spellcasting magi tests the warrior's resolve while protecting the Horde's vulnerable foothold in Arathi. At the isolated Horde redoubt of Hammerfall, survival demands unwavering martial strength. Drum Fel, recognizing the growing capabilities of travelers aiding the outpost, refuses to let anyone rest on easy victories. Rather than facing minor skirmishers, warriors must prove their mettle against what Fel considers a genuine threat: the hulking Boulderfist ogres. These brutes have consistently harassed the Horde expedition and tested the resolve of Hammerfall’s defenders. Fel offers simple terms for the task—warriors are expected to return successful in flesh or honorably in spirit, with praise promised for sheer tenacity in battle. The Boulderfist clan has established an entrenched lair southwest of Hammerfall, extending their territory toward the grand dwarven bridge connecting Arathi to the Wetlands. Unlike undisciplined beasts, the ogres command both crushing physical power and lethal mystical arts, fielding durable brutes alongside cunning magi. Their aggressive presence poses a direct challenge to the Horde's supply lines and regional dominance. By ordering the destruction of ten Boulderfist brutes and four magi, Drum Fel seeks to blunt their strength, ensuring the Boulderfists understand that the warriors of Hammerfall will neither yield ground nor tolerate rivals in Arathi.

quest:68.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This investigation unearths a forgotten chapter in the dark tale of Stalvan Mistmantle. A dusty, unsent letter pulled from a neglected footlocker in Moonbrook provides tangible proof of where he stayed before his vanished trail turned cold, leading back to Darkshire's records. While tracking down the history of Stalvan Mistmantle, an old footlocker tucked away in Moonbrook yields a vital piece of the puzzle: a dusty, unsent letter. Moonbrook, once a thriving agricultural settlement, fell into ruin and now teems with outlaws and restless specters. Stalvan's presence here was brief enough to escape common memory, but this neglected missive definitively places him in the hamlet. Delivering the letter back across the border to Darkshire gives Clerk Daltry the missing documentation he needs. While Daltry finds it peculiar that the letter was never mailed, the evidence is indisputable. With the Moonbrook connection verified, the bureaucratic paper trail can finally guide the investigation toward where Stalvan fled next.

quest:681.text: Northfold Manor. Captain Nials, at Refuge Pointe, asks for help against the Syndicate holding Northfold Manor. Their hold on the land between the defenders of Stromgarde and Southshore makes it hard for supplies to arrive. Stromgarde has been carved up between the ogres, the Syndicate and the Alliance, and every faction fights the others to a bloody stalemate. The Alliance's forces dwindle while their enemies grow. The defenders need help from Southshore, but supplies are slow to arrive. The Syndicate holds the ground between the defenders and Southshore. Captain Nials wants you to go to their base at Northfold Manor and cut down their highwaymen and mercenaries, in the hope that the pressure on the supply trains eases and more get through.

quest:683.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. Sara Balloo's Plea is a somber errand undertaken on behalf of a grieving dwarven widow in Ironforge. Unable to face her monarch directly in her state of sorrow, Sara entrusts a personal appeal to King Magni Bronzebeard regarding her fallen husband, Sully Balloo. After receiving the tragic final letter recovered from the watery depths of the Thandol Span, Sara Balloo finds herself paralyzed by mourning. Rather than let her husband Sully's sacrifice fade into obscurity, she writes a plea addressed directly to the throne of Ironforge. Too overwhelmed by heartbreak to appear before court etiquette herself, she entrusts the sealed parchment to a trusted champion of the Alliance to petition King Magni Bronzebeard on her behalf.

quest:684.text: WANTED: Marez Cowl. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty quest issued against a high-ranking Syndicate operative entrenched within the ruins of Stromgarde. As both an influential advisor and a dark warlock trafficking with demons, Cowl represents a severe threat to the Alliance forces attempting to secure the Arathi Highlands. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty decree posted to eliminate one of the Syndicate's key leadership figures in the Arathi Highlands. Marez Cowl serves as a high-ranking advisor and field operative within the organization, orchestrating their activities in the ruined capital of Stromgarde. By placing a price on her head, Alliance commanders at Refuge Pointe aim to decapitate the Syndicate's local command structure. Unlike typical brigands or dispossessed nobles among the Syndicate, Marez Cowl is a practitioner of dark sorcery. She is known as a cunning warlock who openly traffics with demonic powers to enforce her will and defend Syndicate territory. Approaching her lair within Stromgarde requires confronting not only cutthroats and conspirators, but the fell entities she commands.

quest:685.text: WANTED: Otto and Falconcrest. A bounty posted by the Stromgarde Militia marks Lord Falconcrest, leader of the local Syndicate forces, and his deadly bodyguard Otto for death. Eliminating them strikes a crucial blow against the criminal organization's foothold in the Arathi Highlands. Proof of their demise must be delivered to Captain Nials at Refuge Pointe. The Stromgarde Militia has issued an official bounty targeting two key figures in the Arathi Highlands: Lord Falconcrest and his ferocious bodyguard, Otto. Stationed out of Refuge Pointe, the beleaguered defenders of Stromgarde seek to break the Syndicate's hold over their ancestral lands. Hunters must bring the heads of both targets to Captain Nials to claim the reward. Lord Falconcrest serves as the mastermind behind the Syndicate's coordinated push into the Arathi Highlands. His death represents a vital strategic victory for the Alliance, promising to severely disrupt the criminal network's operations in the region. Beside him stands Otto, a brutally effective bodyguard whose blades have already cut down dozens of Stromgarde's remaining militia soldiers.

quest:686.text: A King's Tribute. A King's Tribute is an Alliance quest offered by King Magni Bronzebeard in the High Seat of Ironforge. Deeply moved by the grief of Sara Balloo, whose husband Sully fell defending the Thandol Span, the King decides to honor the fallen soldier with a lasting monument. He dispatches an adventurer to relay his royal commission to Grand Mason Marblesten. When King Magni Bronzebeard receives the plea of Sara Balloo, he does not dismiss the grieving widow. While he acknowledges that common folk may struggle to understand the brutal necessities of war, the loss of every soldier fighting beneath the Alliance banner weighs heavily upon his conscience. Unable to reverse the grim finality of death on the front lines, Magni chooses to ensure Sully Balloo's sacrifice is never forgotten. Rather than issuing empty platitudes, the King resolves to raise a physical memorial in Sully's honor. He appoints the adventurer as custodian of his royal will, sending them across Ironforge to confer with Grand Mason Marblesten. Entrusted with the King's personal commission, the master stonemason prepares to carve the memory of a fallen defender into stone.

quest:689.text: A King's Tribute. King Magni Bronzebeard has commissioned a monument to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who perished defending the Thandol Span. To honor the fallen warrior with enduring dignity, Grand Mason Marblesten dispatches travelers to Hillsbrad to retrieve pristine Alterac Granite. When King Magni Bronzebeard decided that fallen soldier Sully Balloo deserved a lasting memorial, the task fell directly to Ironforge's finest craftsman, Grand Mason Marblesten. Balloo lost his life during the disaster at the Thandol Span, a vital artery connecting the dwarven lands to northern kingdoms that has suffered brutal attacks by Dark Iron saboteurs. To Marblesten, fulfilling the king's royal decree means creating a sculpture that will withstand both time and war, ensuring that dwarven sacrifice is neither overlooked nor forgotten in the Great Forge. A master dwarven mason will not settle for ordinary quarry rock for a king's project. Marblesten insists that Sully Balloo's likeness can only be captured in Alterac Granite, a dense, resilient stone prized for its durability and clean texture. The challenge lies in securing it: the best deposits lie around Darrow Hill within the contested foothills of Hillsbrad. Venturing deep into the troubled north is dangerous, but dwarven stonework demands materials worthy of the heroism they commemorate.

quest:69.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This errand marks a pivotal turn in the search for the elusive Stalvan Mistmantle, leading investigators out of the gloom of Duskwood and back toward the heart of the kingdom. A hasty, scratched-out entry discovered in Darkshire's town registry points across the river to Goldshire. Following the paper trail to the bustling Lion's Pride Inn is the next step in uncovering where the mysterious tutor went. While reviewing Darkshire's records, Clerk Daltry catches an oversight in the town registry. Tucked beneath an earlier entry for Stalvan Mistmantle lies a second destination, hastily written and partially scratched out as if someone had second thoughts or meant to obscure their movements. The note indicates that Stalvan intended to travel northwest toward Elwynn Forest, specifically to the Lion's Pride Inn. Departing the shadowed groves of Duskwood for the sunny roads of Goldshire offers a stark contrast, but the shadow of Stalvan's past reaches even here. The Lion's Pride Inn serves as the bustling crossroads of Elwynn Forest, welcoming travelers, merchants, and soldiers alike. Innkeeper Farley presides over the busy taproom, making him the ideal person to ask about an educated wanderer seeking lodging.

quest:690.text: Malin's Request. In Stormwind, Malin asks for help recovering relics from fallen Stromgarde. Archmage Malin sends seasoned Alliance adventurers north to Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands, where an expedition seeks the magical relics left behind when Stromgarde fell. Archmage Malin serves in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum and acts for his former mentor, Archmage Trelane. When Stromgarde fell into chaos, Trelane made a desperate stand at the Tower of Arathor. As hostile forces took the city, he had to abandon his post and leave powerful enchanted possessions behind. Malin fears those relics may fall into hostile hands. He sends capable mercenaries north to strengthen his agents in the field and reclaim Trelane's lost belongings. Refuge Pointe lies on the road to Trelane's relics, in the central Arathi Highlands. The outpost is a hard-pressed refuge for Stromgarde loyalists, and Malin's chief contact there is the dwarf Skuerto. Syndicate outlaws, Witherbark trolls, and Boulderfist ogres press the outpost from every side. When you arrive, Skuerto and the garrison are stretched too thin to welcome you warmly without immediate help.

quest:691.text: Worth Its Weight in Gold. At Refuge Pointe, Apprentice Kryten is after Witherbark tusks, medicine pouches and a shadow hunter's knife, all reagents for Archmage Malin, who sent him and Skuerto to gather them. He asks you to seek them among the Witherbark trolls in the southeast of Arathi. Archmage Malin sent Kryten and Skuerto to Arathi to collect reagents, and Kryten had no idea how to gather them until you arrived. He needs ten Witherbark tusks, four medicine pouches and one shadow hunter knife. The Witherbark trolls make their home in the southeast of Arathi. By Kryten's research, any Witherbark troll should have tusks, and the witch doctors carry the medicine pouches. The knife belongs to the mightiest shadow hunters, handed to them after they finish their rites of passage. Only battle will show which of them has one.

quest:6921.text: Amongst the Ruins. Tasked by Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost, Horde adventurers delve into the flooded temple of Blackfathom Deeps to recover a fathom core. The Earthen Ring seeks this relic to uncover the dark elemental plots of the invading Twilight's Hammer cult. The ancient night elven temple of Blackfathom Deeps, once sacred to Elune, has fallen under the dominion of sinister forces. Deep within its submerged passages, the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer have established a stronghold. Stationed at the windswept shore of Zoram'gar Outpost in Ashenvale, the Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea observes the growing taint with rising alarm, recognizing that the cult intends to subjugate the local elements against the land and its defenders. To counter the cult's designs, Je'neu tasks Horde champions with securing a fathom core from the underwater fathom stone within the Moonshrine Ruins. When correctly deciphered by skilled shamans, the core reveals an exhaustive chronicle of elemental currents and disturbances. With this artifact in hand, the Earthen Ring hopes to pierce the veil of the Twilight's Hammer's operations and shield the region from elemental catastrophe.

quest:6922.text: Baron Aquanis. Upon vanquishing the water elemental Baron Aquanis within Blackfathom Deeps, adventurers recover a Strange Water Globe containing tainted, putrid fluid. Brought to Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring, the artifact provides crucial evidence of the elemental corruption spreading beneath Ashenvale. Je'neu believes it will prove what corrupted the baron, and he wouldn't be surprised if it were the Twilight's Hammer cultists lurking in the submerged ruins. Baron Aquanis was no ordinary water spirit, but a powerful elemental corrupted by foul sorcery within the flooded grottos of Blackfathom Deeps. When destroyed, the elemental leaves behind a Strange Water Globe—an impervious orb holding a sloshing, putrid fluid that seemingly sustained and warped the creature's natural essence. The object defies physical damage, harboring energies that are deeply distressing to those attuned to the balance of the elements.

quest:693.text: Wand over Fist. Skuerto at Refuge Pointe has worked out where the first of Trelane's items ended up. Kor'gresh has Trelane's Wand of Invocation in Boulderfist Hall, and Skuerto wants it brought back. After your work for Apprentice Kryten, Skuerto has found where Trelane's first item went. Kor'gresh holds it in Boulderfist Hall, and has been throwing blasts of ice at his own kin to keep them in line. Skuerto reckons the ogre must be close to figuring out all of the wand's powers. Boulderfist Hall lies south of Refuge Pointe and then east of Thandol Span.

quest:694.text: Trelane's Defenses. With the wand in hand, Skuerto turns to the ogres that surround the Tower of Arathor. To bring the tower's defenses to life, he needs an azure agate from the Boulderfist shaman, to be taken to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe. Ogres surround the Tower of Arathor in Stromgarde. Skuerto says the tower's defenses must be activated if you are to stand a chance against them and still reach the items alive. Certain gems from the tower have caught the fancy of the Boulderfist shaman, who carried them off, though Skuerto says they will not keep them for long. Bring one azure agate to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe, who knows the spell to enchant it so that it works as a key.

quest:695.text: An Apprentice's Enchantment. Apprentice Kryten has enchanted the agate you brought him from the Boulderfist shaman. Touched to a pedestal at the foot of the tower, it will wake the tower's defenses. Before you leave, he sends you to Skuerto for the rest. Kryten hands you the enchanted gem. He explains that touching it to a pedestal at the foot of the tower will wake the tower's defenses, and that you should use it when you are ready to go in after the rest of Trelane's items. He will await your return at the camp. First, speak to Skuerto, who will fill in whatever else you need to know.

quest:696.text: Attack on the Tower. With the tower's defenses awake, Skuerto at Refuge Pointe sends you into the ogre-held tower for Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. They should lie in chests inside, and Skuerto says Malin will be more than pleased if you bring them back. After Kryten's enchantment, Skuerto tells you what to look for: Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. The three should be sitting in chests inside the tower, and you should have no trouble opening them yourself, though the ogres call for care. The tower's defenses will not deal with them on their own, and if the ogres find you stealing from them, they will put the hurt on you.

quest:697.text: Malin's Request. Skuerto gives you a sealed letter for Archmage Malin, who is found in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. It tells Malin that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon, and Skuerto is certain Malin will repay you well for helping them in Arathi. After the work in Arathi, Skuerto hands you a letter to take back to Stormwind. Its message for Archmage Malin in the Mage Quarter is that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon. Skuerto has no doubt that Malin will repay you well for helping them, and sends you off with a wish for a safe journey.

quest:6981.text: The Glowing Shard. The Glowing Shard is a mysterious emerald-hued gem plucked from the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Swirling with smoky essence beneath its polished surface, this disturbing relic drives adventurers to seek answers in Ratchet and beyond. Drawn from deep within the Wailing Caverns, the glowing shard immediately unnerves those who hold it. Brilliant green and seemingly solid, it holds churning, mist-like shadows beneath its crystalline face. The crystal exerts a subtle pull, demanding attention while exuding a deeply unsettling aura that hints at the corrupted nature of the slumbering druids and their nightmare-infested sanctuary.

quest:70.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation directs searchers to an abandoned letter left behind at Goldshire's inn years ago. Following the trail of Stalvan Mistmantle leads out of Elwynn Forest and into Stormwind's Canal District. When Innkeeper Farley of the Lion's Pride Inn is asked about Stalvan Mistmantle, he recalls a stormy night years ago. A traveling courier had sought shelter from the pouring rain, only to rush downstairs around midnight in sheer panic. Dressed in only his sleepwear, the courier bolted straight out into the dark storm and was never seen again. In his panicked flight, the courier abandoned his satchel and personal chest in the upstairs room. Among the forgotten cargo lay an unsent letter bearing the name Stalvan, addressed to someone residing in the Canal District of Stormwind City. The chest remained untouched at the foot of the bed until Farley permitted it to be opened.

quest:700.text: A King's Tribute. A King's Tribute marks the final step in honoring the sacrifice of the fallen dwarven soldier Sully Balloo. After fine granite is gathered from the ruins of Lordaeron, Grand Mason Marblesten sculpts a solemn memorial monument in Ironforge on the orders of King Magni Bronzebeard. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned a permanent monument to honor Sully Balloo, a brave dwarf who lost his life in service to his people. Crafted by Grand Mason Marblesten using high-quality granite transported from the war-torn lands of Lordaeron, the finished memorial stands in Ironforge as an enduring testament to fallen soldiers whose sacrifices preserve the dwarven kingdom. When presented with news of the monument's completion, Magni reflects somberly on the limits of stone and mortality. While acknowledging that carved rock can never truly equate to a brave dwarf's life, he hopes the memorial endures so future generations walking Azeroth will never forget the heroes who bled to secure their tomorrow.

quest:701.text: Guile of the Raptor. Guile of the Raptor is a quest in which Tor'gan seeks to awaken the dormant warrior spirit within Gor'mul. By harvesting the hearts of Highland Fleshstalkers, Tor'gan plans to fashion an enchanted item imbued with the cunning and predatory power of the raptor. Tor'gan works to restore a listless compatriot named Gor'mul, whose warrior spirit has fallen dormant. Rather than relying on simple persuasion, Tor'gan turns to primal magic to shock Gor'mul back into action. By crafting a charm imbued with the essence of wild predators, he hopes to reintroduce Gor'mul to martial resolve and demonstrate the strength of their new power. To channel the predatory instincts of the wild, Tor'gan requires the hearts of Highland Fleshstalkers. In shamanic and primal traditions, the heart of a cunning hunter carries its ferocity and guile. Tor'gan weaves both a physical token and a spell from these trophies, aiming to infuse Gor'mul directly with the predator's cunning so he can rediscover his true calling.

quest:702.text: Guile of the Raptor. After the earlier Guile of the Raptor, Tor'gan hands you an orb and sends you to Gor'mul at Hammerfall. Its energy carries the essence of the raptor, meant to stir Gor'mul's spirit and give him new purpose. Tor'gan gives you an orb whose energy is meant to fill Gor'mul with the raptor's essence. He hopes it will rouse the warrior's spirit and set him on a fresh course in life. Once Gor'mul is himself again, Tor'gan means to explain the current state of the Horde to him and gain a great warrior's help in the unceasing battles. Gor'mul greets your return with sourness, saying he wants nothing more than more of Tor'gan's pity and mocking you with talk of brightly colored string.

quest:7162.text: Proving Grounds. Proving Grounds is an initiation rite given by Lieutenant Haggerdin to Alliance recruits enlisting with the Stormpike Guard in Alterac. To earn an official Stormpike Insignia, aspirants must venture into the harpy-infested Icewing Caverns and recover a planted battle standard. Proving one's courage in the cavern marks the first step toward rising through the expedition's military ranks. The Stormpike Guard wages a relentless campaign in Alterac Valley against the Frostwolf Clan. Lieutenant Haggerdin, coordinating forces from the Alliance encampment in the Alterac Mountains, refuses to send green recruits onto the battlefield without a test. Before granting any soldier an official place in the guard, Haggerdin demands proof of skill and nerve by sending them into the treacherous Icewing Caverns southwest of Dun Baldar. The trial is straightforward in concept but deadly in execution: a Stormpike banner stands planted deep within the subterranean ice tunnels. The caverns are not empty; vicious frost harpies nest in the frostbitten recesses and eagerly tear apart unwary trespassers. Returning with the banner intact demonstrates that a recruit can navigate dangerous terrain, withstand brutal predators, and maintain discipline under pressure. Surviving the cavern and returning the standard earns a soldier the Stormpike initiate's insignia, welcoming them officially into the expeditionary force. As Haggerdin promises, the insignia is not merely a trinket—it is a mark of rank that can be enhanced as a soldier earns greater honor on the battlefield, aspiring toward legendary honors such as the Eye of Command.

quest:72.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation directs searchers to the Canals of Stormwind City, where Caretaker Folsom watches over the remaining possessions of the ruined Flintridge family. Looking for answers regarding the mysterious Stalvan Mistmantle, adventurers must dig through crated estate goods while confronting restless spirits tied to a past massacre. Tracking Stalvan's movements leads out of the shadowed groves of Duskwood and into the heart of Stormwind. Beside the city canals, Caretaker Folsom looks after what little remains of the Flintridge household. According to Folsom, his father served the estate before him and had the grisly task of mopping up blood in the wake of a horrific household slaughter—a tragedy somehow tied to the name Stalvan. With the Flintridge trust funds entirely drained and royal tax vultures circling, the family's surviving heirlooms and packed belongings are slated for auction. Whatever keepsakes and papers survived the bloodshed sit piled into shipping crates along the canal embankment. Uncovering Stalvan's trail requires prying open these sealed boxes before the estate's remaining worldly goods are scattered to collectors across the kingdom.

quest:729.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. In southern Darkshore, hostile stone golems overrun a dig site, and Archaeologist Hollee seeks help in Auberdine. She fears for Prospector Remtravel, her senior colleague, whose research often blinds him to mortal danger. Archaeologist Hollee crossed the sea with the Explorers' League, sent by Master Greywhisker to apprentice under Prospector Remtravel. His discoveries had made him renowned in Ironforge's academic circles. The League sent him to study ancient ruins along Darkshore's untamed coast. As the pair excavated what seemed to be the remains of a great civilization, violent stone golems burst from the earth and overran the site. Hollee fled in panic through the night to Auberdine, the night elf port, to seek help. Remtravel barely noticed the danger. Absorbed in the relics he had uncovered, the elderly prospector stayed among the rubble while lumbering constructs surrounded his camp. South of Auberdine, anyone who reaches him finds him grumbling about missing stone brushes and misplaced fossils.
