quest:731.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. At the southern ruins of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel presses on with his dig, hoping to find a prize for the Explorers' League. Hostile troggs and his forgetfulness make the search perilous, and word of his safety must reach his assistant in Auberdine. Far south in Darkshore, Remtravel's Dig lies among ancient ruins. Dwarven excavators searching there uncovered troggs, who drove out the workers and besieged the camp. Remtravel will not leave for Auberdine empty-handed. He wanders into danger to recover a fossil, hoping to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

quest:7321.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. Soothing Turtle Bisque is a culinary task offered by Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill. The Forsaken cook aims to disprove the notion that the undead lack culinary talent by preparing a hearty broth from local snapjaw meat. Players must hunt freshwater turtles around the waterways of Hillsbrad Foothills and the shores of Lordamere Lake to master his prized recipe. It is widely assumed that the Forsaken have entirely abandoned the comforts of life, including the art of fine dining. Christoph Jeffcoat, stationed in Tarren Mill, vigorously rejects that assumption. Boasting that his rich, soothing turtle bisque is good enough to tempt souls back from beyond the grave, Jeffcoat seeks to prove that undead hands are capable of delicate, heartwarming craft even in a land tainted by plague and war. Ordinarily, Jeffcoat gathered his own ingredients from the waterways of Hillsbrad Foothills and the eastern shores of Lordamere Lake in neighboring Alterac. However, duties in Tarren Mill and the encroaching presence of Alliance forces have pinned him down. He relies on passing Horde cooks to hunt the snapjaws, harvest their meat, and bring it back so the culinary tradition can endure.

quest:736.text: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. The Star, the Hand and the Heart is an Undercity quest wherein Keeper Bel'dugur tests an aspiring leader seeking to establish a new chapter of their order. To earn the essential Yagyin's Digest, the petitioner must track down three items of power whose names Bel'dugur dares not speak aloud. Within the shadowed corridors of the Undercity, ambitious practitioners seeking to lead their own circle turn to Keeper Bel'dugur. To establish a new flock and open a chapter of their order, an aspiring leader requires Yagyin's Digest, an authoritative text of ritual lore guarded by the keeper. Bel'dugur stands ready to support his fellow brother, but demands proof of worthiness before yielding such authority. Keeper Bel'dugur will not part with Yagyin's Digest lightly. He requires three distinct items of power to fulfill his side of the exchange. These relics carry such perilous or sacred significance that their names cannot even be spoken aloud; Bel'dugur instead pens them onto a private note. Only a practitioner capable of tracking down and retrieving all three unspoken artifacts proves worthy of founding their own chapter.

quest:74.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This step in the investigation leads deep into an old crate of Flintridge heirlooms left beside the canals of Stormwind City. Sifting through the dusty relics uncovers a torn journal page, offering a vital handwritten clue to the past life of Stalvan Mistmantle that leads to Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest. While digging through a sealed crate filled with musty heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits, investigators uncover a lone torn journal page hidden beneath a ceramic vase. Written in Stalvan Mistmantle's own hand, this remnant provides an intimate glimpse into the mind of a reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

quest:741.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. Hollee sends Remtravel's fossil from Darkshore to Darnassus. She stays behind to watch the wandering prospector, and Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker takes a keen interest in the find. Prospector Remtravel has unearthed a curious fossil along Darkshore's coast. He cares more about digging deeper than following protocol. Archaeologist Hollee stays behind to watch over him among the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists. She asks you, an Alliance traveler, to carry the specimen to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild keeps a scholarly delegation. Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea under the Explorers' League banner, searching Kalimdor's soil for ancient relics and lost history. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker marvels at Remtravel's knack for finding ancient treasures. Night elves see their forests as living sanctuaries, while the League sees ancient lands as ground to study and decipher.

quest:742.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. The Ashenvale Hunt is a summons dispatched to young Horde champions visiting Thunder Bluff, urging them north into the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Delivered by the city's heralds, the call directs travelers to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to take part in a proving hunt. Within the serene heights of Thunder Bluff, runners keep the burgeoning Horde informed of opportunities beyond the borders of Mulgore. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation aimed at proven adventurers looking for greater challenges. With the Horde establishing footholds deep in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, young warriors are called upon to bolster those outposts and test their survival skills in a far harsher environment. Ashenvale represents both rich resources and severe peril for the Horde. Two prominent encampments anchor the faction's presence in the territory: Splintertree Post along the main road, and a remote outpost perched upon the western coast at Zoram Strand. Arriving at Splintertree Post puts incoming recruits directly under the wing of Senani Thunderheart, a veteran outdoorswoman organizing a massive hunt designed to tame the wilderness and claim glory for the Horde.

quest:75.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle leads out of Duskwood to an isolated home in southeastern Elwynn Forest. Marshal Haggard, an aging veteran whose eyesight has deteriorated, directs you to an upstairs chest containing an old bundle of papers left behind when he moved in. Marshal Haggard lives far from town on the southeastern fringes of Elwynn Forest, near the borders of Duskwood and Redridge. When he moved into his secluded home, he found a chest tucked away upstairs packed with old parchments. With his failing eyesight clouding over, he abandoned any effort to read them, leaving the documents undisturbed until an investigator comes asking about Stalvan.

quest:750.text: The Hunt Continues. The Hunt Continues is an early rite of passage assigned by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. It tasks aspiring hunters with gathering mountain cougar pelts from the southern hills to clothe the tribe's children and mend their tents. In Camp Narache, young hunters are taught that taking a beast is never an idle pursuit or a search for trophies. Grull Hawkwind charges fledgling adventurers with venturing into the southern hills of Red Cloud Mesa to track down mountain cougars. Rather than proving martial prowess alone, the task emphasizes responsibility to the community, showing that true hunters must provide essential provisions for their people. Life on the mesa demands durable materials to withstand the open elements. Grull explains that the cougar hides are urgently needed to sew clothing for the tribe's children and to mend worn hide tents throughout Camp Narache. Proving oneself capable of securing these prized pelts earns the gratitude of the elders, and Grull promises to bring word of the hunter's selfless contributions directly to his father, Chief Hawkwind.

quest:755.text: Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the beginning of an initiate's spiritual journey on Red Cloud Mesa. Directed by Chief Hawkwind, travelers seek out Seer Graytongue in the southern hills of Camp Narache. Undertaking these venerable ceremonies is considered a vital trial of passage for tauren coming of age. Upon the Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind directs young tauren seeking to prove themselves to Seer Graytongue. Residing in the quiet hills directly south of Camp Narache, Graytongue oversees the spiritual beginnings of the youth. This simple journey marks the formal threshold between everyday camp life and the serious commitments demanded by tribal custom. The Earthmother is central to the creation beliefs and everyday existence of the tauren. Her rites serve as sacred trials of maturity, resilience, and spiritual depth. As Seer Graytongue cautions all who arrive at his sanctuary, embarking upon the Rites of the Earthmother is no light endeavor, requiring total dedication to the traditions of the mesa.

quest:78.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This errand marks a turning point in uncovering the history of Stalvan Mistmantle, sending investigators from Elwynn Forest back into the shadowed town of Darkshire. Guided by Marshal Haggard's memory of his service days, you bring a recovered journal page to Tavernkeep Smitts at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to identify the chilling handwriting. After recovering a weathered, torn journal page from Marshal Haggard's chest in Elwynn Forest, the retired commander cannot read the faded script due to his failing eyesight. Recognizing that the trail leads back across the river, Haggard recalls his past commanding the Stormwind Guard and remembers spending evenings at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He directs you to Tavernkeep Smitts, a barkeep whose long tenure has made him an unofficial custodian of local history and rumors.

quest:7807.text: A Donation of Wool. A Donation of Wool is a material requisition organized by the Gnomeregan Exiles to gather essential textile supplies. Displaced from their technological home city, the exiled gnomes rely on sixty pieces of wool cloth from generous adventurers across the realm to sustain their community. Contributing to the drive grants formal recognition among the gnome refugees. Following the fall of Gnomeregan to trogg invaders and radioactive contamination, the surviving gnomes found themselves displaced from their high-tech metropolis. Operating as refugees primarily hosted by their dwarven cousins in Ironforge, the Gnomeregan Exiles face severe logistical strain. Routine material drives for basic goods like cloth are essential to keep their people clothed, supplied, and organized while surviving outside their ancestral halls. To avoid overtaxing individual benefactors, the organizers of the drive request exactly sixty pieces of wool cloth per volunteer. By pooling modest contributions from across the realm, the exiles can amass the bulk textiles required for bedding, bandages, and clothing without placing an unsustainable burden on any single supplier. In exchange, the gnomes offer formal recognition among their people to anyone willing to aid their recovery effort.

quest:789.text: Sting of the Scorpid. Sting of the Scorpid is an early trial assigned by Gornek to Horde recruits at the Den in the Valley of Trials. Novices are challenged to hunt venomous scorpid workers northwest of camp and return ten tails to prove their combat readiness. The task serves as a vital lesson in surviving battlefield hazards and respecting even the smallest adversaries. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Gornek tests novice Horde recruits by sending them against the local wildlife. The venomous scorpids roaming the arid dirt northwest of the Den have humbled seasoned warriors and clumsy initiates alike. To prove their battlefield competence, young champions must venture into the rocks, slay scorpid workers, and return with ten of their severed tails as proof of prowess. While deadly, the venomous predators also supply the very salvation of injured initiates. The Den maintains stockpiles of antivenom brewed directly from extracted scorpid venom to treat fallen novices. Beyond surviving the venom, Gornek emphasizes a core tactical truth: in the chaos of battle, arrogance is fatal, and even the smallest foe wields enough lethal venom to bring down a mighty warrior.

quest:79.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This quest marks the moment where scattered rumors about Stalvan Mistmantle solidify into undeniable proof of a brutal crime. Tavernkeep Smitts hands over long-hidden muddy journal pages, directing the investigator straight to Night Watch Commander Althea Ebonlocke. For years, the grim fate of a visiting noble family remained an unresolved tragedy in Duskwood. Tavernkeep Smitts and Marshal Haggard, then a leader of the Stormwind Guard, originally investigated the massacre site and discovered a handful of torn, muddy journal pages. Without handwriting samples or corroborating papers, the notes sat cold, unable to officially implicate the recluse rumored to dwell in the wilderness. The evidence gathered across Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood finally connects the handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle, turning town gossip into an open-and-shut case of murder.

quest:79008.text: ... and that note you found. In Westfall, a scorched note survives beside a dying campfire. Its brief message points toward a place called the twin land. Across Westfall's abandoned fields and wind-scoured plains, travelers find camps left by vagrants, outlaws, and desperate wanderers. This small camp may have been left in haste or secrecy; its provisions lie abandoned, and embers still glow. A scorched slip of parchment rests among the scattered debris. The blistered note bears two short sentences: “Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.” The words point away from Westfall, but give no clear direction. What place shares a name, geography, or fate with this land?

quest:79092.text: Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal. Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal is an arcane volume documenting the investigations of the master mage of the Tower of Azora. Delivered to the scholars of the Ironforge Library, the journal adds valuable magical insights to the great dwarven archive. Archmage Theocritus is known throughout the Alliance as an esteemed spellcaster stationed at the Tower of Azora in the eastern reaches of Elwynn Forest. Over years of solitary study, Theocritus has investigated curious artifacts, ley line anomalies, and nearby magical threats, recording his findings within detailed journals. Recovering such a volume represents a rare opportunity to study the personal observations of a senior Kirin Tor archmage. The Explorers' League and the caretakers of the Ironforge Library maintain one of the greatest archival repositories on the continent. By delivering Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal to their care, adventurers ensure that its arcane insights are safely preserved and cataloged alongside the historic volumes of Khaz Modan. The librarians actively welcome any further magical discoveries that can broaden their collective wisdom.

quest:79192.text: Stepping Stones. A weathered note in the Barrens points travelers toward Stepping Stones, a mountain refuge near Desolace. It says two couriers made deliveries for the New Plague, and calls what happened to them simple apothecary accidents. A torn message hangs from a wooden plank at a backcountry camp in the Barrens. Mercenaries, cutthroats, and drifters pass through such camps for brief shelter, far from the eyes of the Crossroads or Ratchet. Among the wilds' ordinary signs, the note offers a reason to look beyond the camp and toward the mountains.

quest:79236.text: Cherry for Your Thoughts?. In Booty Bay, a mercenary named Tokal is seeking a drink in exchange for the truth behind recent attacks on human and dwarven outposts. While rumors point the finger at the Horde, Tokal insists her group was operating under a private mercenary contract. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, an individual named Tokal is keeping a low profile while watching out for law enforcement. A series of aggressive raids recently devastated human and dwarven camps, fueling rumors that the Horde had orchestrated the attacks. When approached by travelers who clearly do not work for the inquiring marshal, Tokal is quick to push back against the widespread narrative, offering a different version of events in exchange for a drink.

quest:80.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This crucial step in the investigation of Stalvan Mistmantle brings the gathered evidence before Darkshire's authorities. With a bloodstained journal page in hand, Commander Althea Ebonlocke directs the investigator to Clerk Daltry to authenticate the handwriting once and for all. Following the trail of journal pages recovered across Duskwood and the surrounding human territories, the Night Watch finally holds what appears to be damning evidence against the elusive tutor, Stalvan Mistmantle. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has harbored suspicions about the man for some time, but bringing formal judgment requires absolute certainty. A single bloodstained page is not enough to pass sentence until it can be proven beyond doubt that the macabre scribblings originated from Stalvan's own hand.

quest:815.text: Break a Few Eggs. Break a Few Eggs is an errand assisting a harried cook who must keep up with endless meal preparations. Securing fresh, fragile ingredients without breaking them keeps the kitchen running and the cooking on schedule. Feeding a crowd is an exhausting, never-ending endeavor. Between breakfast, lunch, and dinner, there is scarcely any time to step away from the stove, let alone leave the kitchen to scrounge for raw provisions. In Break a Few Eggs, a hard-pressed cook turns to passing adventurers to secure fresh eggs before the next meal service falls behind. Transporting eggs requires a gentle touch that brute force cannot replace. The cook may offer sharp words and little praise, but intact ingredients speak for themselves. Once the eggs are delivered safe and unbroken, the cook wastes no time sending the gatherer off and returning straight to work over the fire.

quest:822.text: Chen's Empty Keg. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn turns to another recipe shared by Chen Stormstout. Trogg ale calls for rare organs and glands from beasts of the Barrens. After helping Brewmaster Drohn recreate Chen Stormstout's first draught, you learn the wandering pandaren shared more than one brewing secret. Drohn has the formula for trogg ale, a strange brew made not from grain, but from potent parts of the wild beasts of central Kalimdor. To make trogg ale, Drohn needs lightning glands from stormhides, a thunderhawk saliva gland from greater thunderhawks, and a hearty liver from the plains' roaming kodos. Once distilled, these ingredients make a fiercely stimulating drink for life in the wilderness.

quest:824.text: Je'neu of the Earthen Ring. This errand directs Horde adventurers to deliver a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals to Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring. As a shaman dedicated to elemental harmony, Je'neu seeks to understand the spreading corruption along the Zoram Strand and within Blackfathom Deeps. Studying the relic offers hope of halting the unnatural blight poisoning the region's waters. When strange, contaminated elementals began surfacing across Ashenvale, scouts took notice of the unnatural power animating them. Among the remains lay a befouled water globe, an intact vessel pulsing with corrupted magic. Knowing standard soldiers and scouts lacked the spiritual insight to diagnose such an anomaly, Mastok Wrilehiss directed Horde travelers to seek out someone with deep knowledge of ancient legends and elemental lore: Je'neu Sancrea. Je'neu Sancrea belongs to the Earthen Ring, an order of shamans committed to preserving balance among the primal forces of Azeroth. While Horde forces guard the frontier along the Zoram Strand, Je'neu concentrates on the spiritual wound festering in the nearby temple ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. To him, an elemental drawing power from a tainted vessel is not merely an isolated threat, but an alarming omen that unseen, ancient powers are perverting the natural order.

quest:8249.text: Junkboxes Needed. At Ravenholdt Manor, Fahrad maintains an endless demand for sturdy, locked containers to train the guild's rising rogues. Because the practice locks provided by the manor's own craftsman are too simple for advanced students, Fahrad trades specialized throwing knives to anyone willing to supply authentic heavy junkboxes. Within the hidden redoubt of Ravenholdt Manor, nestled in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, training never ceases. Master thief Fahrad oversees instruction for the guild's operatives, placing high value on practical lockpicking mastery. While Zan provides practice contraptions for new recruits, Fahrad considers that crude work entirely unfit for experienced operatives who must crack real, stubborn mechanisms in the field. To keep the manor supplied with real-world mechanisms, Fahrad contracts out for heavy junkboxes swiped from dangerous targets across Azeroth. Though only skilled thieves can lift these boxes from marks in the wild, Fahrad does not restrict his business solely to rogues. Anyone who delivers batches of these locked chests—even if already picked clean of major valuables—earns Fahrad's favor and a supply of the manor's lethally balanced throwing blades, provided a token coin remains inside to motivate the initiates.

quest:837.text: Encroachment. Encroachment is a Horde quest directed by Gar'Thok at Razor Hill in central Durotar. It charges champions with striking deep into the western bramble dens to eliminate the entrenched Razormane quilboar threatening the borders of the young orc nation. When Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor and founded Durotar, they found much of the harsh, arid land already inhabited by the Razormane quilboar. These aggressive, boar-like creatures proved a constant thorn in the side of the new settlement. Through sustained military efforts, the Horde drove back the bulk of their numbers, yet fortified pockets of Razormane continue to cling stubbornly to their thorned redoubts west of Razor Hill. Gar'Thok, an officer stationed at Razor Hill, oversees the effort to purge the lingering Razormane threat once and for all. He tasks seasoned defenders with striking directly into the western bramble camps to eliminate their scouts, warriors, and dustrunners. For Gar'Thok and the Horde leadership, allowing the quilboar any foothold near Razor Hill invites disaster, and striking them here is seen as the first step toward securing Kalimdor. Eliminating the quilboar defenders clears the path for Horde forces to torch the bramble dens, preventing the Razormane from reclaiming the western foothills. By burning these structures to the ground, the Horde removes an enduring menace and secures the western perimeter of Durotar, safeguarding vital supply roads between Razor Hill and the wider realm.

quest:843.text: Gann's Reclamation. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire seeks travelers to strike back at Bael Modan. The wandering tauren exile was driven from his clan’s ancestral home and hunting grounds, and asks you to slay the dig’s workers and bring him its leader’s journal. Gann Stonespire walks alone along the southern road, seeking bloody restitution for his fallen kin. His clan’s ancestral birthplace and hunting grounds lay among the red bluffs south of the Barrens. Dwarves from Ironforge came to build Bael Modan, and drove the tauren out or killed them to make room for quarries and trenches. Gann says peaceful protests and diplomacy failed. Now he seeks vengeance for the clan that was displaced and slain. At Bael Modan, dwarven excavators tear into the hills with steam engines and explosives. Prospector Khazgorm leads the dig deep into the earth. Gann asks you to thin the ranks of Bael'dun excavators and foremen, kill Khazgorm, and take the prospector’s personal excavation notes. He wants the notes to learn what the Alliance expedition seeks in the sacred soil.

quest:846.text: Revenge of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire prepares to strike back at the Bael Modan dwarves. After Prospector Khazgorm's death, he sends Horde allies into the fortress for volatile munitions to fuel his attack. Gann Stonespire knows Prospector Khazgorm's death only slowed the Bael Modan dig site. Dwarven work will resume, and another foreman will soon oversee the machines tearing through Gann's ancestral land. He refuses to watch the earth suffer more excavation. Instead, Gann plans to turn the invaders' demolitions gear against them and rupture their stronghold from within. Bael Modan's fortress holds an excavation base and a garrison of soldiers, riflemen, and officers protecting dwarven interests in the Barrens. Gann has learned that its defenders carry nitroglycerin, wood pulp, and sodium nitrate, materials used in industrial demolition. He sends Horde allies past the perimeter to take these volatile supplies from the dwarves. With enough gathered, he can assemble a powerful satchel charge.

quest:847.text: Guile of the Raptor. After Tor'gan's orb gave Gor'mul the raptor's essence, the power he felt has him wondering about the shamans' magic. He sends you to tell Tor'gan he has been convinced, for the time being, and will listen. Gor'mul wonders aloud whether the power coursing through him is the shamans' power that Tor'gan tried to show him. He finds it interesting. He asks you to tell Tor'gan that he has been convinced, for the time being, and will hear what Tor'gan has to say.

quest:849.text: Revenge of Gann. At Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire turns the dwarves’ own plans against their flying machine. The Horde agent seeks revenge for the fallen Stonespire tribe. At Bael Modan, the dwarven excavation sits atop the ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. The Prospectors rely on a gyrocopter for their reach and military strength. It is stationed on a watchtower above the dig, where it surveys the surrounding Barrens and protects the dwarves’ supply lines. For Gann, the machine also marks the Alliance’s intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

quest:857.text: The Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan, a relic called the Tear of the Moons has left Feegly the Exiled mad and obsessed. General Twinbraid has locked it away as a curse, but Feegly still demands its return. The dwarves found the Tear of the Moons while cutting into the southern Kalimdor hills for Bael Modan. It was their first major discovery, and its strange influence fell at once on Feegly, one of the expedition's workers. Feegly claimed the Tear granted him immense power and turned violently on his comrades to protect it. General Twinbraid saw the relic's corrupting hold, called it cursed, took it from Feegly, and secured it in the keep. Banished from the excavation camp, Feegly took refuge among the cliffs. Bitter and obsessed, he begs passing travelers to steal the Tear back.

quest:862.text: Dig Rat Stew. Grub waits east of the Crossroads, hungry for a pot of dig rat stew. He sends travelers to Bael Modan in the southern Barrens to bring back dig rats for his recipe. Across the dry Barrens, hunters bring down zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors. Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads, craves something different: dig rats. He says he is hungry all day and offers to share his recipe with any traveler willing to catch the burrowing rodents. Bael Modan lies deep in the southern Barrens, where dwarven prospectors dig into the red earth. Their work has disturbed nests of dig rats. The dwarves see the small rodents as an infestation, while Grub sees a feast close to the excavation. Grub says dig rats taste best after rotting for several weeks. For a hungry traveler who wants food now, he accepts fresher meat. His recipe shows how forgiving roadside cooking can be on Kalimdor's frontier.

quest:868.text: Egg Hunt. Across the Barrens, Korran seeks silithid eggs for study. The Horde scholar at the Crossroads has heard of intelligent insect creatures in the south and wants intact eggs brought to Orgrimmar. Korran watches the Barrens from the Crossroads and reports to Orgrimmar. While the Horde faces tribal conflicts and Alliance incursions, he studies strange changes in the land. Intelligent, hive-minded insect creatures have begun burrowing into the southern Barrens. Korran needs samples to learn where the silithid come from and what drives them. With an excavation claw, you go to the Field of Giants and take intact eggs from the dirt mounds. Disturbing a mound draws the nearby brood to defend it, showing the swarm's uncanny coordination.

quest:8682.text: Skyseer the Elder. Skyseer the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit residing atop Freewind Post during the Lunar Festival. Travelers seek out his presence high above Thousand Needles to pay their respects to the ancestors and receive his ancient blessing. Perched upon the lofty wooden bluffs of Freewind Post, Elder Skyseer appears bathed in a radiant pillar of celestial light. Positioned near the bridges leading toward the massive mechanical lifts, his ghostly presence offers a quiet sanctuary amid the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles. Elder Skyseer receives visiting adventurers who come to honor the past during the celebration of the Lunar Festival. Beyond acknowledging their homage, the venerable elder can guide travelers toward his kin scattered across Kalimdor, including Elder Morningdew and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8724.text: Morningdew the Elder. Morningdew the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit visited during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. Illuminated by a radiant beam of starlight, she offers ancient wisdom and directs pilgrims toward other elders scattered across Kalimdor. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their blessings with travelers. Elder Morningdew appears bathed in a shaft of lunar light, standing out starkly against the dusty red stone and noisy industrial hubbub of Thousand Needles. She reminds mortal travelers to look beyond earthly concerns to the starry expanse above. When approached, Morningdew encourages seekers to look toward the countless stars for answers to earthly mysteries. Beyond her contemplative greetings, she serves as a guide for festival pilgrims, sharing knowledge of the locations of other venerated spirits walking the lands, including Elder High Mountain, Elder Grimtotem, Elder Mistwalker, Elder Moonwarden, and Elder Windtotem.

quest:87288.text: Soft Saber Pelts. Soft Saber Pelts represents a trade agreement aimed at keeping wilderness roads secure from predatory cats. Hunters bring in the thick furs of local sabers so they can be crafted into warm, protective blankets and shawls. Traversing the untamed paths of Azeroth requires constant vigilance against prowling predators. Large sabers frequently roam near well-traveled thoroughfares, presenting a persistent hazard to couriers, merchants, and lone adventurers. While local inhabitants admire the grace and majesty of these great cats, allowing their numbers to swell unchecked along trade routes invites deadly ambushes. Gathering hunters to keep the local roads safe serves as a necessary measure for communal survival. Hunting such impressive beasts is not done merely for sport or eradication. In frontier encampments, every resource is valued, and the dense, velvety coats of wild sabers are prized for their warmth and durability. Once brought in by capable hunters, the pelts are tailored into fine shawls and heavy blankets capable of fending off harsh weather, ensuring that nothing taken from the wild goes to waste.

quest:873.text: Isha Awak. Along the Merchant Coast, Mahren Skyseer calls you to a hunt in the Great Sea. You are to slay Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, and bring back its heart for a rite of spirit and respect. South of Ratchet, Isha Awak prowls beneath the waves. Known as the Deep Doom, this immense sea creature commands the coastal waters with great strength. Human forces camped along the shore fear those waters after losing many scouts and soldiers to the predator's hunger. Mahren Skyseer reveres the leviathan, unlike the humans who fear it. To the tauren mystic, Isha Awak is no curse or mere pest, but a worthy foe whose might tests a hunter's resolve. Slaying the beast is an act of spiritual communion. Its heart holds the beast's essence, and claiming it lets the hunter carry that untamed spirit forward.

quest:874.text: Mahren Skyseer. At Camp Taurajo, hunters who have mastered the plains are sent east to Mahren Skyseer. Jorn Skyseer sends them to his sister to learn coastal tracking along the Barrens shore. Jorn Skyseer tests hunters at Camp Taurajo against the dangerous beasts of the southern Barrens. Once they have proved themselves on the red plains, he points them beyond dry earth and open savanna. A tracker must learn to follow prey through swamps, over sheer crags, and beside the crashing waves of the Great Sea. Mahren Skyseer keeps a camp far east along the coast. While Jorn studies thunderhawks and plains stalkers, his sister follows creatures that live in the salt spray. Reaching her means crossing dangerous ground. Kul Tiras marines and Theramore expedition forces hold fortified outposts and watchtowers across the coastal lowlands.

quest:876.text: Serena Bloodfeather. Across the northern Barrens, harpy raids threaten the Crossroads supply lines. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing flock, driven by a blood feud with the Horde after Rexxar slew her sister. Ending her campaign could break the harpies’ coordination. Witchwing harpies strike the trails northwest of the Crossroads under Serena Bloodfeather’s command. Their attacks are driven by more than hunger: Serena seeks vengeance against the Horde. During Durotar’s founding, the beastmaster Rexxar slew her sister, the notorious matriarch Bloodfeather. Serena has rallied her flock to attack supply trains, scouts, and merchants traveling the arid trails.

quest:878.text: Tribes at War. Mangletooth bargains for help against the Bristleback from his cage in Camp Taurajo. The captive Razormane quilboar offers intelligence about quilboar incursions in exchange for the deaths of rival spiritual leaders. Mangletooth, a Razormane quilboar, is held in Camp Taurajo by the tauren. The Barrens has long been contested by two powerful quilboar tribes, the Razormane and the Bristleback. The Horde struggles to secure its settlements and supply lines against sudden ambushes. Mangletooth offers insight into who is tormenting Thork's outpost, but he asks a Horde champion to kill the Bristleback's most revered casters. Mangletooth sends you north to strike at the Bristleback's spiritual heart: its Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers. Both tribes revere the earth and draw power from ancient magic tied to their demigod progenitor, Agamaggan. Killing the casters weakens Bristleback rituals, leaves the tribe vulnerable to Razormane rivals, and eases pressure on nearby trails.

quest:879.text: Betrayal from Within. At Camp Taurajo, Betrayal from Within begins with Mangletooth's offer of bloody vengeance. Imprisoned in a cage, the quilboar says his kin left him for dead. He offers Horde travelers knowledge of the three Razormane warlords who emerged from Razorfen Kraul to organize assaults across the Barrens. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth has lost all loyalty to his Razormane kin. They left him behind in defeat, and he faces execution in his cage. Now he wants vengeance against the leaders who abandoned him. He offers Horde travelers knowledge of the true architects behind the ruthless raids across the plains. Razormane attacks keep troubling the Horde, and Thork at the Crossroads struggles to curb them. Mangletooth names three commanders from deep within Razorfen Kraul: Lok Orcbane, a formidable warrior, and his companions Nak, a tracker, and Kuz, a spellcaster. They direct Razormane raiders from encampments far to the south. Mangletooth demands their severed skulls as proof that his betrayers have fallen before his own end arrives.

quest:883.text: Lakota'mani. At Camp Taurajo, hunters bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer after the hunt. The offering honors the mighty kodo's spirit and marks the hunter as an equal to its strength. Among the Barrens herds, Lakota'mani is a kodo of great size and endurance. In Taur-ahe, the tauren tongue, his name means “Earthshaker,” and his steps rumble across the plains. Tauren hunters track and defeat such a beast not for slaughter, but to meet the raw vigor of Kalimdor's wildlife in a sacred hunt. When you bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, the hunt reaches its close. Jorn sees a new power and stride in hunters who return from the encounter. Presenting the trophy earns his blessing, honoring Lakota'mani's courage and primal spirit as companions on your path.

quest:884.text: Owatanka. Across the southern Barrens, Owatanka roams as a swift thunder lizard known to the tauren as Bluebolt. Slaying the beast yields a crackling tailspike, carried to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo in honor of the elders’ tradition of learning from Kalimdor’s primordial beasts. Owatanka prowls the southern Barrens, where tauren hunters speak of him with reverence. Unlike his massive, plodding kin, he moves with blinding speed. The tauren call him Bluebolt, for the storm changed him. Tauren lore says lightning struck Owatanka long ago. The thunder lizard survived, and the strike filled him with unending energy and fury. Even after his death, his tailspike crackles with stray sparks when handled, a remnant of the storm’s power. Taking Owatanka's Tailspike to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo marks a hunter’s prowess and spirit. Jorn recognizes the encounter in the eyes of any hunter who has outmatched the beast’s speed. Presenting the trophy honors Bluebolt’s enduring swiftness.

quest:885.text: Washte Pawne. Across the southern Barrens, Washte Pawne's quill leaves a sting that hunters carry to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. Its pain makes the hunt a trial of regret for the tauren. Thunderhawks are elusive creatures of the Barrens, and wandering nomadic tribes treat them with reverence. Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter” in Taurahe and holds a special place among them. Its death is no ordinary hunt: shamans whisper that striking down a thunderhawk can bring omens of triumph or misfortune. After Washte Pawne falls, its feather burns with a pain that lingers on the skin. Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo explains that the ache is not poison, but regret. Taking a magnificent life bears a burden. The hunter must face that sorrow and turn it into lasting wisdom.

quest:8852.text: Ten Signets for War Supplies. Warlord Gorchuk trades Horde Commendation Signets for war supplies in Orgrimmar. Champions give up formal recognition for equipment that can help keep soldiers supplied at the front. Warlord Gorchuk oversees the Horde's supplies in the Valley of Spirits. As the Horde gathers its legions, weapons, rations, and armor must reach the front. Champions who have proved their dedication can trade commendation signets for useful equipment drawn from the army's reserves. Horde Commendation Signets usually prove a soldier's service and bring prestige with the leadership. Trading them for gear gives up that formal recognition for the chance to survive the fighting. Gorchuk knows that a satchel of supplies or a sturdy weapon can mean the difference between life and death when armies clash.

quest:889.text: Spirit of the Wind. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a burst of speed drawn from Agamaggan's blood shards. The captive quilboar's ritual helps them cross the Barrens swiftly. Crossing the Barrens quickly can help you avoid its beasts and centaur warbands. At Camp Taurajo, the captive quilboar Mangletooth draws on red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. Give him ten, and he channels their lingering power into a burst of swiftness called the Spirit of the Wind. Quilboar honor Agamaggan, the Great Boar whose blood was spilled across central Kalimdor during the ancient War of the Ancients. Mangletooth knows the rites that channel that spilled blood, even in captivity. The ritual stirs wild vigor, lending a runner speed to match the zhevra herds. Though quilboar are bitter enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth shares Agamaggan's boons with travelers who bring him fresh shards.

quest:89.text: The Everstill Bridge. The Everstill Bridge is a rebuilding effort led by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire to repair the town's damaged stone bridge. Progress has ground to a halt because iron meant for the project was redirected into weapons during the last orc invasion, and the replacement caravan from Stormwind was ambushed by Redridge gnolls. The stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill is the lifeblood of Lakeshire, connecting the western roads back toward Elwynn Forest with the far bank and the northern passes. During the recent orc incursions, the town was pushed to the brink. With survival hanging in the balance, Lakeshire melted down its structural iron supplies to forge munitions, blades, and plate armor to repel the Blackrock invaders, leaving the bridge incomplete and vulnerable. Foreman Oslow petitioned the House of Nobles and Stormwind for fresh construction materials to finish repairs. A supply caravan laden with iron was dispatched, but it never arrived. A warband of Redridge gnolls ambushed the convoy along the road, carting away vital iron pikes and rivets into their camps in the northern hills. Without adventurous travelers willing to reclaim the stolen hardware, the bridge project remains stalled while gnolls and orcs tighten their grip on the mountains.

quest:891.text: The Guns of Northwatch. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun in Ratchet wants the guns at Northwatch Hold silenced. Alliance gunners there have been blasting merchant vessels, so he sends you down the Merchant Coast to strike the artillery officers and bring back badges from fallen infantry. Northwatch Hold guards the southern Barrens coast for the humans of Theramore. Its soldiers watch Horde activity in Kalimdor, but fear has made them see every unfamiliar sail as a threat. The guns on the ramparts fire without warning at passing ships, endangering Ratchet's merchant traffic and its privateering vessels. Captain Brightsun wants the attacks on his ships answered. Captain Fairmount commands Northwatch, with Whessan and Smythe directing its guns. Defeating them and taking Theramore medals from the garrison throws the artillery into disarray and gives Ratchet's ships room to travel along the Merchant Coast.

quest:893.text: Weapons of Choice. At Camp Taurajo, Tatternack Steelforge investigates reports of sturdy Razormane weapons. He sends travelers past the Field of Giants to recover them, so the Horde can judge the threat. The Razormane are making unusually durable weapons in the southern Barrens. Most quilboar are dismissed as crude fighters with tools of wood, bone, and stone, so the reports have caught the Horde’s attention. Tatternack Steelforge, an orc smith at Camp Taurajo, is investigating under orders from Warchief Thrall. He doubts the quilboar know proper metalwork and wants proof of whether they have learned new techniques or found better supplies. Tatternack needs weapons from different parts of the Razormane arsenal to study their craft. South of the Field of Giants, scouts face Razormane war camps and seize weapons from their fighters. Razormane Stalkers carry backstabber daggers, Razormane Seers wield charred wands, and frenzied shock troops bear heavy war shields. Each item offers a glimpse of the martial and mystic arts behind the Razormane push against Horde territory.

quest:897.text: The Harvester. A severed head found in the southern Barrens brings The Harvester’s strange presence to Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer examines the remains, and the creature’s intrusion raises concerns for the land’s spiritual and ecological balance. In the southern Barrens, you find the severed head of a silithid called the Harvester. Lions, raptors, and kodos roam these grasslands, but this chitinous insectoid is unlike the native wildlife. Its presence suggests an alien ecology has reached the open plains of Kalimdor.

quest:898.text: Free From the Hold. Gilthares Firebough is held at Northwatch Hold after Alliance forces sink his ship off the Barrens coast. The elf deckhand wants to reach his captain in Ratchet. Gilthares Firebough is held in the dungeons at Northwatch Hold. Theramore uses the fortress as its military foothold on the Barrens coast, where its garrison watches for threats. Gilthares had been aboard a ship carrying moonshine along the trade route between Ratchet and Booty Bay when Alliance forces bombarded it and sent it beneath the sea. He alone survived the wreck. The soldiers took him to Northwatch and accused him of being an enemy agent conspiring against the Alliance. Gilthares says he is only a deckhand who was carrying illicit liquor. With help from Horde forces, he fights his way out of Northwatch Hold and flees north along the shore toward Ratchet. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun welcomes him back to the crew of the Thalo'dan Privateers.

quest:899.text: Consumed by Hatred. Mankrik turns his grief at the Crossroads into a campaign against the Bristleback quilboar. The orc was separated from his wife in a violent ambush, and now he calls on Horde travelers to kill the creatures and bring back their tusks. Mankrik carries the grief of a quilboar ambush that left him battered and his wife missing. At the Crossroads, he watches the arid horizon, still thirsting for the blood of the Bristlebacks despite the many he has killed himself. He calls on fellow Horde travelers to help him continue the fight. Mankrik demands sixty Bristleback quilboar tusks. Each one is a measure of suffering returned to the creatures that tore his life apart. The trophies cannot heal his grief or end his desire for revenge, but seeing the Bristlebacks bleed brings the wounded warrior a fleeting, bitter satisfaction.

quest:90.text: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs. Seasoned Wolf Kabobs is an Alliance culinary quest offered by Chef Grual at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. Grual seeks to prepare his signature house dish, tasking adventurers with hunting wild wolves in Duskwood for the meat, while his seasoning herbs arrive by shipment from Stormwind City. It highlights the everyday survival challenges and resourcefulness required to keep a besieged hamlet fed. Darkshire is an isolated settlement surrounded by the creeping horrors of Duskwood, where trade caravans rarely venture and normal agriculture has completely collapsed. Despite the ever-present gloom and lurking undead, the town's citizens still require sustenance. Chef Grual, presiding over the kitchens of the Scarlet Raven Tavern, makes practical use of the forest's dangerous fauna by transforming wild wolf meat into hearty skewers. Because local timber and soil cannot sustain delicate crops, Grual relies on specialized spices brought in from the capital to make the gamey forest meat palatable. To complete Grual's recipe, travelers need only secure lean flanks from the ferocious wolves stalking Duskwood. Grual has just received his latest shipment of Stormwind Seasoning Herbs, so the meat is all he lacks. The shipment underscores Darkshire's delicate connection to the broader kingdom: while royal military aid has dwindled, small-scale civic ties and supply lines between the city merchants and outer hamlets still barely endure.

quest:906.text: Betrayal from Within. In the central Barrens, the hunt for Lok Orcbane reaches its end. His fall will weaken the Razormane raids, and you carry his severed head to Thork at the Crossroads. Mangletooth, a captured Razormane quilboar held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, names Lok Orcbane as the chieftain directing attacks on Horde caravans. After you slay Lok deep in the southern thorn mazes, Mangletooth gives you the chieftain's skull. He finds it amusing that the orcs will benefit from betrayal within the tribe without knowing a captive quilboar helped them.

quest:91.text: Solomon's Law. Solomon's Law is a local decree issued through Bailiff Conacher in the Lakeshire Town Hall. It condemns the Shadowhide gnolls of Redridge to death for colluding with Morganth, an enemy of Stormwind. Adventurers are tasked with enforcing the town's harsh frontier justice by bringing back pendants taken from the gnolls. Lakeshire stands largely isolated from Stormwind's immediate military support, forcing Magistrate Solomon and his town officials to govern Redridge with strict frontier authority. Operating out of the town hall, Bailiff Conacher serves as the arm of the local magistrate court. When external threats menace the township, the court has little recourse other than putting bounties on offenders' heads, relying on freelance mercenaries and traveling defenders to uphold the kingdom's statutes. The legal justification for exterminating the Shadowhide clan rests on their alliance with Morganth, a rogue spellcaster entrenched in the eastern hills. Under the laws of Lakeshire and the Kingdom of Stormwind, directly aiding a declared enemy of the realm carries a mandatory sentence of death. Because the gnolls actively carry out Morganth's bidding, the court regards them not merely as wild scavengers, but as treasonous belligerents subject to execution.

quest:913.text: Cry of the Thunderhawk. Cry of the Thunderhawk is the culmination of Jorn Skyseer's hunting trials in the southern Barrens. Entrusted by the elders at Camp Taurajo, a hunter must seek out a winged serpent soaring through the scrublands and bring back its wings to prove their mastery over the savanna's fiercest beasts. After proving their mettle against prowling plainstriders, prowlers, and agitated thunder lizards, hunters in the Barrens are directed toward their ultimate challenge by Jorn Skyseer. The thunderhawk is considered one of the most fierce aerial predators inhabiting the scrublands surrounding Camp Taurajo. Slaying one requires patience, sharp aim, and an awareness of the sky that few landbound predators possess. Returning with the thunderhawk's wings marks the end of a novice's tutelage under Camp Taurajo's watchful eyes. For the tauren, hunting is not mere slaughter but an ongoing spiritual walk in harmony with the Earthmother and the natural hierarchy of the wild. Besting such a proud creature shows that the hunter acts with strength, courage, and honor—virtues required before stepping out into harsher wildernesses beyond the central plains.

quest:914.text: Leaders of the Fang. Leaders of the Fang is a pivotal Horde quest tasked by Nara Wildmane from the heights of Thunder Bluff. It directs adventurers into the Wailing Caverns to strike down the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang and retrieve their twisted dream gems. Halting these rogue druids is essential to preventing their serpentine nightmare from permanently overtaking the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex ventured into the subterranean springs of the Wailing Caverns with a selfless ambition: to use the Emerald Dream to restore lush vitality to the arid Barrens. Tragically, when his slumber took root, his dream turned into a waking nightmare. The acolytes who accompanied him lost their devotion to nature's harmony, succumbing to the nightmare's corruption and adopting the mantle of the Druids of the Fang. To reshape the Barrens into their own viperous Eden, the leaders of the splintered sect channel the warped dream energies through specialized foci known as dream gems. Lord Cobrahn, Lady Anacondra, Lord Pythas, and Lord Serpentis each bear one of these gems. As long as these artifacts remain in their grasp, their corrupting influence will seep outward into the soil and waters of Kalimdor.

quest:91723.text: Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in Elwynn Forest given by Hamish Bergwort at the Tower of Azora. Hamish's sensitive arcane equipment is being disrupted by erratic magical surges radiating from the north. To restore stability, travelers must enter Jasperlode Mine and cull the kobold geomancers responsible for the disturbances. Inside the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort oversees delicate arcane apparatus that requires fine calibration. Unfortunately for the scholar, the surrounding countryside is far from quiet. Repeated surges of uncontrolled energy constantly throw off his measurements, rendering careful magical adjustments impossible until the source of the interference is addressed. Investigation traces the magical pulses directly northward to Jasperlode Mine. The subterranean tunnels have been claimed by kobolds, whose geomancers channel crude earth magic within the stone. While their sorcery lacks scholarly refinement, the sheer frequency of their crude rituals generates elemental ripples potent enough to travel through the earth and unsettle Azora's sensitive instruments.

quest:91724.text: Delicate Instruments. Delicate Instruments is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest focused on restoring magical stability to the Tower of Azora. Hamish Bergwort's sensitive equipment is being disrupted by erratic spellcasting practiced by nearby Defias rogue wizards. Resolving the disturbance requires putting an end to the amateur sorcery around Stone Cairn Lake. Within the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort attempts to conduct delicate magical experiments, only to be repeatedly interrupted by unexplained ambient disruptions. In an arcane sanctuary where precise measurements are everything, even slight ripples in the local magical weave can ruin hours of careful work. Bergwort suspects the disruptions are not natural, but rather the result of crude spells cast nearby. The source of the magical static traces back to Stone Cairn Lake, where Defias rogue wizards have been practicing unchecked spellcraft. The Defias Brotherhood's reliance on rogue spellcasters introduces unstable, amateur magic into the Elwynn countryside. Dispatching these rogue wizards silences the magical noise, finally allowing Bergwort's sensitive instruments to register clean readings.

quest:91725.text: Stolen Enchanting Supplies. Stolen Enchanting Supplies is an errand undertaken near the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. An apprentice named Blixie Fitzwink lost a shipment of magical reagents during a gnoll ambush, and adventurers must retrieve the stolen goods from camps around Stone Cairn Lake. Recovering the materials spares the apprentice severe chore duty and keeps Master Theocritus's arcane studies supplied. A routine supply run turns perilous when Blixie Fitzwink, an apprentice assisting Master Theocritus, is ambushed by hostile gnolls between the trading post and the Tower of Azora. Fleeing for her life, she drops her cargo, leaving valuable enchanting reagents scattered among the gnoll camps dotting the shores of Stone Cairn Lake. Desperate to avoid weeks of disciplinary cleanup duty following arcane polymorph experiments, she appeals to passing adventurers to recover the missing goods. The Tower of Azora serves as an arcane bastion in eastern Elwynn Forest, where Master Theocritus conducts sensitive magical research. Sourcing delicate reagents requires regular traffic with local trading posts, but the rising boldness of gnoll packs around Stone Cairn Lake makes transport hazardous. Recovering the lost supplies ensures that Theocritus's studies continue uninterrupted while keeping his beleaguered assistant out of trouble.

quest:91732.text: Good Steel. Good Steel is an Alliance quest originating at Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. In the wake of recent conflicts, high-quality metal has become scarce, leaving the camp's woodcutting equipment worn and difficult to replace. Craftsman Hagar Lowe tasks adventurers with delving into Jasperlode Mine to salvage well-crafted pickaxes so their steel can be repurposed. Following the devastating conflicts that have battered the human kingdoms, high-grade steel has become an increasingly scarce luxury in Elwynn Forest. At Eastvale Logging Camp, daily timber harvesting relies heavily on durable axes, saws, and hardware, but the tools currently available have suffered badly from substandard metal and constant wear. Without reliable shipments coming from Stormwind's foundries, camp craftsmen like Hagar Lowe are forced to find inventive solutions to keep the forestry camp functioning. To replace worn equipment, Hagar sets his sights on Jasperlode Mine, an abandoned excavation north of the camp. The miners who worked the rich veins before the mine's fall used finely crafted picks forged from an era when steel was plentiful and expertly tempered. Rather than letting those sturdy implements rust away in the dark, adventurers are dispatched to venture into the infested tunnels, recover the abandoned picks, and bring them back to Eastvale so their superior metal can be melted down and repurposed for the camp's lumberjacks.

quest:91733.text: Downstream. Downstream is a quest in eastern Elwynn Forest tasked by Ormin Pelford at Eastvale Logging Camp. After Ormin's wagon accidentally overturns into the river, adventurers are asked to brave murlocs and wolves downstream to recover waterlogged timber supplies. While transporting a shipment of gear back from a local trading post, laborer Ormin Pelford suffered a mishap when his wagon tipped over along the waterway near Eastvale Logging Camp. The cargo tumbled into the current and was quickly swept downstream before he could secure it. Without these vital woodworking tools, the loggers face delays in their timber operations. Retrieving the waterlogged cargo is complicated by the hazardous local wildlife. Aggressive murlocs claim the muddy shoals downstream, while predatory wolves roam the surrounding woods. Unable to fend off these threats alone, Ormin relies on hardy travelers to braze the riverbanks, salvage the submerged saw, axe, and toolbox, and bring them back safely.

quest:91736.text: Applejack Still. The Applejack Still is a distillation apparatus used to process fermented apples into high-proof liquor. Approaching the device reveals a stinging vapor of concentrated fruit, which the machine condenses and dispenses as a clear spirit. The Applejack Still is a functional distillation device constructed to refine fermented cider into high-proof spirits. Anyone stepping close to the apparatus is immediately greeted by a pungent aroma of concentrated apples sharp enough to sting the nostrils. Its piping and condensing coils efficiently extract and concentrate the essence of the orchard harvest into potent liquor. Once activated and allowed to run its course, the machine condenses the vaporized alcohol into a clear, purified spirit. The finished applejack dispenses neatly into a waiting bottle at the outlet, ready for consumption or storage. Despite the rough-and-ready nature of field distilling, the apparatus reliably produces a clear and potent brew.

quest:91740.text: Croaky's Head. Croaky's Head is the severed bounty from a menacing murloc leader who terrorized the roads of eastern Elwynn Forest. Bringing proof of the creature's death to the Stormwind guard at Ridgepoint Tower offers grim relief to a garrison grieving their fallen comrades. It marks an essential victory for local defenders struggling to secure Elwynn's contested waterways. Murlocs along the rivers and streams of Elwynn Forest have grown increasingly bolder, ambushing unwary travelers and threatening vital trade routes. Among these aquatic raiders, Croaky stood out as a particularly aggressive chieftain, rallying other murlocs and leading attacks dangerously close to local roads. For merchants, farmers, and travelers moving between Elwynn and Redridge, the creature's presence turned peaceful roadways into deadly hazard zones. Striking down this aggressive raider halts a relentless series of ambushes, removing a brazen menace that openly challenged Stormwind's hold over the eastern woodland outskirts. Ridgepoint Tower stands as Stormwind's easternmost sentinel post in Elwynn Forest, guarding the strategic crossing into Redridge Mountains. The guards stationed here, led by Officer Merell Ross, have found themselves stretched thin against the surrounding dangers. The escalating murloc aggression recently claimed the lives of two watchmen on patrol, shaking the outpost and highlighting just how vulnerable the border has become. Presenting Croaky's severed head to Officer Ross delivers tangible proof of retribution, lifting the beleaguered garrison's morale and giving the defenders an opening to finally drive the aquatic raiders back from Elwynn's borders.

quest:91741.text: Nibbled-On Book. The Nibbled-On Book is a volume from Northshire Abbey's library recovered from kobold scavengers in Northshire Valley. Bearing the tooth marks of a confused or ravenous creature, it must be returned to Brother Paxton to preserve the abbey's modest collection. Among the subterranean pests troubling Northshire Valley, kobolds are notorious scavengers known for dragging off anything left unguarded. When an adventurer recovers a chewed tome dropped by a slain kobold, it becomes evident that the creature was not merely hoarding shiny trinkets, but actively trying to gnaw through the cover and parchment. The text clearly originates from the library shelves of nearby Northshire Abbey, bearing marks from the pests' voracious appetites. Inside Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton diligently tends to a small library intended for the quiet contemplation and instruction of the Brotherhood of Northshire. Unfortunately, the brazen vermin creeping around the valley have developed a troublesome habit of slipping in and snatching volumes straight off the shelves. While Brother Paxton is grateful to recover this particular nibbled volume, he remains anxious about the rest of his scattered collection still missing in the hands of the valley's pests.

quest:91743.text: Rascally Rodents. Rascally Rodents is a quest in Northshire Valley where Brother Paxton tasks adventurers with recovering stolen books from the local kobolds. Though Paxton initially fears the vermin are devouring his library, retrieving the texts reveals an unsettling mystery behind the creatures' motives. Brother Paxton in Northshire Valley is in distress over the local kobold infestation, which has spilled over from the surrounding hills and mines into the sacred grounds. Convinced that the ravenous creatures have begun devouring the texts from his collection, he enlists the aid of young adventurers to hunt down the vermin and salvage whatever volumes remain before the entire library is lost.

quest:91745.text: Mining Consultant. Mining Consultant is a Northshire Valley quest that sends adventurers to confer with Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed outside Echo Ridge Mine. Her observations reveal an unusual development: the local kobolds have begun plundering books from Northshire Abbey's library. The kobold infestation at Echo Ridge Mine has taken an unexpected turn. Rather than merely defending subterranean claims and gathering candles, the creatures have caught the attention of local authorities due to strange, coordinated disturbances. Adventurers are directed to seek out Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed near the mine's entrance, to ascertain what she has witnessed from her vantage point outside the tunnels.

quest:91746.text: Elmpaw's Head. Elmpaw's Head is a trophy quest rewarding an adventurer for hunting down the formidable beast Elmpaw. The creature's head is traded to an artisan who prepares mounted trophies for wealthy collectors. Elmpaw's Head marks the conclusion of a hunt against the creature known as Elmpaw. Felling such a beast is regarded as an impressive accomplishment by wilderness trackers and collectors alike, who value tangible proof of victory over dangerous wildlife. Upon presenting Elmpaw's severed head, the hunter is rewarded directly by an enterprising handler. Rather than letting the remains go to waste, the recipient prepares and mounts the trophy to sell to affluent patrons looking to adorn their mantles with fierce wild prizes.

quest:91751.text: Rough Wolf Pelts. Rough Wolf Pelts is an introductory skinning quest in Elwynn Forest offered by Helene Peltskinner near Goldshire. With her husband away assisting near Northshire Abbey, Helene relies on capable skinners to harvest raw hides from local wolves to complete her pending leatherworking orders. Just outside Goldshire, Helene Peltskinner works diligently to supply travelers and residents with cured leather and furs. While her husband typically hunts the prowling timber wolves of Elwynn Forest to keep her workshop supplied, duties near Northshire Abbey have taken him away from the workbench. Left with a backlog of customer orders to finish, Helene enlists the aid of passing apprentices willing to turn their skinning knives toward the local wildlife. The dense woodlands of Elwynn Forest teem with timber wolves that stalk the edges of farmlands and roadways. For novice skinners, gathering rough wolf pelts serves as practical field experience in the trade of hide harvesting. Delivering these skins allows Helene to maintain her business and keep trade flowing through Goldshire, while providing wandering hunters a chance to hone their woodcraft.

quest:91752.text: The Big Picture. The Big Picture is a Northshire Valley task concerning a thieving kobold named Shinyfinder Narf, who has been hoarding stolen books deep within the local mine. Adventurers are dispatched by local authorities to recover the illustrated volumes and return them to Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey. A peculiar incident has disrupted the peace of Northshire Valley: kobolds lurking around the region have been seen scurrying away with books, crying out 'Picture for Narf!' While kobolds are typically infamous for scavenging candles and shiny trinkets, one particular cave-dweller known as Shinyfinder Narf has developed an appetite for illustrated tomes, accumulating a whole sack of them in his subterranean hideout.

quest:91758.text: Follow That Kobold!. Follow That Kobold! is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley dealing with a bizarre theft from the local mines. A kobold has fled with a sack of Brother Paxton's books, prompting the abbey to recruit the dwarven hunter trainer Tordrin Sternblade to assist in tracking the thief. Just when the workers and clerics of Northshire Abbey believed the vermin problem in the mines was under control, an unusual report arrived from Kelsey: a lone kobold was spotted fleeing the tunnels hauling a heavy sack of books. The stolen volumes belong to Brother Paxton, who urgently requires their return to the abbey's collection. Tracking a nimble subterranean scavenger through the wooded grounds of Northshire requires specialized skill. To find the thief, adventurers are directed behind the abbey to the stables to seek out Tordrin Sternblade, a dwarven Hunter trainer newly arrived from Ironforge who possesses the wilderness knowledge needed to pick up the scent.

quest:91772.text: Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds. 'Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds' is a quest that leads adventurers out of Northshire Valley to track wandering kobolds into Elwynn Forest. Using a tracking kit, players discover the trail leads toward the infested Fargodeep Mine and report the findings to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire. As the kobold infestation in Northshire Valley escalates, signs indicate that the vermin are organizing beyond the isolated abbey grounds. Equipped with a tracking kit, scouts are dispatched to follow the trail of the creatures to determine where they are concentrating their efforts. This reconnaissance serves as a crucial bridge between Northshire's local troubles and the broader defense of Elwynn Forest.

quest:91775.text: Book Return. Book Return is an Elwynn Forest quest directing adventurers to recover Brother Paxton's lost reading materials from the infested depths of Fargodeep Mine. Chief among the missing volumes is 'Fun with Elementals,' a beginner's guide that risks granting the mine's kobolds dangerous conjuration abilities if left in their clutches. While investigating the growing kobold menace within Fargodeep Mine, Marshal Dughan tasks adventurers with recovering missing volumes belonging to Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey. Among the scattered texts lost in the dim subterranean tunnels is a particularly volatile primer titled 'Fun with Elementals.' Paxton fears that the instructions within are so accessible that even the mine's crude kobold squatters could decipher them and conjure an elemental creature in the depths. Fargodeep Mine was once a prosperous gold venture for the kingdom of Stormwind, but recent troubles have allowed vermin to overrun its lower levels. As Elwynn's defenders stretch thin, recovered texts must be stored safely in a protective book bag to survive the damp, treacherous caverns. Retrieving Paxton's lost library ensures that mundane records are preserved and hazardous arcane lessons stay out of primitive hands.

quest:91777.text: Rare Books. Rare Books is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley focused on recovering two stolen magical primers for Brother Paxton. Kobolds have hauled the missing texts into the Jasperlode Mine, where they appear to be studying elementary magic and summoning rituals. Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey faces a crisis in his library: several volumes have been carried off by vermin infesting the valley. Only two books remain missing from his catalog: 'Geomancy for Curious Young Wizards' and 'Arcane Explainer: Magical Stuff in Simple Words'. These educational primers were carted away into the depths of the Jasperlode Mine by the occupying kobolds.

quest:91859.text: A Curious Pair. A Curious Pair begins when Trevan Rol notices an unusual duo passing through the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Under the banner of the Earthen Ring, a tauren was seen traveling alongside a high elf—an alliance rare enough in Horde territory to prompt immediate suspicion. The Sepulcher is a grim waystation where strangers are scrutinized carefully, especially those claiming diplomatic business. When two representatives purporting to belong to the Earthen Ring passed along the road, local scout Trevan Rol caught sight of them. While a tauren walking under the shamanic order's mantle surprised no one, his cloaked companion struck the Forsaken as exceedingly bizarre: an unmistakable high elf. The presence of a quel'dorei traveling openly alongside a member of the Horde's shamanic circles naturally raises questions for the Forsaken sentries. The Earthen Ring typically concerns itself with the balance of the elements and rarely fields high elves in Lordaeron, let alone as companions to tauren envoys. To verify where this unusual pair went and what business they might have in the forest, travelers are directed to consult Deathguard Baldren at the edge of town.

quest:91904.text: A Sealed Crate. A Sealed Crate is a turn-in task involving recovered trade goods that have fallen into the hands of highwaymen or were lost along commercial routes. Adventurers return intercepted cargo to trade handlers to secure regional supply lines and receive payment. Wagon trails and shipping lanes have become treacherous due to a sharp rise in ambushes by bandits and thieves targeting trade caravans. Unsuspecting haulers and couriers frequently lose their shipments when caught unawares, leaving heavy sealed crates abandoned along wild roads and wilderness paths until someone recovers them. Merchants and supply coordinators maintain standing bounties for the safe return of missing merchandise. Adventurers who retrieve displaced crates and haul them back to regional collection points help restore compromised distribution lines, earning direct monetary compensation for safeguarding commerce.

quest:92415.text: Remember That I Love You. "Remember That I Love You" begins with a torn, stained parchment discovered among the undead-stalked graves in the Ruins of Lordaeron. The letter tells the tragic tale of a lost child belonging to the Heartweaver family. Seeking answers requires carrying this fragile relic south to the orphanage in Stormwind City. Amid the blighted earth and shambling undead haunting the ruins of Capital City, survivors and scavengers occasionally stumble across reminders of the Third War's devastation. This torn, blood-stained bundle of parchment has barely survived the undead-trodden grounds of the graveyard. Mentioning a missing child of the Heartweaver lineage, it is a testament to lives shattered when Prince Arthas and the Scourge tore through the kingdom. With Lordaeron fallen and the Undercity claiming the catacombs below, the few refugees who escaped south scattered across the kingdoms of the Alliance. In Stormwind City, Orphan Matron Nightingale tends to the children who lost their parents to the wars. Delivering the blood-stained letter to her care represents one of the few hopes that a surviving child of the Heartweaver family might be identified and brought closure.

quest:92456.text: A Green Sample. A Green Sample is an errand offered by Shylamiir in Stormwind City, directing adventurers to infiltrate the secluded magical city of Dalaran. Expecting a pristine specimen of mana-infused vegetation from the central garden, the expedition uncovers unexpected demonic taint among the Kirin Tor's flora. In Stormwind City, the enigmatic Shylamiir seeks an adventurous traveler willing to run a discreet errand into restricted lands. Intrigued by the Kirin Tor's unusual pursuit of botany, Shylamiir desires a living specimen of the mana-infused vegetation cultivated within Dalaran's central garden. Because the secretive sorcerers keep their borders closed to outsiders, obtaining such flora requires someone adept at slipping into places uninvited.

quest:92466.text: Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is an elemental trial undertaken by spiritual initiates to prove their steadfastness. By retrieving requested materials, the petitioner demonstrates their grit and determination to their instructor. Successfully enduring the task confirms their readiness to proceed to the next stage of their training. The Call of Earth is a foundational trial for aspiring practitioners of the elements. Initiates are tasked with fulfilling specific demands to test their patience, resilience, and connection to the stubborn, enduring nature of the earth. Fulfilling the request demonstrates that an adventurer possesses the inner fortitude required to commune with primeval forces. Upon returning with the requested offerings, the mentor recognizes the petitioner's unquestionable grit and determination. Having proven steadfast in the face of elemental demands, the initiate earns recognition and is deemed prepared to undertake the next step of their spiritual journey.

quest:92467.text: Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial in which an elemental initiate drinks an Earth Sapta at the Rise of Spirits to pierce the veil between worlds. Guided by an elemental spirit, the seeker learns the endurance and steadfast resolve of the earth as the foundation for rekindling their lost bond with the winds. To perceive the unseen elemental world, shamans utilize saptas—potent magical brews specifically formulated to align a mortal spirit with a particular elemental realm. When consumed by those possessing sufficient resolve, a sapta opens one's spiritual vision to elemental manifestations that are otherwise hidden from mortal sight. Because of their profound nature, these potions are closely guarded secrets known only to select practitioners. Ritual tradition strictly demands that saptas be consumed solely within sacred sites. For communion with the earth, initiates are directed northeast through a pass to the Rise of Spirits. Drinking the draught upon these consecrated grounds allows the seeker to pierce the veil and behold what the spirits wish to reveal.

quest:92468.text: Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial of communion where an initiate obtains a piece of Rough Quartz from an earth spirit. Brought to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, this mineral shard becomes the core of the practitioner's first Earth Totem, grounding their bond with the elemental forces. The quest begins when an earth spirit grants an initiate a shard of Rough Quartz as living proof of their communion. The spirit instructs the bearer to take this token to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, explaining that even the smallest fragment carries enduring strength. The spirits demand patience, resilience, and wisdom before granting their favor and respect. Windshaper Boros uses the Rough Quartz as the core to fashion an Earth Totem. He reminds the initiate that the elemental path is multifaceted: although their ultimate desire may be to hear and sing the songs of the wind, true mastery requires understanding all four elemental forces, starting with the unyielding ground beneath their feet.

quest:92479.text: A Scribbled Letter. A Scribbled Letter is a summons delivered to adventurers at Northshire Abbey following their early clashes with nearby kobolds. Sent under the seal of Tordrin Stemblade, it directs promising recruits to seek out his training and guidance. The letter marks a crucial step in preparing defenders to face the escalating perils threatening the kingdom of Stormwind. Upon returning from skirmishes with the kobold camps infesting the valley, adventurers at Northshire Abbey receive a hasty missive. Marked with the seal of Tordrin Stemblade, the note requests their prompt attention before attending to other business. The letter serves as an urgent summons to connect budding champions with formal mentorship within the abbey's protective grounds. When presented with the letter, Tordrin Stemblade remarks on how times have changed, observing how unfamiliar folk have taken up weapons in defense of the realm. Acknowledging that the surrounding wilderness grows more hazardous by the day, he invites travelers to seek out his counsel day or night as they master their skills and assist the beleaguered people of Stormwind.

quest:92489.text: Power Overwhelming. Power Overwhelming is a quest issued by High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind City to assist the secluded Kirin Tor. Players are dispatched to the ruined city of Dalaran to quell a dangerous outbreak of wayward arcane energy manifested as a Mana Elemental. Following the devastating destruction of Dalaran at the hands of the arch-demon Archimonde during the Third War, the Kirin Tor retreated inward. Once welcoming scholars and sorcerers from across the world, the surviving magi have grown secretive, reclusive, and deeply distrustful of outsiders as they work tirelessly behind closed borders to rebuild their ruined city. Recent reconstruction efforts to restore Dalaran to its former glory have met severe complications. Dangerous leaks of volatile arcane energies have surged out of control, coalescing into beings of pure mana. Fearing that Dalaran might fall to internal turmoil or abandon its historic ties to the Alliance, High Sorcerer Andromath dispatched champions from Stormwind to quell the Mana Elemental and remind the Kirin Tor of their enduring allies.

quest:92514.text: Welcome to Shen'dar Village. Welcome to Shen'dar Village introduces travelers to the key figures and local dynamics of Shen'dar Village.
