When the Scourge tore through the kingdom of Lordaeron, its palaces, archives, and proud insignias were largely obliterated or left to decay under the shadow of the Undercity. Surviving physical artifacts bearing the royal crest are exceedingly rare. Recovering an intact or weathered crest from the northern ruins represents a tangible piece of human history rescued from oblivion. Following the Third War, thousands of northern refugees fled south toward the Kingdom of Stormwind, carrying only memories of their homeland. In Stormwind City, Lady Dena Kennedy is keen to acquire such remnants of Lordaeron, making relics like this crest deeply cherished in the southern capital.

quest:95195.text: Bloodied Insignia. Bloodied Insignias are tragic remnants of the fallen defenders of Lordaeron, scattered among the kingdom's blighted ruins. Bearing the old crests of the Alliance, these battered badges represent soldiers whose families fled south to Stormwind during the Third War. When Prince Arthas returned to scour Lordaeron with the Scourge, its grand military was overwhelmed and butchered. Countless soldiers perished defending the Capital City and the surrounding lands, leaving behind few physical traces beyond rusted armor and bloodstained brass. These old Alliance insignias belonged to the men and women who stood their ground against the undead onslaught. Trampled into the soil and rubble of the ruins, each medal is an artifact of the kingdom's final, desperate stand. Many survivors of Lordaeron fled south across the sea, settling as refugees in Stormwind City. Decades of alliance and kinship tie the two human realms together, leaving many in the south yearning for closure concerning their missing loved ones. General Marcus Jonathan, commander of the Stormwind city guard, takes custody of these bloodied insignias so that the memory of the northern defenders is preserved and their surviving families may finally learn their fate.

quest:95250.text: Abominable Creatures. Abominable Creatures is a quest given by Captain Truman, a human loyalist desperately awaiting reinforcements on the outskirts of Lordaeron's fallen capital. Believing his commander—a revered Grand Marshal—is still valiantly fighting in the nearby Ruins of Lordaeron, Truman implores a capable adventurer to track him down. The mission exposes the grim fate of the kingdom's lost defenders and the bitter hostility smoldering among surviving loyalists. Captain Truman stands vigilant at his post, anxiously awaiting long-overdue reinforcements to support the defense of Lordaeron. Confident in the martial prowess of his superior—a renowned Grand Marshal whom he describes as a tall, statuesque hero—Truman remains bound by duty after being commanded to hold the line while his commander charged into the ongoing fray. Harboring deep suspicion toward outsiders and openly scorning those he considers lesser breeds, the captain refuses to trust local irregulars. When a capable traveler approaches, Truman seizes the opportunity to enlist aid, pleading for someone to venture into the ruined territory to check on his master's well-being and assess the battle. The search directs adventurers straight into the perilous Ruins of Lordaeron, the shattered capital that fell to the Scourge during the Third War. Although Captain Truman expects his glorious leader to be standing triumphant over the fallen, the reality within the blighted city is far grimmer. The ruins are overrun with horrors, undead remnants, and abominations wandering the broken stone plazas. Navigating these devastated streets requires confronting the brutal truth of what happened to the defenders who ventured into the city. Instead of finding an immaculate knight holding the line, travelers discover that the commander has met a tragic, twisted end among the monstrosities occupying the courtyards.

quest:95328.text: Whispering Horror Residue. Whispering Horror Residue is the squirming remnant of a strange beast recovered from beneath the Whispering Forest. Gathered by intrepid adventurers, these void-touched remains are brought to Father Lankester in Undercity's War Quarter for shadow research. Whispering Horror Residue represents the bizarre, squirming remains scraped up from a defeated beast dwelling beneath the Whispering Forest. Rather than abandoning such an unnatural curiosity, resourceful adventurers gather the twitching material in hopes that researchers within the Undercity can turn it to good use. The creature's remains find an eager recipient in Father Lankester, located within the War Quarter of Undercity. Lankester notes that the Whispering Forest has long been touched by the void, welcoming the chance to examine physical remnants of that dark corruption as he delves into the mysteries of shadow.

quest:95350.text: Welcome to Azeroth. 'Welcome to Azeroth' is an introductory quest that sends a traveler from Thunder Bluff to Orgrimmar on behalf of the Windshapers. Guided by the spiritual ties of the Earthen Ring, the emissary meets with Warchief Thrall to forge bonds of survival and alliance with the Horde. Venturing into the sprawling expanse of Kalimdor, newcomers quickly discover that survival hinges on brotherhood. The Windshapers look beyond their isolated origins to the peoples walking below, recognizing that isolation offers no defense against the threats of Azeroth. By extending a hand to the neighboring tauren city of Thunder Bluff and looking toward the orcish bastions to the east, they seek steadfast companions to brave the wilderness together. The journey carries envoys to the soaring towers of Thunder Bluff before directing them across the barrens to Orgrimmar, the mighty capital of the Horde. Waiting in the tranquil Valley of Wisdom is Warchief Thrall, the guiding heart of the coalition. Standing before Thrall marks the official entry of the Windshapers into the political and spiritual fabric of Kalimdor, bound by common purpose and shared respect for the elements.

quest:95646.text: Horrors in the Highland. Rethiel the Greenwarden senses a foul corruption seeping through a mountain gully into the unsalted waters above the Wetlands. Adventurers must ascend to the excavation sites to slay a Highland Horror and recover its root core. Rethiel discovers that an ancient energy is stirring, warning that ongoing digging threatens the safety of everyone in the region. Deep in the Wetlands, Rethiel the Greenwarden senses a disturbing shift in the land. A foul taint seeps through a mountain gully, infecting the freshwater creatures inhabiting the highlands above. Unlike the hardy life shaped by the brackish lowland waters, these freshwater beings have never known the sea's protective salt, leaving them entirely defenseless against spreading evil. Rethiel calls upon adventurers to venture up to the excavation sites, slay a Highland Horror, and retrieve its root core.

quest:95647.text: Lost in the Thicket Things. A concerned alchemist asks travelers to track down her missing husband, Ardin Grassman, who vanished after pursuing rumors of towering, unknown grasses. Ardin's botanical curiosity led him straight toward a nearby excavation site, where dangerous wildlife and spider attacks have besieged the crew. In 'Lost in the Thicket Things', an alchemist seeks help tracking down her missing husband, Ardin Grassman. Ardin possesses an uncanny, instinctual affinity for nature, routinely braving steep cliffs and distant wilderness to gather rare herbs and botanical specimens to stock her alchemy supplies. When a passing excavation crew brought word of bizarre, towering grasses unlike anything seen before, Ardin's curiosity got the better of him, and he set out to inspect the flora for himself.

quest:95772.text: Songblade Search. Songblade Search is a dwarven errand in which Dorin Songblade asks travelers to check on his brother Daewyn in the Wetlands. Daewyn set off with an archaeological crew from Loch Modan to dig in unexplored hills, but his uncharacteristic silence left his brother fearing the worst. Dorin Songblade remained behind at his workshop, inundated with orders to refit girdles, while his brother Daewyn joined a dwarven excavation crew setting out from Loch Modan. Daewyn ventured north into the rugged hills of the Wetlands, eager to explore virgin ground untouched by dwarven pickaxes. However, Daewyn customarily sends letters immediately after arriving, and his silence left Dorin deeply unsettled.

quest:95795.text: Fallen in the Fen. Fallen in the Fen is a somber journey begun by uncovering a fallen dwarf amidst an excavation site. Delivering the tragic news to his brother, Dorin Songblade in Lakeshire, brings closure to a heartbroken craftsman who had been forging gifts for his departed kin. A quiet tragedy unfolds at the excavation sites, where the lifeless body of an adventurous dwarf is discovered. After covering the remains with the dwarf's own cloak, an adventurer carries the grim news back to Lakeshire to find his kin.

quest:95805.text: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha. Grace of An'she and Mu'sha is a sacred tauren pilgrimage undertaken on Red Cloud Mesa to honor the sun and moon as the celestial eyes of the Earthmother. By carrying fragile, smoldering incense to an elevated shrine in the southeastern hills, travelers show respect to the heavenly lights that bring warmth, life, and direction to the plains. In tauren myth, the sun and the moon are known as An'she and Mu'sha, revered as the twin eyes of the Earthmother. While the elemental spirits dwell directly within the stones, winds, and waters of Azeroth, these celestial twins watch over the world from the heights of heaven. Their constant journey across the sky marks the eternal rhythm of day and night, granting warmth, guidance, and hope to all living creatures. Honoring the twins is an essential spiritual duty, teaching that balance requires reverence not only for the land beneath one's feet, but also for the light shining down from the sky. To honor the celestial twins, a pilgrim must carry smoldering incense into the southeastern hills overlooking the mesa, nestled just south of the prickly quilboar grounds. The journey is an exercise in attentiveness and speed: the fragrant embers must be delivered before they burn away to cold ash, and travelers must take care to keep them away from water along the trail. Upon reaching the elevated shrine, the pilgrim casts the embers into the sacred fire, letting the aromatic smoke carry their respect up into the sky toward the sun and moon.

quest:95809.text: Heartwoven. Heartwoven is an Alliance quest in the Wetlands centered on a simple message of survival and affection. After clearing an escape route for a stranded gatherer in the marshes, adventurers carry a hand-braided reed heart back to Caitlin Grassman in Menethil Harbor. Out in the treacherous marshes of the Wetlands, life and labor carry constant peril. Ardin Grassman, who went out to see the strange grasses at the excavation sites, found himself stranded amidst the swamp's dangers until a passing traveler cleared a path through the wilderness. Exhausted but determined, he pauses to catch his breath and secure his harvest before heading back toward the safety of the port. Before making the trek home, the gatherer takes marsh reeds from his pack and braids them into a woven heart. He entrusts this token to the adventurer to carry ahead to Caitlin Grassman in Menethil Harbor. In the bustling coastal settlement, Caitlin waits in deep worry, clutching the woven reed heart to her chest in relief upon hearing that he survived and will soon return for a warm meal.

quest:95810.text: Lost Relic Carry. Lost Relic Carry involves recovering a fractured piece of an ancient rock-mech automaton and delivering it to Prospector Whelgar in the Wetlands. The relic's unknown composite material hints at the sophisticated engineering of the Titans, earning serious reverence from dwarven researchers. Deep within ancient grounds, adventurers can uncover a fractured component of a rock-mech automaton. Far from being simple rubble, its unusual composite material reveals the craftsmanship of an advanced, ancient mechanism tied to the Titans. Prospector Whelgar, stationed at the Wetlands excavation site, studies remnants of antiquity. Carrying the relic out of danger and delivering it to him provides valuable physical evidence for dwarven scholars probing into their ancient heritage.

quest:95998.text: The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival quest where the traveler Sam teaches fledgling adventurers the art of roughing it in the wild. By pausing to rest beside a basic campfire, travelers learn how to sustain themselves on the road before pursuing specialized tradeskills. The wide lands of Azeroth call to countless restless souls seeking fortune, danger, and renown. Yet raw ambition alone cannot shield a fledgling adventurer from the biting cold or exhaustion of the open road. Mastering basic wilderness craft—knowing when to stop, build a fire, and gather one's strength—is the quiet foundation upon which every legendary journey is built. Sam's invitation offers newcomers a chance to pause and learn these essential outdoor survival habits. Taking shelter beside a warm campfire does more than stave off the night chill; it provides a vital moment of recuperation known as boosted rest. Seasoned survivalists recognize that endurance in the wild depends on resting properly between expeditions. Once these survival basics are understood, craftsmen and gatherers can turn their attention to tradeskills, learning how to assemble dedicated camp fixtures tailored to their specific work out in the field.

quest:95999.text: WANTED: Incinerator Gar'im. WANTED: Incinerator Gar'im is a bounty posted by the authorities in Lakeshire against a hostile orc commander entrenched in Render's Valley. Gar'im commands a dangerous contingent of shadowcasters and is purported to be working with the Blackrock clan holding Stonewatch Keep. Magistrate Solomon offers a handsome bounty for proof of his demise. The Redridge Mountains have grown increasingly perilous as the Blackrock orcs push out from their mountain bastions. In Render's Valley, Incinerator Gar'im leads an active incursion, spearheading dark sorcery alongside loyal shadowcasters. With the local town guard stretched thin and the crown's armies largely absent, Magistrate Solomon has turned to independent mercenaries to eliminate Gar'im, who is purported to be working with the Blackrock of Stonewatch Keep. Gar'im is renowned for his destructive magic and command over shadow-weaving casters. To claim the township's reward, hunters must venture deep into enemy-held territory, defeat the incinerator, and return his shattered staff to Lakeshire's town hall as physical proof that the threat has been severed.

quest:96.text: Call of Water. You carry the Shard of Water back to Islen Waterseer along the Barrens coast. Your journey proves your harmony with restorative energies and earns you a Water Totem. You carry a gift from the Minor Manifestation of Water back across the sea. To earn it, you crossed continents to the tainted shores of Silverpine Forest and faced the corruption there. Water gives life, adapts, and heals, yet its pliant nature leaves it open to blight and dark magic. Before the Minor Manifestation, you witnessed pure elemental will and received the Shard of Water. Now, as you return to the sun-scorched Barrens, the shard reminds you that water connects distant corners of the world. When you give Islen Waterseer the shard, she weighs more than proof of your journey. She tests whether you have learned the balance between preservation and renewal. Lordaeron's spreading rot can hide small victories, yet cleansing even one wellspring matters to the spirits. Islen recognizes your offering and gives you a Water Totem. Through it, you can channel cleansing, healing, and mana-restoring streams into the mortal realm, binding you to the tide.

quest:96050.text: Camping 101: Fishing. Camping 101: Fishing guides outdoorsmen in the essential crafts and etiquette of wilderness survival. It teaches adventurers how to create a decorative Fish Bowl for their campsite and emphasizes the necessity of learning campfire craft from a cooking trainer before heading into the wild. Life on the road across Azeroth demands practical knowledge of the frontier. For aspiring anglers and wanderers, setting up an orderly site requires understanding basic outdoor etiquette. Townsfolk and guards frown upon travelers pitching tents and scattering gear in the center of settlements, so anyone wishing to rest must take their supplies out beyond city borders and into the open wilderness. A proper expedition site requires several essential amenities. Above all, no campsite is considered functional without a warm campfire, a skill traditionally imparted by culinary instructors. Once a fire is sparked, seasoned travelers can lay out specialty accoutrements such as a handcrafted Fish Bowl, transforming a simple rest stop into a fully outfitted angler's haven.

quest:96056.text: Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory quest that instructs adventurers in the art of fashioning wilderness furnishings from harvested animal pelts. It directs skilled skinners to Balthus Stoneflayer in Ironforge to learn how to craft a comfortable Camp Chair for their campsite. Skinning fallen beasts is among the most practical disciplines an adventurer can cultivate while traversing the wilds of Azeroth. Beyond supplying raw leather for armorers and crafters, the hides gathered from predatory cats, bears, and beasts can be repurposed directly in the field. This introductory task directs skinners to transform raw materials into practical wilderness amenities rather than simply selling them off. The quest sends skinning practitioners to seek out Balthus Stoneflayer in the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Balthus knows the secrets of turning prepared animal pelts into a functional Camp Chair. However, he demands that an adventurer first demonstrate clear proficiency in the art of skinning before he agrees to impart his crafting techniques. Life on the road takes a heavy physical toll on travelers and hunters alike. A sturdy Camp Chair offers an adventurer a chance to sit down and unwind by the fire, regaining their energy and sharp senses. Taking a moment to recuperate ensures that when the next dangerous dust-up begins, the adventurer is fighting at peak condition and can strike where it counts.

quest:96101.text: The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory quest offered by the outdoorsman Raan, who teaches novice adventurers the fundamentals of wilderness survival. By resting beside a basic campfire to gain Boosted Rest, wanderers learn essential campcraft before venturing toward nearby trade trainers to learn practical professions. The Great Outdoors serves as an introductory lesson in surviving beyond the safety of settlement walls. Offered by an experienced wilderness traveler named Raan, the task reminds wandering adventurers that raw ambition and steel are useless without the practical campcraft needed to endure harsh elements. Raan welcomes aspiring wanderers into the ranks of restless souls seeking fortune and glory, offering practical guidance to those willing to learn. The core requirement of the lesson is deceptively simple: taking a seat by Raan's basic campfire until the warmth grants the Boosted Rest effect. Out in the vast, untamed territories of Azeroth, knowing how to pause, set up camp, and recuperate can mean the difference between life and death. Once the basics of camping are mastered, Raan directs novices toward local village trainers to take up a trade and learn to craft specialized campsite fixtures.

quest:96243.text: Call of Earth. Call of Earth is an introductory summons calling an initiate to attune with the spirits of the stone. Directed to Coldridge Valley, the traveler must seek out Teo Hammerstorm within the dwarven holdfast of Anvilmar. For an initiate walking the path of the elements, the call of earth is the vital first communion. While elemental energies may already stir across the skin, learning to speak directly with stone establishes a steadfast balance. It teaches the spirit how to find immovable strength, setting firm footing beneath one's boots and within the spirit itself. Initiates in the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh are directed into the shelter of Anvilmar, a massive holdfast forged by hammer, fire, and will. Within this venerable redoubt in Coldridge Valley waits Teo Hammerstorm, who instructs fledgling shamans on how to heed the rumbling earth and begin their elemental duties.

quest:96339.text: Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle. Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle marks the collection of a mysterious package held on your behalf. Left behind by an unidentified messenger, the parcel was narrowly saved from being dumped into the sea before reaching your hands. A mysterious parcel addressed specifically to you was dropped off with an unwilling caretaker. The unknown courier insisted you would arrive to collect it, leaving so swiftly that the receiver could not even refuse delivery. Fortunately, you arrived just before the unclaimed box was tossed into the ocean alongside the evening's refuse. Inside the delivered parcel is a Replica Ironforge Air Rifle, a souvenir honoring the renowned firearm traditions of the dwarven capital. While dwarven mountaineers and marksmen carry deadly firepower through Dun Morogh, replicas like this celebrate the intricate barrelwork and pneumatic mechanisms perfected by Ironforge craftsmen.

quest:96394.text: The Restless Dead. The Restless Dead addresses an alarming disturbance within the crypts of the Hall of Thanes, where ancient dwarven spirits have been roused from their rest. With the caretakers terrified to enter the vaults, an adventurer must descend into the catacombs to put the angry phantoms and the spirit of Anvilmar back to sleep. Deep beneath the surface in the Hall of Thanes, ancestral crypts hold generations of honored dead. Normally resting in quiet slumber, the spirits have been violently agitated by an unseen disturbance in the vaults. Strange noises echoing up from below have spooked the site's caretakers, who refuse to enter the lower chambers to perform their duties until order is restored. Adventurers are called upon to descend into the shadowed stone halls and quiet the agitated souls.

quest:96403.text: Important Heirlooms. Important Heirlooms is a quest where an adventurer aids a nervous gnome named Thom, who was caught lurking in the Hall of Thanes when Dark Iron dwarves breached the vaults in subterranean mole machines. The task involves retrieving scattered dwarven relics under the dubious guise of historic preservation. While exploring the subterranean vaults of the Hall of Thanes, an enterprising gnome named Thom was interrupted by the sudden arrival of Dark Iron dwarves tunneling upward in mole machines. Unable to secure the area himself, Thom recruits passing adventurers to brave the hostile dig site and retrieve valuable dwarven relics scattered across the chambers before the invaders seize or destroy them.

quest:96604.text: The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival quest offered by Brakk to aspiring adventurers. By learning to rest beside a basic campfire, travelers discover the fundamentals of sustaining themselves in the wild before pursuing practical tradeskills. Venturing into the untamed reaches of Azeroth requires more than martial grit; it demands the basic knowledge to endure the elements. Brakk greets aspiring adventurers with a hearty 'Lok-tar', recognizing the restless spirit of those seeking fortune and glory. To survive the long road ahead, every traveler must first master the art of making camp and recovering their strength amidst the wilderness. Taking a seat beside Brakk's Basic Campfire imparts the essentials of recuperation, granting a restorative rest in the open air. Once these survival fundamentals are understood, novice adventurers are directed toward local village craftsmen. There, they can learn tradeskills and discover how to build functional camp fixtures suited to their chosen craft.

quest:96605.text: The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory quest that instructs aspiring adventurers in the fundamental arts of wilderness survival. Guided by the traveler Kaga, newcomers learn how to recuperate beside a basic campfire before advancing to learn tradeskills and craft specialized camp fixtures. Every adventurer setting foot beyond the safety of civilization quickly discovers that raw courage is not enough to survive the frontier. The Great Outdoors introduces newcomers to the vital necessity of wilderness acclimation. Taught by the experienced traveler Kaga, this brief lesson reminds fledgling heroes that thriving in unexplored territories begins with knowing how to establish a camp and endure the open elements. A simple campfire is often all that stands between an explorer and the exhaustion of the untamed wilderness. By taking a seat beside Kaga's hearth and gaining the Boosted Rest buff, adventurers discover the recuperative power of camp life. Once the fundamentals of wilderness rest are understood, Kaga urges travelers to visit nearby settlement artisans to learn tradeskills and master the crafting of professional camp fixtures.

quest:96606.text: The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival lesson offered to hunters by an experienced scout named Lyreena. It emphasizes the importance of resting beside a campfire to recover and gain the Boosted Rest buff while journeying through the untamed wilds. Venturing beyond civilization's borders demands more than sharp aim and keen senses; it requires respect for the raw untamed elements. An experienced scout named Lyreena offers guidance to wandering hunters, welcoming them to pause their trek and take comfort by her campfire. In the perilous wilds of Azeroth, knowing how to establish a hearth and replenish one's strength between hunts is just as critical as knowing how to track quarry. A roaring campfire provides comfort against the nocturnal cold, offering a moment of calm where weary travellers can shake off fatigue. Sitting close to the blaze allows adventurers to gain Boosted Rest, revitalizing their energy and preparing them for the rigors of exploration. Taking time to sit by the embers teaches young adventurers that patience and rest are enduring pillars of wilderness survival.

quest:96608.text: The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors introduces wandering adventurers to the essentials of wilderness survival and campcraft. By taking a seat at Eric's campfire, travelers learn how to recuperate properly in the wild before taking up tradeskills to support their journeys. Stepping out into the wider world requires more than ambition and a weapon or holy symbol. For fledgling travelers, survival depends on knowing how to rest properly amidst the elements. At his basic campfire, the seasoned traveler Eric welcomes wandering adventurers to take a seat, warm themselves by the embers, and discover how vital proper rest is before tackling the untamed wilderness. A simple fire is only the beginning of maintaining an effective campsite on long journeys. Upon learning the fundamentals of wilderness recovery, travelers are encouraged to visit tradeskill trainers in neighboring settlements. There, artisans and crafters teach how to assemble specialized camp fixtures, allowing adventurers to practice their professions and support their expeditions wherever the road leads.

quest:96626.text: Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking teaches budding adventurers that cooking is the fundamental cornerstone of establishing a camp in the wild. By learning the craft from Cook Tomas in Goldshire, travelers acquire the ability to build campfires and pitch their own wilderness camps. For any adventurer braving the wilds of Azeroth, setting up camp begins with a reliable blaze. The quest Camping 101: Cooking instructs novice wanderers that culinary training is not merely about preparing hot meals; it is the vital foundation for survival in the wilderness. By mastering the cooking profession, travelers learn how to strike a proper campfire, turning an untamed clearing into a safe refuge. New travelers in Elwynn Forest are sent to speak with Cook Tomas in Goldshire to learn the fundamentals of the craft. Upon receiving his instruction, adventurers gain the ability to establish basic wilderness camps. While initial camps are simple and hold limited furnishings, honing one's cooking proficiency unlocks larger fires, while other crafting disciplines offer further options to furnish and customize a campsite.

quest:96629.text: Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking introduces adventurers in Dun Morogh to the essential survival skill of cooking. Beyond preparing provisions, learning this trade enables travelers to light campfires that serve as the foundation for wilderness campsites. For any traveler braving the wilds, establishing a reliable campsite begins with a flame. In Dun Morogh, novice adventurers are directed to Kharanos to learn the fundamentals of cooking under Gremlock Pilsnor. Cooking is not simply about sustaining oneself with hot meals on the road; a sturdy campfire serves as the literal and practical anchor for any outdoor camp. A newly learned campfire allows an adventurer to pitch a humble camp anywhere in the open wilderness. While rudimentary fires support only minimal furnishings, improving one's cooking proficiency unlocks the ability to build larger blazes. Furthermore, artisans skilled in other crafting trades can fashion additional furnishings to transform a simple rest stop into a fully outfitted encampment.

quest:96634.text: Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking is an introductory quest that instructs adventurers on the essentials of wilderness camping through the art of cooking. By learning to start a campfire from local trainers like Zarrin in Dolanaar, travelers establish the necessary anchor for setting up wilderness camps. It marks the first step toward mastering outdoor survival and outfitting personal campsites. Every long journey across the wilderness begins with the ability to build a warm fire. In Camping 101: Cooking, fledgling adventurers are directed to seek out culinary training as their initial lesson in bushcraft. Learning to cook is more than preparing meals from wild game; the essential skill of lighting a basic campfire serves as the physical and practical anchor for any outdoor camp. Without a fire to ward off the chill and keep the dark at bay, establishing a reliable campsite in the wilds is impossible. Learning to kindle a basic campfire grants the ability to establish modest camps throughout the wilderness. Although an entry-level camp can support only a few rudimentary furnishings, dedicated adventurers can expand their capabilities. As an adventurer hones their cooking proficiency, they unlock methods to kindle larger, sturdier blazes. Furthermore, artisans versed in other tradeskills can consult their respective trainers to learn how to craft furnishings and improvements to enrich their camps.

quest:96646.text: Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking is an introductory quest that teaches adventurers the culinary arts as the vital foundation for wilderness survival. By learning to start a campfire from Zerril Softbreeze in Shen'dar Village, travelers unlock the ability to pitch their own campsites in the wild. For an adventurer traveling across untamed lands, understanding survival begins with the hearth. Camping 101: Cooking introduces wanderers to the art of culinary craft, not merely for preparing meals, but because mastering a basic fire is the essential first step to establishing a safe resting spot in the wild. Aspiring campers are directed to speak with Zerril Softbreeze in Shen'dar Village to learn the fundamentals of the cooking trade. Once an adventurer understands how to kindle a campfire, they gain the ability to establish a small campsite anywhere across the wilderness. Although rudimentary camps support only minimal furnishings, improving one's craft allows for larger fires and richer arrangements crafted with aid from other tradeskills.

quest:96655.text: Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking introduces adventurers to the essential craft of survival in the wilderness. By directing travelers to Cook Torka in Razor Hill, it teaches the fundamentals of cooking and campfire creation necessary to establish personal campsites in the wild. For any wanderer setting foot beyond settlement gates, surviving the wilderness requires more than sharp steel and sturdy armor. The quest Camping 101: Cooking directs budding adventurers to Cook Torka in Razor Hill to learn the culinary arts. In the open wastes of Durotar and beyond, cooking represents far more than preparing a hot meal—it is the foundational discipline required to light a reliable campfire, which serves as the heart of any campsite. Mastering the basics allows travelers to pitch a modest camp nearly anywhere across the frontier. While a novice campfire supports only a handful of essential furnishings, further dedication to the craft opens new possibilities. Deepening one's cooking expertise allows the construction of larger blazes, while pursuing other trade skills provides the craftsmanship needed to furnish and enhance camps into reliable bastions against the untamed wild.

quest:96661.text: Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking is an introductory quest that instructs adventurers on how basic culinary knowledge forms the foundation of establishing a campsite in the wilderness. By seeking out Pyall Silentstride in Bloodhoof Village, travelers learn to build a campfire to anchor their camp and prepare for life on the frontier. Every long journey through the untamed wilds demands basic wilderness survival, and every true camp begins with fire. For wanderers stepping across Kalimdor, the quest Camping 101: Cooking introduces the essential relationship between culinary training and frontier survival. Cooking is not merely about preparing nourishing meals from hunted game; it provides the fundamental knowledge needed to build a working campfire out in the elements. Without a fire, an adventurer has no camp to return to when night falls. In the rolling plains of Mulgore, adventurers are directed to Pyall Silentstride in Bloodhoof Village to learn the basics of cooking. With this foundational training, an adventurer gains the ability to strike a campfire anywhere in the wilderness and pitch a basic camp. While initial camps are simple and allow few furnishings, advancing one's cooking proficiency unlocks the secrets of kindling larger fires. In turn, craftsmen versed in other trades can craft furnishings to flesh out their frontier outposts.

quest:96821.text: Legging It. Legging It is a quest focused on clearing a dangerous southern path to protect working peons. Threats along the roadway had frightened the labor force into halting their travels, stalling essential duties. By driving back the dangers, adventurers restore safe passage and enable the workforce to return to their assignments. Legging It addresses a disruption in local labor operations where peons became too frightened to journey southward. Rather than performing their assigned tasks, the workers refused to risk travel along the road due to looming perils. By intervening to push back threats along the path, travelers restore enough security for overseers to send their crews back to work. Peons represent the backbone of Horde infrastructure, responsible for timber harvesting, quarrying, and building outposts. Because peons possess little martial prowess, even minor roadside predators or hostile scouts can freeze supply chains. Ensuring that transit corridors remain clear is essential for keeping settlements supplied and productive.

quest:96822.text: For Honor. For Honor is a quest dedicated to commemorating fallen warriors so their deeds are not forgotten. By completing the task, an adventurer ensures that the sacrifices of these combatants endure in memory. The quest For Honor is a solemn mission centered on memorializing fallen combatants. In a world continuously tested by conflict, ensuring that soldiers who gave everything are not forgotten stands as a vital duty for those who survive them. Upon fulfilling the task, the quest giver confirms that the fallen fighters will endure in memory thanks to your efforts. The completed deed ensures their sacrifices remain recognized and respected rather than fading into obscurity.

quest:96825.text: This Fruit Could Bite Back. This Fruit Could Bite Back is a foraging quest focused on collecting wild prickly pears in the arid lands near Orgrimmar. The fruits are prepared into food while their seeds are saved for future planting, with the aim of cultivating a resilient desert crop to nourish the Horde capital. Durotar is a rugged, sun-baked landscape where traditional farming is nearly impossible. To support the burgeoning capital of Orgrimmar, resourceful inhabitants turn to native desert flora. The prickly pear, a hardy cactus fruit equipped with protective spines, thrives in the arid soil and provides much-needed nourishment when gathered with care. Gathering prickly pears is not merely about providing an immediate meal. While the flesh of the fruit is prepared into tasty dishes, the harvested seeds are carefully preserved for cultivation. The ambition is to plant these resilient crops all around Orgrimmar, establishing an accessible and enduring food source right outside the fortress walls.

quest:96895.text: The Argent Emissary. The Argent Emissary marks the arrival of two Forsaken representatives of the Argent Dawn tracking Scourge cultists near the Undercity. Their presence underscores both the shared fight against the Scourge and the simmering tension between the neutral order and the Forsaken authorities. Two Forsaken emissaries from the Argent Dawn have recently arrived in Tirisfal Glades, setting local authorities on edge. Although the Argent Dawn opposes the Scourge, the local Forsaken remain suspicious of any armed, neutral order operating unmonitored within their sovereign territory. Even the shared heritage of the emissaries does little to soothe their vigilance. The emissaries did not come to admire the ruins of Lordaeron; they are pursuing a group of Scourge cultists discovered lurking southeast around the outskirts of the Undercity. Determined to root out the agents of the Lich King before they establish a foothold, one of the emissaries has moved into position near the city gates to monitor the enemy's movements.

quest:96896.text: A Righteous Cause. A Righteous Cause witnesses a conversation between Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr as they reflect on the defense of the Undercity against Naxxramas. Their exchange highlights the memory of Garek Bandarion, an undead hero who rediscovered how to wield the Holy Light as a paladin. The quest illuminates the rare Forsaken who strive to maintain their connection to the Light despite the skepticism of their kin. A Righteous Cause centers on a poignant reunion between two veteran defenders of Lordaeron: Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr. Having survived the harrowing assault when Naxxramas unleashed the Scourge upon the Undercity, the two reflect upon their fallen comrades and the difficult path walked by Forsaken who still revere the Holy Light. The focal point of their shared memory is Garek Bandarion, the fallen hero after whom the keep was named. According to Leonid, Garek may have been the very first of the Forsaken to rediscover how to wield the Holy Light as a true paladin. While most Forsaken have turned away from the Light entirely, Danitha and her cohort dedicate themselves to preserving Garek's legacy and exploring the potential of holy unlife. Following his discussion with Danitha, Leonid prepares to depart the keep. His loyalties lie with the ongoing fight against the Scourge in the ravaged east, where he makes his station at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands, welcoming any able-bodied adventurers willing to take up arms for the cause.

quest:96897.text: The Cult of the Damned. The Cult of the Damned is a task confronting mortal servants of the Scourge active within Tirisfal Glades. By culling Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers, defenders prevent the Lich King's insidious living agents from repeating the betrayals that originally shattered Lordaeron. The Cult of the Damned represents the mortal face of the Scourge. Composed of living men and women who swore fealty to the Lich King, these cultists act where mindless dead cannot. In Tirisfal Glades, where inhabitants already contend with roaming undead and relentless zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, newly discovered cells of Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers signal an insidious attempt by the Scourge to re-establish a foothold. Lordaeron was brought to ruin not merely by marching legions of the dead, but by neighbors who betrayed neighbors. The Cult of the Damned originally infiltrated villages, poisoned granaries, and orchestrated the kingdom's collapse from the shadows. Standing vigilant against fresh Cult activity in Tirisfal is essential to ensure that history does not repeat itself in the scarred lands of the north.

quest:96898.text: Remnants of War. Remnants of War tasks adventurers with recovering shattered shards of the necrotic focusing crystal blown off Naxxramas during its assault on the Undercity. Both the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn suffered heavy losses repelling the citadel, and gathering these dangerous fragments prevents Scourge cultists from reclaiming their dark magic. Not long ago, the dread citadel Naxxramas loomed directly over Tirisfal Glades, seeking to wipe out the Undercity and erase the Forsaken entirely. In a desperate defense, the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn fought back the floating fortress at great cost. During the clash, the immense necrotic focusing crystal mounted atop Naxxramas was destroyed, blasting fragments across the glades below. Though the citadel was driven off, the fallout remains embedded in the soil. Scourge cultists have moved in to retrieve the necrotic crystal fragments, hoping to harness the dark magic still lingering inside them. Collecting these shards deprives the Scourge of raw unholy power, though clearing every piece from Tirisfal will take years.

quest:96899.text: Bandarion Keep. Bandarion Keep is a quest in Tirisfal Glades directing adventurers to meet Argent Dawn Commander Leonid Barthalomew at a secluded fortress. Once an Argent Dawn staging base against the Scourge, the stronghold is now maintained by Danitha and her order of paladins. Bandarion Keep is an Argent Dawn quest that directs adventurers across Tirisfal Glades to meet Commander Leonid Barthalomew. After aiding the Dawn against Cult of the Damned activity, travelers are pointed northwest toward the fortress to rendezvous with the commander and learn more about the order's ongoing crusade against darkness. The stronghold once served as a vital staging post for the Argent Dawn as they combated Scourge incursions throughout Tirisfal Glades. When the Dawn shifted its focus toward the Eastern and Western Plaguelands, the fort was left behind and threatened to decay into ruin, until the paladin Danitha and her companions assumed stewardship over its walls.

quest:97.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation finally confirms the sinister truth connecting the elusive tutor to Darkshire's records. Clerk Daltry successfully matches the handwriting found on the recovered documents to Stalvan Mistmantle, prompting an immediate report to Commander Althea Ebonlocke. It marks the moment the Night Watch's suspicions harden into undeniable fact. After combing through distant manors, inns, and municipal archives across the human kingdoms, the fragmented trail returns to Darkshire's town hall. Clerk Daltry compares the bloodstained journal page against the signatures in the Town Registry. The result is unequivocal: the penmanship belongs to Stalvan Mistmantle, giving the Night Watch the hard evidence needed to treat the matter as an urgent local threat.

quest:970.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks a critical turn in the investigation of the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand, shifting the pursuit from the ruined Tower of Althalaxx in Darkshore across the border to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier dispatches adventurers into nearby cultist camps to secure a potent Glowing Soul Gem. Unlocking this artifact reveals the grim sorcery that fuels the cult's influence over the northern forests. After uncovering the ominous activities around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, reports led directly south into Ashenvale to Delgren the Purifier. Stationed at Maestra's Post, Delgren has long contended with the Cult of the Dark Strand encroaching on the ancient elven woods. Recognizing that the cult's threat spans across both territories, Delgren resolves to strike at the heart of their vile sorcery. Northeast of Maestra's Post lies the ruins of Ordil'Aran, now overrun by fanatical Dark Strand cultists. Delgren identifies that their operatives carry glowing soul gems—dark vessels enchanted with sinister magic that sustain the cult's power. By hunting down the cultists among the ruins and reclaiming one of these gems, Delgren intends to shatter their enchantment and expose the true source behind their malevolent rite.

quest:97005.text: Chol'aruk the Ravener. A horror stalks a cave on Thorn Hill in the Barrens, where the Razormane call it Chol'aruk the Ravener. Bainham seeks its severed head to avenge comrades lost to similar beasts. Northwest of Bainham's camp in the Barrens, Thorn Hill rises above the Savannah. Razormane tribes have long fought over the plateau. Now rumors speak of a monstrous abomination in one of its caves, called Chol'aruk or the Ravener by the Razormane. Some travelers dismiss tales that it can swallow an armored orc whole. Those who have seen the carnage know the danger is real. Bainham knows Chol'aruk is no campfire tale. He has fought similar horrors and bears scars from those encounters, while mourning comrades who fell to such beasts. He fears the abomination threatens everyone crossing the Savannah. Bainham asks seasoned champions to climb Thorn Hill, enter its underground lair, slay Chol'aruk, and bring back its massive head.

quest:971.text: Knowledge in the Deeps. Knowledge in the Deeps is an Alliance quest offered by Gerrig Bonegrip in Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. He tasks adventurers with trekking across the sea to the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale to recover the ancient Lorgalis Manuscript. Beneath Bonegrip's scholar veneer lies an ominous agenda tied to dark entities and apocalyptic prophecy. Hidden away in the damp reaches of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip presents himself as a devoted collector of ancient texts. Yet his scholarly pursuits carry a distinctly sinister undertone. Bonegrip is not interested in mundane history or civic chronicles; he explicitly hunts for forgotten lore capable of opening doorways and awakening 'Those Who Sleep.' His talk of surviving beyond 'the end days' marks him as an eccentric—or a dangerous devotee of shadowy, slumbering powers. Bonegrip directs seekers halfway across Azeroth to the shadowed shores of Ashenvale, where the ancient night elven sanctuary of Blackfathom Deeps lies drowned. Before the Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart, night elven scholars gathered immense magical knowledge in their coastal temples. Amidst the flooded corridors, now crawling with naga, satyrs, and Twilight's Hammer cultists, rests the Lorgalis Manuscript—a text of forbidden lore kept in a Pitted Iron Chest.

quest:972.text: Water Sapta. At Islen Waterseer's shore, a young Horde shaman receives Water Sapta for a journey across the Great Sea. The trial leads from the Barrens to Silverpine Forest, where a spring has been corrupted. Among Horde shaman, a sapta is a draught made to open the senses to the world's spirits. To ordinary eyes, a stream may look calm and a pond still. Drink a sapta, and the veil of the physical world parts, showing the elementals that dwell in the water. Islen Waterseer gives the shaman the draught after they have shown their devotion to the spirits. She lives alone on the barren shore south of Ratchet. She sends the initiate across the Great Sea, away from Kalimdor's dry valleys, to Silverpine Forest. There, an elemental corruption is poisoning Lordaeron's streams, and the shaman must face it.

quest:97220.text: Philmor's Favor. Philmor's Favor is a delivery task in Stormwind prompted by an ongoing shortage of local dockhands. Couriers are asked to transport a delicate Gatehouse shipment to a secluded stockroom entrance situated on the second floor of Trias' Cheese shop in the Trade District. A persistent shortage of dockhands across Stormwind has strained the city's routine freight operations. To keep local cargo schedules from falling behind, handlers look for reliable travelers willing to haul sensitive crates directly into the commercial quarter. The shipment is marked for the Gatehouse, but its drop-off is anything but conventional. Rather than passing through the main guardhouse entryway, the crate is carried up to the second floor of Trias' Cheese shop in the Trade District. The shop conceals a stockroom entrance used to quietly move supplies and ceremonial gifts intended for the guard's officers away from prying eyes.

quest:97222.text: Gatehouse Goods. Gatehouse Goods is a local Stormwind task involving the transport of a shipment up the stairs within Trias' Cheese. Because the cheese shop shares a floor with the adjacent gatehouse, goods can be quietly dropped outside the stockroom door for guards to collect. The arrangement highlights the tight, interconnected urban design of Stormwind's commercial and defensive quarters. Gatehouse Goods entails a straightforward delivery task nestled within the bustling streets of Stormwind. The job requires carrying a gatehouse shipment up the interior stairs of Trias' Cheese. While the famed cheese shop is an entirely distinct business with its own separate inventory, its physical structure shares a floor with the neighboring gatehouse facilities. This architectural quirk makes the shop's upper landing a practical passage for moving supplies between neighboring quarters without disturbing the front avenues. The delivery protocol is precise: couriers must leave the crate directly outside the stockroom door rather than carrying it inside. Regular gatehouse guards keep an eye on incoming traffic and assign personnel to retrieve packages as they return to their posts. Furthermore, the stockroom's door is deliberately built with inward-swinging hinges, ensuring that goods stacked outside will never block the entryway or hinder those inside from moving freely.

quest:97223.text: Bloodtalon Matriarch. The Bloodtalon Matriarch is the formidable leader of a swift and cunning raptor pack near Sen'jin Village. After proving too dangerous and stubborn to tame as an adult, she must be confronted so her offspring can be raised from the egg as loyal companions for the Darkspear tribe. The Bloodtalon pack is renowned along the coast of Durotar for its remarkable speed and keen cunning. Handlers in Sen'jin Village prize these traits above all else when seeking dependable mounts and companions for the Darkspear tribe. However, full-grown raptors possess stubborn and violent instincts, making adults almost impossible to domesticate once they have adapted to life in the wild. Despite multiple attempts to capture and train the Matriarch directly, her escalating aggression turned her into an outright threat to the surrounding territory. To safeguard the tribe while ensuring her exceptional bloodline was not lost, the trolls resolved to quell the dangerous mother and salvage her clutch, ensuring the next generation can be raised as loyal allies from the egg.

quest:97225.text: Forgotten Loa Idols. Forgotten Loa Idols centers on recovering sacred religious effigies for the Darkspear trolls. These lost relics are urgently needed to resume vital spiritual ceremonies and preserve the tribe's enduring bond of reverence with their patron wild spirits. For the Darkspear trolls, spiritual balance is inextricably bound to their connection with the loa—the primal animal spirits and wild gods of their ancestral heritage. Forgotten Loa Idols involves recovering displaced religious relics essential for conducting tribal ceremonies. Without these sacred objects, spiritual leaders cannot perform the rites required to maintain harmony with their divine guardians. While several hostile troll factions across Azeroth practice blood sacrifices or seek to compel spirits by force, the Darkspear pride themselves on maintaining a bond of mutual respect and humble reverence. To the Darkspear, falling out of favor with their patrons is a grave catastrophe, making the restoration of these lost idols a vital act of tribal preservation.

quest:97236.text: Fang of Githyiss. The Fang of Githyiss is a rare and formidable specimen taken from a giant arachnid stalking the wilds near Aldrassil. Delivering the fang to a naturalist in the sanctuary allows scholars to study the monstrous creature and monitor the predatory threats nesting within Shadowglen. The Fang of Githyiss is a trophy and biological sample harvested from the overgrown spider Githyiss, who lurks in the wilds of Shadowglen. A beast of such notable bulk poses a clear threat to young travelers venturing out from Aldrassil, making the recovery of its fang both a matter of safety and scientific interest. Rather than letting the creature's remains rot in the underbrush, resourceful scouts take the specimen back to the sanctuary of the great tree. Within Aldrassil, night elf naturalists and scholars keep close track of the wildlife roaming the forest floor. Presenting a fresh, intact fang from a creature of Githyiss's magnitude provides crucial insight into the arachnid populations flourishing beneath Teldrassil's canopy. The local researchers welcome such unexpected discoveries, utilizing the massive fang to further their ongoing studies into the aggressive fauna of the glade.

quest:97243.text: Call of Fire. Call of Fire sends an initiate through the winds of Skywall to seek out Olariaan Swiftburn, a shen'dorei Windshaper attuned to the element of fire. By bringing the Torch of Dormant Flame to the Shrine of Flames in the Gustberry Lowlands, the traveler begins learning to heed the call of the flame even within the domain of air. Even within Skywall, the domain ruled by the air elementals, the broader currents of the Elemental Plane remain connected. The spirits of earth, water, and fire still speak to those with the sensitivity to hear them. The Windshapers count among their fellowship individuals uniquely receptive to these other forces, including Olariaan Swiftburn, a shen'dorei who fosters a deep attunement with the element of fire. Initiates are entrusted with the Torch of Dormant Flame and directed toward the Gustberry Lowlands. Far out along the island rim, tucked west of Valanaar, stands the Shrine of Flames. There, Olariaan Swiftburn receives the dormant flame, offering to instruct aspiring students in answering the demanding call of fire amidst the churning currents of the air realm.

quest:97244.text: Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a quest from the Windshapers commanding the execution of Skypriest Faladiel, a former brother who betrayed his order for power. Adventurers must track the rogue skypriest to the Gustberry Lowlands and retrieve his heart to fuel a powerful elemental ritual. Call of Fire tasks adventurers with hunting down Skypriest Faladiel, a former Windshaper who abandoned his loyalties to join the Al'Aketh. Once a dedicated caller of flame, Faladiel chose power over allegiance, turning on his fellow order members and leaving their blood upon his hands. The Windshapers dispatch an agent to deliver their uncompromising judgment upon him. Faladiel has secluded himself at a farm within the Gustberry Lowlands, situated northeast past Valanaar and just south of the Shrine of Akir. Slaying the rogue skypriest serves more than mere vengeance; the Windshapers require his heart as a grisly component for an upcoming ritual, believing that consuming the heart of a betrayer allows their sacred flames to burn with unmatched intensity.

quest:97245.text: Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a quest in which adventurers are tasked by Olariaan Swiftburn to locate and confront the ancient forest sprite Kuramaa in the Shen'dar Highlands. By invoking the sprite from its stump and defeating it with flame, travelers obtain its powerful wooden mask. The relic is then brought to the Gustberry Lowlands to ignite an eternal flame and commune with the spirits of fire. In the Shen'dar Highlands, local residents whisper tales of Kuramaa, an ancient forest sprite that resides inside a twisted tree stump at the summit of a hill near the regional Anchor Pylon. To draw the reclusive entity into the open, a challenger must strike the bark of its wooden home with a bare fist, demanding its presence and testing their mettle in combat. Overcoming Kuramaa is no simple task for wielders of the arcane or divine, as the sprite possesses deep natural wards against most forms of magic. Only searing flame can pierce its ancient bark and bring it low. Defeating the creature yields Kuramaa's wooden mask, an artifact imbued with great power. Even so, Kuramaa is eternal, bound to reform and manifest again when called upon.

quest:97246.text: Meal Appeal. Meal Appeal is an Orgrimmar errand given by Thatog, an orc tied down by his daily duties who worries his young son Migi is skipping meals to play. Travelers are asked to pick up a prepared lunch from Borstan's Firepit and track down Migi playing behind Grommash Hold. It offers a grounded look at domestic family life within the Horde's capital. In the bustling red-rock avenues of Orgrimmar, everyday domestic life continues alongside the drills of grunt warriors and the machinations of the Horde. Thatog, bound to his daily post by duty, finds himself unable to keep a watchful eye over his energetic young son, Migi. Left to his own devices, Migi spends from morning till dusk racing through the city streets with his friends, consistently neglecting his stomach until returning home famished. Rather than let the boy go hungry yet another afternoon, Thatog arranges for a hot meal at Borstan's Firepit. Because Migi will not bother to stop his games to pick up lunch himself, Thatog asks passing adventurers to act as a personal courier. The errand takes travelers from Borstan's cookfire to the open yard behind Grommash Hold, where Migi and the rest of the neighborhood youths can almost always be found caught up in their childhood games.

quest:97257.text: Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a shamanic rite of passage overseen by the Windshapers within Skywall. Initiates must aid in invoking spirits of flame, capture the Eternal Flame, and race against time to kindle the brazier at Valanaar. Successfully completing the trial proves one's respect for the elements and earns the initiate their Fire Totem. The Call of Fire is a sacred trial of elemental attunement conducted within Skywall. Led by Olariaan of the Windshapers, initiates gather at the Brazier of Offering to invoke the spirits of flame from the Firelands. If the offerings are deemed worthy, the spirits ignite the altar with the sacred Eternal Flame, ready to be harnessed by a worthy aspirant. Once lit, the Eternal Flame must be captured onto a torch and carried swiftly across Skywall to Valanaar. Because the energies of the Firelands naturally weaken and disperse in the swirling atmosphere of the elemental air realm, the initiate faces a race against time to reach the Brazier of Eternal Flames before the flame dies out. Rekindling the brazier at Valanaar proves the initiate's discipline and reverence toward the elements. In recognition of this achievement, the Windshapers bestow the initiate with their Fire Totem. As taught by the elders, elemental power readily serves those who respect it, but will mercilessly consume those who do not.

quest:97263.text: Your Package Has Arrived. "Your Package Has Arrived" is an urgent courier task concerning misplaced mail intended for delivery in Ironforge. A courier crate sent all the way from the Wildhammer stronghold of Aerie Peak was left abandoned beside a mailbox, addressed specifically to Eldrun Stormbreaker. Travelers who discover the parcel are tasked with completing its journey and seeing that it reaches its rightful owner. A postal mishap leaves several stray parcels abandoned beside a city mailbox, left out in the open rather than carried safely to their destinations. Among this jumbled heap of neglected freight sits an urgent parcel marked for delivery all the way from Aerie Peak, the mountain redoubt of the Wildhammer dwarves in the Hinterlands. Transporting goods between distant outposts across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron can be perilous and chaotic, meaning mislaid parcels occasionally require an alert passerby to step in and finish the delivery route properly. The misplaced package bears clear labeling designating Ironforge as its destination and Eldrun Stormbreaker as its final recipient. Marked explicitly with an urgent notice, whatever cargo the bundle holds was deemed important enough to be expedited from the rustic peaks of the Hinterlands to the subterranean halls of the dwarven capital. Taking up the crate means taking on the responsibility of the postal service, ensuring that Eldrun receives what was sent across mountain ridges and wild hills before it can be stolen or forgotten completely.

quest:97277.text: Grund and Gozwin. Grund and Gozwin recounts an ambush at a campsite in the snowy northwestern hills, where a dwarf and a gnome were attacked by a predatory snow leopard. Although the gnome survived thanks to his partner's shotgun, his prized mechanic's log was left behind in the commotion. Adventurers are sent into the hills to recover the delicate notes and slay the stalking beast. While traveling together in the snowy hills, the dwarf Grund and his gnomish companion Gozwin set up an encampment for the evening. As Grund turned his back to prep a boar over the fire, a snow leopard prowler lunged from the brush and grabbed Gozwin in its jaws. Reacting instantly, Grund grabbed his trusty shotgun and blasted a round over the beast's head, startling the predator into dropping the gnome and fleeing into the cold crags. Although Gozwin escaped the jaws of the cat with deep scratches rather than fatal injuries, their camp was thoroughly disrupted. In the chaos of the retreat, Gozwin dropped his prized Mechanic's Log—a technical notebook containing critical schematics for his mecha-walker. Terribly anxious that someone might discover his engineering secrets, the battered gnome could not rest until an adventurer agreed to venture northwest into the hills to reclaim his book and slay the prowling predator.

quest:97281.text: A Simmering Storm. A Simmering Storm begins when an adventurer recovers a strange, spark-emitting relic known as the Dull Stormy Orb from the harpies of Drygulch Ravine. Bearing the swirling miniature storm to the goblin tinker Rezlak provides insight into the harpies' odd trinkets and earns the interest of Ratchet's enterprising salvagers. While contending with the aggressive Dustwind harpies nesting throughout Drygulch Ravine, travelers may come across an unusual curiosity: the Dull Stormy Orb. Though its outer surface appears muted and worn, holding the object reveals a steady vibration of raw electrical current. Inside the sphere, dark mist churns endlessly, illuminated at random intervals by sharp internal sparks. It is unmistakable proof that the harpies were manipulating storm magic through strange relics. Rather than leaving such volatile magic in the talons of wild harpies, the orb can be brought directly to Rezlak. Stationed at the entrance of Drygulch Ravine, the pragmatic goblin tinker takes an immediate interest in the strange relic, noting that its discovery recalls old advice from his employer in Ratchet, Chief Engineer Gazlowe. Whatever the harpies intended to brew with the miniature storm, it now sits in goblin hands.

quest:97282.text: Stormy Potential. Stormy Potential is a quest in Durotar given by the goblin Rezlak near Drygulch Ravine. Hoping to protect his trade caravan against marauding harpies, Rezlak seeks to supercharge a depleted orb using the potent electrical organs of native thunder lizards. Near the shadow of Drygulch Ravine in Durotar, the goblin Rezlak found himself facing two problems: a caravan under constant threat from local harpies, and an intact magical orb completely depleted of power. Remembering the pragmatic advice of Ratchet's chief engineer Gazlowe—to seize opportunity whenever it knocks—Rezlak hatched an ambitious plan to solve both problems at once by supercharging the dormant device. To restore the drained orb, Rezlak required a potent, immediate source of raw electricity. The gorge to the west of Drygulch Ravine is home to thunder lizards—creatures known for internal organs capable of generating and conducting lethal jolts of lightning. By sending an adventurer to harvest these charged organs, Rezlak hoped to safely channel their volatile current directly into the device, giving his vulnerable supply wagons a formidable defense against future harpy ambushes.

quest:973.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Delgren the Purifier sends you south from Darkshore into Ashenvale to hunt Ilkrud Magthrull. The orc warlock resides at Fire Scar Shrine, where you are to slay him and recover his tome. Delgren the Purifier traces the dark cultists at the Tower of Althalaxx to Ilkrud Magthrull, an orc warlock. Ilkrud works from Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, and Delgren fears his magic could spread through the elven woodlands. He sends you to kill the warlock and take his tome, hoping its contents will reveal his master's designs.

quest:97539.text: Silky Sutures. Silky Sutures is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands offered by Doctor Gregory Victor in the outpost of Hammerfall. Frustrated by unrepaired siege damage and dwindling medical supplies, the camp's resident physician recruits adventurers to gather venomous highland spider silk for use as emergency field sutures. The task highlights the desperate, resource-starved conditions facing the defenders of Hammerfall as they struggle to keep their guards and laborers on their feet. Hammerfall endures in the rugged Arathi Highlands, but the encampment shows visible signs of prolonged strain. Unrepaired siege damage marks the perimeter, leading the local physician, Doctor Gregory Victor, to bitterly observe that neglect seems to be official policy. Despite the crumbling fortifications and lack of broader support, Victor refuses to let the decay claim his infirmary. Maintaining a working clinic is essential for keeping the laborers and sentinel guards upright and ready for conflict. Dwindling supplies have left the Hammerfall medical ward on the brink of exhaustion, forcing Doctor Victor to turn to battlefield improvisation. When conventional bandages and stitches run scarce, the tough, tensile silk harvested from highland spiders can be twisted into surprisingly resilient field sutures. Though Victor dryly quips about the risk of infection being the least of a wounded soldier's concerns, harvesting the silk provides the infirmary with the vital equipment needed to patch up wounded defenders in a hostile territory. Operating a frontline clinic under siege conditions requires a hardened temperament, which Doctor Gregory Victor displays in abundance. Greeting travelers with mordant jokes about grave prognoses and spider-string stitches, the physician masks the grim reality of Hammerfall's isolation. Regular aid remains rare in the highlands, making any assistance from visiting champions crucial to sustaining the clinic. Through improvised remedies and stubborn defiance, Victor ensures that Hammerfall's wounded receive care even when the outpost around them seems abandoned to rot.

quest:97583.text: WRIGGLE.. WRIGGLE. is an encounter with an excitable young slime that loves to dance until it runs out of energy. To revive and befriend the creature, an adventurer must fetch a special batch of nutritious sludge from the canals of the Undercity. WRIGGLE. involves interacting with a lively, excitable little slime that delights in mirroring the dance movements of friendly travelers. Despite its enthusiasm, dancing quickly exhausts the small ooze, leaving it weary and in need of sustenance to restore its strength. To revitalize the tuckered-out creature, adventurers must seek out Nutritious Slime Sludge, a peculiar mixture sold within the rancid canals of the Undercity. Upon absorbing this favored foul treat, the energized slime eagerly bonds with its provider, ready to follow its new friend.

quest:976.text: Supplies to Auberdine. Supplies to Auberdine is an escort mission where Alliance adventurers protect Feero Ironhand as he carries critical provisions and messages from Maestra's Post northward toward Darkshore. Given the growing menace radiating from the Tower of Althalaxx and the presence of hostile infiltrators in Ashenvale, safe passage cannot be taken for granted. Maestra's Post sits on the western frontier of Ashenvale, a quiet outpost caught between the wild tensions of the forest and the troubled lands of Darkshore. Following investigations into the sinister activity surrounding the Tower of Althalaxx, Delgren the Purifier gathers vital supplies and intelligence bound for Sentinel Starbreeze in Auberdine. Rather than risking solitary couriers, the outpost relies on armed escorts to accompany Feero Ironhand as he treks along the forest road.

quest:97891.text: Prompt Potion Runner. Prompt Potion Runner is an urgent Undercity delivery quest where players must race an unstable concoction across the slime canal to the Apothecarium. The quest highlights the physical infirmities of undeath and the volatile nature of Forsaken alchemical research. In the subterranean corridors of the Undercity, the Forsaken alchemist Alessandro urgently needs a swift courier. Having prepared a highly volatile concoction with an extremely short shelf life, he cannot risk transporting it himself across the city's toxic slime canal due to the fragile state of his undead joints. An adventurer must sprint against the clock to ensure the brew arrives intact before it degrades into useless sludge. The destination is the Apothecarium, where Doctor Martin Felben eagerly awaits the delivery for his ongoing research. Felben reveals that the previous six couriers or attempts failed because the potions destabilized mid-transit. A timely arrival allows the doctor to continue his shadowy experiments uninterrupted, underscoring both the volatility of Royal Apothecary concoctions and the physical indignities of undeath.

quest:97903.text: Camping 101: First Aid. Camping 101: First Aid is an instructional quest that sends skilled travelers to Rawrk in Razor Hill, who teaches them how to craft their own First Aid Kit for wilderness survival. It emphasizes the necessities of self-reliance on the trail, reminding adventurers to master campfire creation and respect local settlements by camping out in the wild. Survival in the untamed expanses of Durotar and beyond requires more than just raw martial strength; it demands self-sufficiency on the trail. In Razor Hill, Rawrk offers instruction to capable wanderers seeking to fashion essential wilderness gear. Through Camping 101: First Aid, practitioners who have proven their basic proficiency learn to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit, giving them the means to mend wounds and tend to injuries far from the safety of an apothecary or infirmary. Setting up camp is an art governed by practical frontier etiquette and necessity. Rawrk cautions adventurers that pitching tents in the center of settlements like Razor Hill is unwelcome, meaning these wilderness stations must be tested out in the open wilds. Furthermore, no campsite is functional without a roaring campfire to stave off the night, making a passing familiarity with the culinary arts—where firemaking is first mastered—a vital asset for any prospective camper.

quest:97907.text: Camping 101: Mining. Camping 101: Mining is an instructional trade quest directing budding miners to Krunn in Razor Hill. By demonstrating proficiency in their trade, miners learn to forge a Lodestone, a specialized camp fixture that enhances the combat prowess of warriors gathered around a wilderness fire. Mining offers an honest living that provides practical materials for exploration and survival in the wild. As miners develop their trade and demonstrate proficiency with pick and ore, they can learn to craft specialized campsite equipment. In Durotar, skilled miners are pointed toward Krunn in the settlement of Razor Hill to discover how to forge a Lodestone for their travels. A Lodestone serves as an attractive centerpiece for adventurers resting in the wilderness. When set up beside a camp, it provides martial fighters gathering by the fire with an added edge to their combat prowess. However, proper camp etiquette requires leaving civilized settlements behind: townsfolk frown upon camps being erected in city squares, meaning travelers must seek the open wild to test their craftsmanship. Even the sturdiest lodestone is useless without a proper fire to anchor the camp. A basic campfire is necessary before establishing any resting spot, and those unfamiliar with building fires are encouraged to seek out a culinary instructor. Training in the cooking arts ensures that wilderness expeditions have the warmth and basic sustenance required to survive outside town walls.

quest:97908.text: Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory wilderness quest directing skinners in Orgrimmar to Thuwd to learn how to craft a Camp Chair. By putting harvested hides to use for field comfort, adventurers can establish proper campsites out in the wilds of Kalimdor. Harvesting the pelts and hides of fallen beasts is one of the most practical survival skills an adventurer can cultivate in the wild. While raw leathers usually feed armorcraft, skilled skinners can also turn their harvested pelts into field comforts. In Orgrimmar, instructors direct capable skinners to Thuwd to learn the craft of assembling a sturdy Camp Chair from cured hides. Townsfolk and guards frown upon travelers pitching temporary camps along busy city thoroughfares. As Thuwd reminds new craftsmen, a camp chair is meant for open territory away from settlement walls. Furthermore, no wilderness camp is complete with seating alone; a proper site requires a warm campfire, a basic technique taught by cooks across Kalimdor.

quest:97921.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. Camping 101: Herbalism is a training quest that directs skilled gatherers to seek specialized wilderness instruction in Elwynn Forest. Upon demonstrating proficiency in harvesting flora, herbalists are pointed toward Herbalist Pomeroy to learn the art of crafting campsite utilities. Completing this training unlocks the ability to create Incense Candles, botanical aids designed to bolster the focus and spirits of spellcasters resting in the field. For wandering herbalists, harvesting herbs across the wilds of Azeroth serves purposes well beyond brewing basic restorative draughts or selling bundles of flowers to city merchants. As practitioners hone their gathering craft, opportunities arise to apply their floral knowledge toward wilderness survival. Field camps require more than just a roaring fire and dry bedroll; maintaining the endurance and mental acuity of a traveling party demands specialized comforts. Experienced foragers recognize that certain plants hold aromatic properties capable of invigorating weary minds. By directing promising herbalists toward established mentors, this task bridges simple gathering with practical fieldcraft, proving that a keen eye for nature's bounty can sustain an entire expedition far from civilization. Aspiring herbalists seeking to expand their campsite craft are sent into the heart of Elwynn Forest to consult with Herbalist Pomeroy. Well-versed in the botanical varieties of the surrounding woodlands, Pomeroy understands how dried petals, aromatic stems, and natural resins can be blended into functional camp gear. Rather than using herbs solely for alchemy flasks, she instructs gatherers in the construction of an Incense Candle. When burned at a campsite, this fragrant creation soothes exhausted travelers and lifts the spirits of mana-reliant companions. Finding Pomeroy and proving one's competence with the sickle ensures that an herbalist becomes an indispensable asset to any adventuring party venturing into the untamed wild.

quest:97922.text: Camping 101: Leatherworking. Camping 101: Leatherworking directs apprentice leatherworkers to Adele Fielder in Goldshire to learn the craft of making a travel tent. Pitching a tent in the wild offers shelter and rest against harsh weather, providing adventurers a vital survival tool outside settled towns. For an adventurer wandering far beyond town gates, shelter is as vital as armor. Leatherworkers in Elwynn Forest are directed to Adele Fielder in Goldshire to expand their craft beyond simple belts and tunics. Once a crafter demonstrates proficiency with hide and needle, Adele shares the practical art of assembling a durable camp tent designed to withstand harsh weather on long overland expeditions. A finished tent provides more than just aesthetic cover; it keeps weary travelers cool under scorching suns, dry during driving rainstorms, and well-rested between perilous encounters. However, wilderness etiquette and civic ordinances matter: Goldshire locals and city guards do not tolerate campsites pitched in the middle of town streets. Crafters must head into the open wilderness to set up camp, and Adele reminds all wanderers that no campsite is complete without a proper campfire learned from a culinary trainer.

quest:97923.text: Camping 101: Mining. Camping 101: Mining is an introductory quest that teaches miners how to craft a lodestone to enhance wilderness campsites. Instructed by Gelman Stonehand in Stormwind, prospectors learn to channel resonant earthcraft to bolster their companions' combat prowess around the campfire. Mining is tough, honest labor, but its rewards go far beyond smelting raw ingots and shaping armor. Dedicated miners in Stormwind can learn to harness the natural magnetism of the earth into a functional lodestone. When placed at an expedition's campsite, this stone bolsters the combat vigor of any fighter gathered around the hearth fire. Gelman Stonehand, the seasoned mining instructor in the kingdom's capital, passes down the craft to prospectors who demonstrate proficiency with a pickaxe. A lodestone cannot simply be dropped onto the cobblestones of Cathedral Square or the Trade District.
